The 2026-10-02 production release notes set it out: **`cloudflared` stopped → 530 at once → writes fall back and work**; **power cut, first seconds → 502/504 or a 20 s timeout → writes refused**; **power cut, once the edge notices → 530 → fall back**; **Pi up but sick, or `lanna-care` stopped → 502/503 from cloudflared → refused**. So the one case that falls back cleanly is the drill, and a power cut (the likeliest outage for a box in a house) starts with a window of refused sign-ins and saves, and a sick-but-up Pi never falls back at all. "If it's not going to fail over properly, we need a different solution." **Why it is built this way, so the replacement keeps the guarantee:** a 502/504 can arrive *after* the Pi has written, so replaying it on the Worker could record a second intake (#250), and a thrown fetch cannot tell "never arrived" from "arrived, then dropped" (the decision file's probe table). Any new design must still never apply a write twice. **The key fact to build on: the data is not on the Pi.** Both the Pi and the Worker write to the same Supabase database, so the duplicate risk can be closed *at the database* rather than by guessing at the edge, after which retrying on the Worker is always safe. **Options to weigh, not mutually exclusive:** (1) **Idempotent writes.** Every server action carries a client-generated request id, and the database records it under a unique key in the same transaction as the write (one shared wrapper around `runAction()` plus a `write_requests` table, or a parameter on the RPCs that matter: intake, placements, weights, deliveries, stocktake, uploads' attachment rows). A replay then returns the first result instead of writing again, and **every** failure (502, 504, timeout, thrown fetch) can fall back to the Worker. It removes the "refused by design" rows outright, but it touches every write path, so it needs its own schema PR and a sweep like #441's. (2) **Route on health, not on each request's outcome.** The Pi sends a heartbeat every few seconds (or the Worker's cron probes it) into Workers KV or a Durable Object; when it is stale the Worker serves *everything* itself before trying the Pi, so a new request after a power cut never waits for the edge to notice. Covers the "Pi up but sick" row too if the heartbeat comes from the app rather than the OS. It does not cover a request already in flight when the power goes, which is what (1) is for. (3) **Keep the power on.** A UPS HAT or small UPS for the Pi *and* the router/ONT (the tunnel needs both), sized for a typical Suphan Buri outage, with a clean shutdown on low battery. Cheapest and most direct for the power-cut row; does nothing for a crash or a broken deploy. (4) **A second connector on the same tunnel**, off-site: cloudflared already supports replicas ("A second Pi later" in `scripts/pi/cloudflared-config.yml`), and a free-tier cloud VM (e.g. an always-free ARM instance) running the same build would keep the origin up when the house goes dark. Real redundancy at near-zero cost, but a second machine to deploy to, patch and keep the secrets on, and each replica serves a share of traffic, not only the failover. (5) **Flip it: writes always on the Worker, the Pi only for page renders.** The 1102s came from rendering, not from server actions, so writes might fit the Worker's CPU budget. Then a Pi outage costs reads (which already fall back) and never writes. It hinges on a Pi-rendered form posting to a Worker build, which needs the same server-action ids and a shared `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (the open Deployment item), so verify that first. Paid Cloudflare Load Balancing was considered and is out: it costs every month and cannot target a Worker. **Deliverable:** a short paper (`docs/pi-failover.md`) that measures before it argues: on the real tunnel, time how long a hard power-off takes to become a 530 (pull the plug, POST every second), and what a stopped `lanna-care` returns. Then a recommendation of the cheapest combination that makes every row of the table "falls back and works" without ever risking a double write. My expectation is (1) + (2), with (3) as cheap insurance, but let the measurements decide. React streams a page body inside a Suspense boundary and swaps it in with an inline `$RC(...)` call that waits on `requestAnimationFrame`; the swap stays pending, the page's own client chunks are never requested, and **only the layout hydrates.** An un-hydrated form is a plain HTML form with no `action`, so **Save submits as a GET with every field in the address bar and saves nothing.** Clicking through from another tab is a client-side navigation, never uses that swap, and works — which is exactly the pattern #1001 reported. **THE EVIDENCE:** on `/admin/website?tab=contact`, the pane hydrated **no** button and showed 15 forms all `method=get`; real Chrome hydrated all 13 Save buttons. `requestAnimationFrame(()=>0)` — if it never fires, stop and retest in real Chrome before suspecting the app**; (c) reach the page by **clicking through from another page** instead, which works; (d) a plain-GET form submission in the pane is a symptom of this, not a finding. **THE PART THAT NEEDS A DECISION, and it is the expensive half:** how many existing rows in `docs/card-access-faults.md` and hydrated after a click-through, so none of the rows above is the pane"*, and the one direct load it did make (`/my`, the first screen after sign-in) **showed only the layout, exactly as predicted, and was correctly recorded as nothing.** `claude/card-drive-money` then found three things the original diagnosis did not cover, all of which belong in the same `CLAUDE.md` entry: **(a) A HIDDEN PANE STOPS PAINTING, and `requestAnimationFrame` stops firing there too** — so the symptom is not confined to direct loads, and a page reached correctly by click can still freeze if the pane is not on screen. **Taking a `screenshot` wakes it.** This matters because a stream that follows the click-through rule can still be fooled, and because the harness itself warns that a hidden pane runs as a background page. **(b) PIXEL CLICKS CAN MISS: the screenshot frame is 800x600 while the page is 1024x768**, so coordinates read off a screenshot do not map to the page, and a click lands somewhere else — it missed the resident chooser's **Done**. **`element.click()` through `javascript_tool` worked.** A click that silently lands on nothing looks exactly like a dead control, which is how this becomes a false fault-log row. **(c) `dev-signin.mjs --cards <card>` CALLED TWICE RE-KEYS THE SAME LOGIN, so only the later snippet is valid** — pasting an earlier one signs you in as nothing, or as the wrong card set. **Neither (a) nor (b) is an app fault and neither stream filed a row for one**, which is the behaviour to keep. → *Next up*

Line 90 does the same for `showCompleted`. **The label is "Show cancelled"** (`src/lib/i18n/dictionaries/en.ts:6201`; Thai `src/lib/i18n/dictionaries/th.ts:6004`), which promises only the cancelled ones. **So the label and the behaviour disagree, and nothing is wrong with the data.** **THIS SUPERSEDES THE TWO-ROWS THEORY BELOW:** `visit-duplicates` on production returned *"No cancelled/scheduled pair for one resident and clinic on the same day"*, and the code reading that one row cannot be both overdue and cancelled was correct all along. **Neither the calendar import, the old button, nor the Director's entries are involved.** **DO NOT look for duplicate rows and do not widen `visit-duplicates`.** **THE DECISION, PUT TO HIM 2026-10-27 and the only thing outstanding:** (a) keep the additive behaviour but rename the toggle to say so (*Include cancelled*) and give every cancelled row a visible Cancelled mark so it cannot be mistaken for an overdue one — **the planner's recommendation**, because seeing a cancelled visit beside the live ones is usually what you want; (b) make the toggle exclusive, so ticking it shows cancelled and nothing else; or (c) both toggles become one *Show: upcoming / cancelled / completed* selector. **Whichever he picks, `showCompleted` on line 90 gets the same treatment in the same PR — it has the identical fault and nobody has reported it yet.** **Both dictionaries change, so expect the Thai string too.** **Build it with the browser driven both ways** (toggle off, then on, with an overdue and a cancelled visit present) — that is the whole proof. **>>> DECIDED 2026-10-27 (Lutan, in three messages): "Make it show cancelled only", then "Same with the other chip filters there", then "They all should not be additive".** **THE RULE: a chip filter on `/upcoming-visits` shows THAT status and nothing else.** He did **not** choose the planner's recommendation (rename to *Include cancelled* and mark the rows) and did **not** choose the single *Show:* selector — **do not revive either.** **THE SCOPE, read from the page 2026-10-27 so nobody has to guess which chips he meant** (`src/app/upcoming-visits/VetVisitsView.tsx`): **(1) "Show completed" (line 256, predicate line 90) and (2) "Show cancelled" (line 259, predicate line 91) are the two additive ones and both change.** Each becomes **that status only**, and **the two are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — ticking one unticks the other**, because two "onlys" contradict each other. **With neither ticked the list is exactly as it is today** (scheduled, overdue group at the top). **(3) "Hide overdue" (line 262) IS NOT ADDITIVE AND IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE** — it removes rather than adds, its label *"Hide overdue"* says exactly what it does, and it carries a remembered per-device preference (`localStorage`, `HIDE_KEY`) plus the *"N overdue hidden · show"* banner at line 266. **That is following his instruction, not narrowing it; the planner flagged the exclusion to him in the same breath so he could object, and he can still ask for it.** **(4) The clinic `<select>` (line 253) is ALREADY exclusive** (`!clinic || r.clinicId === clinic`) and is correct — **nothing to do.** **(5) The list / week / month buttons (lines 241-247) and previous / next (203-205) use the same `chip` class but are a VIEW SWITCH and NAVIGATION, not filters. Do not touch them.** **THE LABELS may not need changing at all** — with each chip now doing what *"Show cancelled"* / *"Show completed"* already says, the English and Thai strings (`src/lib/i18n/dictionaries/en.ts:6200-6201`, `th.ts:6004`) may stand as written; **say in the PR which you changed and why.** **WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TIDY-UP:** this is the whole cause of his overdue-and-cancelled report, which cost a production investigation, a read of the live database and very nearly a wrongly-scoped data fix. **PROOF, and it is the deliverable:** drive `/upcoming-visits` with an overdue visit and a cancelled visit both present, and read the list with neither chip on, each on in turn, and both tapped in sequence. **A release note is owed** — he reported it himself, so a user plainly notices it. **DONE 2026-10-27 (`claude/filters-say-what-they-do`).**

- [x] **A directory in a migration's `-- consumer:` header always reads `differs`, so those warnings carry no information: buildable now, small.** **STATUS 2026-10-21:** `migration-consumers.mjs` still compares text directly. Left: resolve a directory to its files, or report it as its own state. Waits on nobody. `scripts/lib/migration-consumers.mjs` decides "was the reader already live" by comparing `git show <ref>:<path>` at the live release and at `origin/main`. For a file that is right. For a **directory** `git show` prints a tree listing whose first line is `tree <ref>:<path>/` — the ref is *in the text* — so the two always differ and the path always reports `differs`. **Proved, not inferred:** `worker/` is a declared consumer of `0236`, has **zero** changed files between `1de7bdb4` and `f2773d25`, and still warned. The four in `0.38.2` were `src/app/clinic-visits/`, `src/app/admin/status/`, `worker/` and `src/app/admin/website/`. **Wrong in both directions, not just noisy:** a tree listing holds only *names*, so even with the ref stripped, a directory whose files changed but whose filenames did not would read `live`. **Why it matters:** this is the signal `docs/decisions/2026-10-02-migration-consumer-header.md` added to catch a real ordering fault, and a check that warns every time is one people stop reading — the same failure as the `test-plan` job's old `continue-on-error`. It never blocks and never changes what is applied, so this is noise rather than risk. **Do:** either resolve a directory to the files under it and compare each, or report it honestly as its own state ("declares a directory, which this cannot check"). **Do NOT** make directory paths silent — that trades a vacuous warning for a vacuous `live` — and **do not** start inferring consumers from the SQL, which was considered and rejected in the 2026-10-02 decision. Reasoning in `docs/decisions/2026-10-21-release-0-38-2-admin-tag-and-directory-consumers.md`.

- [x] **`deploy-pi.sh` updates itself mid-run, so a change to it takes effect ONE DEPLOY LATER - and nothing says so.** Found 2026-10-18 by the `0.36.1` release, the first to ship #708's Pi safety work. **What happened:** #708 added a swap precondition, a `.next.prev` fallback and an automatic asset check to `deploy-pi.sh`. `0.36.1` shipped all three and **none of them ran**, on either clone: no `.next.prev` was created, no swap gate reported, no asset check output. The new script *is* on disk afterwards and `scripts/pi/check-assets.mjs` exists, and the clone is at the release SHA - it was checked out and simply not used. **Mechanism:** `deploy-pi.sh` runs `git fetch` and checks out the target ref near the top, which **replaces the very file bash is executing**. Bash reads a script incrementally, so it carries on with the copy it already had open. **A self-updating deploy script always runs the OLD version on the deploy that introduces the new one.** **Why it matters:** the two things #708 exists to prevent - a half-written `.next` under a running service, and a poisoned year-long asset cache - were both unprotected on the very deploy that shipped their protection, and nobody would have known. The asset check was run by hand instead and passed on both environments, so no harm this time. **It also means any future fix to `deploy-pi.sh` is untested on the release that adds it**, which is the opposite of what a release manager assumes when reading "this is now guarded". **Options:** (a) **Accept and document it** - add a line to `docs/pi-hosting.md` and `docs/release-procedure.md` saying a `deploy-pi.sh` change takes effect on the NEXT deploy, and have the release manager run the new checks by hand on the release that ships them. Cheapest, no code, but relies on someone remembering. (b) **Re-exec after checkout**: once the ref is checked out, `exec "$0" "$@"` with an env guard (e.g. `DEPLOY_PI_REEXECED=1`) so it runs the new script and cannot loop. Small and self-correcting, but `exec` mid-deploy needs care with the log redirect and the `setsid nohup` wrapper the runbook uses. (c) **Split the script in two**: a thin stable launcher that fetches, and a payload script it then invokes - the launcher rarely changes, the payload is always the new one. Most robust, most churn. **Whichever is chosen, say explicitly what happens to the launcher's own updates**, since (c) only moves the problem to a smaller file. Needs a test plan that proves a change to the payload takes effect on the same deploy. See `docs/releases/2026-10-18.md` Defect 1. -> *Deployment (before go-live)*

- [x] **A Pi deploy can poison Cloudflare's cache with a broken stylesheet, and `immutable` keeps it broken for a YEAR. Found live on 2026-10-17 by Lutan, minutes after `0.36.0` shipped (BLOCKING-ADJACENT: it reached a real user on a real phone).** **Symptom:** the app renders with no styling at all - white background, default serif text, no orange - while the page *content* is current and correct. Lutan saw it on his iPhone; the laptop looked perfect throughout. **It survived clearing Safari's cache**: it came back right, then lost the styling again minutes later, which is what ruled out a one-off stale browser cache and made it a server-side finding. **Mechanism:** `/_next/static/**` is served `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, so Cloudflare caches it for a year and never revalidates. `deploy-pi.sh` builds into a fresh `.next` and then **swaps it**, so there is a window in which a request for an asset can be answered with a 404 or a half-written file. **Whichever Cloudflare location serves that request caches the failure for a year.** Because a phone on mobile data and a laptop on wifi can reach different Cloudflare locations, the result looks like "it is only broken on mobile" and is invisible to whoever is checking from the laptop - which is exactly how it played out. **Evidence gathered at the time:** the stylesheet at origin was complete and byte-identical to test (92,570 bytes) on 20 consecutive fetches; the Bangkok edge held a good copy with `CF-Cache-Status: HIT, Age: 26158`; the page referenced exactly that file; a fresh browser rendered it correctly at desktop AND at 375 px with a phone user agent. So nothing was wrong with the build, the HTML, the CSP or the file - only with what some edge nodes had stored. **Resolved on the day by Lutan purging the Cloudflare cache** (Caching -> Configuration -> Purge Everything). **Why this needs a permanent fix: it will recur on every single Pi deploy**, the window is invisible, and the blast radius is a year of broken styling for whoever is unlucky. **Options, in rough order of preference:** (a) **Purge the cache automatically at the end of `deploy-pi.sh`** (Cloudflare API, `purge_everything` or by prefix) - simplest, and it closes the window whatever caused it; needs an API token on the Pi, so weigh that against `docs/security/`. (b) **Make the swap atomic from the edge's point of view** - build into `.next.new`, then `mv` into place in one operation, so no request can ever see a half-written file; cheap, no credentials, but it does not help the 404 window if the directory is briefly absent. (c) **Serve assets from the Worker only**, so a Pi rebuild cannot affect them at all - biggest change, best end state. (d) At minimum, **a post-deploy check that fetches the referenced stylesheet and asserts its length**, so the release manager finds this rather than a user does. **Whatever is chosen, add the purge step to `docs/release-procedure.md`** - there is currently no purge anywhere in the runbook, and `docs/release-smoke-test.md` only mentions a purge in passing for public pages. **Note for whoever picks this up:** there is no purge script in the repo and no Cloudflare dashboard access from a session, so today this is a step only Lutan can do - which is itself an argument for (a) or (b). See `docs/releases/2026-10-17-0-36-0.md`. -> *Deployment (before go-live)* **Ticked 2026-10-19: the fix already existed (scripts/purge-cache.mjs run from the dev machine after each Pi deploy, plus the stylesheet check at the end of deploy-pi.sh). What was missing was the token: Lutan created CLOUDFLARE_PURGE_TOKEN (Zone > Cache Purge > Purge, zones lannacare.org AND lannacareforanimals.org, expires 2027-12-31), saved it in .env.deploy.production, and the purge was run and verified. Still open: see the cutover item below (second zone id).** **(b) and (d) also built 2026-10-19 (claude/pi-deploy-truth): build into `.next.new` and rename in; the asset check runs from an exit trap. Not yet run on a real Pi.**

  **STATUS 2026-10-18: option (a) is BUILT and open as #720, and it is WAITING ON ONE VALUE FROM LUTAN.** `scripts/purge-cache.mjs --env production` purges the zone and then checks the purge took, rather than trusting Cloudflare's own "success". **It diverges from the plan above on purpose:** the token does NOT go on the Pi. `deploy-pi.sh` is driven over `ssh` from the deploy machine, where `.env.deploy.production` already lives and `scripts/lib/env.mjs` already reads it, so the purge runs there and **no Cloudflare credential goes on the internet-facing box at all** - the trade-off this item weighed is avoided rather than accepted (`docs/decisions/2026-10-18-purge-from-the-deploy-machine.md`). **OUTSTANDING, and it is Lutan's:** (1) create an API token at Cloudflare -> My Profile -> API Tokens with **Permissions: Zone -> Cache Purge -> Purge** and **Zone Resources limited to the one zone** serving `lannacare.org`; (2) put it in `.env.deploy.production` as `CLOUDFLARE_PURGE_TOKEN` - **one new value, since `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID` is already there**, and NOT a Worker secret, it must never be pushed as one; (3) run `node scripts/purge-cache.mjs --env production` once after a Pi deploy and confirm it reports a purge and a whole stylesheet. **Until (1)-(3) are done the success path has never executed** - only the refusal paths are tested - so **do not tick this item**; tick it when the first real purge runs. **Also still unexercised:** the wrong-or-under-scoped-token branch (Cloudflare returns `10000`). **Still true meanwhile:** the manual dashboard purge works and is what the runbook falls back to, a Pi-side `deploy-pi.sh` run does not purge by design (its asset check fails loudly when one is needed), and **a purge is global but the check only sees one edge node**, which is why the runbook says purge even when the check is green.

No messages, just everything on the app becomes unresponsive including side nav bar"*. **A page reload clears it; nothing is lost and the photo is never deleted.** **Cause, established 2026-10-18 and not a guess:** `src/app/photos/approve/PendingQueue.tsx` `discard()` (~65) and `src/app/photos/approve/ApproveQueue.tsx` `remove()` (~97) and `approve(ids, confirmFirst)` (~59) all call **`await confirm(...)` INSIDE `startTransition(async () => …)`**. `ConfirmProvider` (`src/components/ConfirmProvider.tsx` ~31) opens the dialog by calling `setOptions(next)` **synchronously inside the promise executor**, so that state update is part of the transition — and the transition cannot finish until the promise resolves, which only happens when the person clicks the dialog. **The dialog never commits, the click never comes, the transition never ends.** Because Next's App Router runs client navigation through transitions too, everything afterwards queues behind the stuck one, **which is why the side nav dies and not merely the button** — that symptom is the tell, and it is what ruled out two earlier wrong theories (a hanging Drive call, and a database/RLS refusal). **The evidence is structural:** **every** other `useConfirm` caller in the app asks first and starts the transition after — checked in `BloodTestTypesTable`, `DietTypesTable`, `EnclosuresTable`, `MapEditor`, `FrequenciesTable`, `ImmunizationTypesTable`, `MedicationsTable`, `ProcedureTypesTable`, `AccessRequests`, `DoctorLoginLink`, `UsersTable` and `AlertActions`. NOT BLOCKING any more; the fix is owned by the cache item in Next up and what is left here is bookkeeping.** Found 2026-10-17 by the release. `./scripts/pi/deploy-pi.sh` compiled successfully (55s production, 51s test) and was then killed by the kernel during `Running TypeScript ...` on **both clones, on the first attempt**, succeeding on a plain retry with nothing changed. The Pi has 4 GB RAM and 2 GB swap; `free -m` showed **174 MB free** mid-build and 3.5 GB available after the kill, so the build itself exhausted memory. **Eleven previous releases built fine - nothing about the Pi changed, the app did**: this release added the 121-screen phone-width sweep, the stories pages and the name-card scanning routes, so the typecheck holds more than it ever has. Two clones failing first time is not bad luck; **expect it to fail from now on.** **Why it matters more than a retry suggests:** `deploy-pi.sh` builds into a fresh `.next` before swapping, so the service keeps serving and **a failed build is quiet** - `lanna-care` stayed `active`, the clone source was already fetched to the release SHA, and only the *served version* gave it away (the runbook's "a git-updated clone is not a deployed clone" trap, met for real). During the window production served `0.34.0` from the Pi while the Worker served `0.35.0` **and the mail announcing `0.35.0` had already gone out**, so the announcement briefly preceded the thing it described. Nothing broke for users, and schema ahead of code is the safe direction. **Deliberately not done during the release:** no `NODE_OPTIONS` cap, no swap change, no `deploy-pi.sh` edit - changing how production builds to work around a fault found in that release is how a small problem becomes a shipped one. **Options to weigh in the PR:** (a) cap V8's heap for the build (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=...`) so it collects rather than grows until the kernel kills it - cheapest, and the standard fix for an OOM-kill; (b) enlarge the Pi's swap; (c) **drop the typecheck from the Pi build entirely**, since `gates.mjs` and CI have both already typechecked the same commit before it can be deployed, which removes the heaviest stage rather than accommodating it. Needs a test plan that exercises a deliberately failing build and shows the operator is told. **ESCALATED 2026-10-17, same day: a later deploy was killed THREE TIMES IN A ROW and the release stalled.** The morning's "succeeds on a plain retry" is **no longer true** — the production release manager session hit attempt 1, 2 and 3 all killed, with the test Worker finishing clean alongside. **So this is now a blocker, not a nuisance, and retrying is not a workaround.** **Two corrections to the options above, both found while advising on the stall:** (1) **There is no separate typecheck step to drop.** `deploy-pi.sh` runs `npm ci` then `npm run build`, and `build` is plain `next build`; the "Running TypeScript ..." stage is *inside* it. So option (c) is **not** deleting a line from the script — it means `typescript: { ignoreBuildErrors: true }` in `next.config.ts`, which today carries a deliberate `tsconfigPath` switch keyed on `NODE_ENV` and a comment explaining why. Any such change must be **gated so it only applies to the Pi build** and must not weaken `gates.mjs` or CI, and the `--ref` hole ("what if someone deploys a ref CI never saw") still needs its answer — most cheaply by making `deploy-pi.sh` refuse, or warn loudly, for a ref CI has not passed. (2) **The immediate workaround recommended was MORE SWAP, not a build change** (`fallocate` a temporary 4 GB `/swapfile2`, `swapon`, retry, and `swapoff`/`rm` afterwards), precisely because it leaves the build untouched — same inputs, same artefact, just headroom — where a `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` cap changes how the build runs even though it should not change what it produces. If swap turns out to be what unblocked it, say so in the PR: it is evidence the fix is about headroom rather than a runaway. **Still true and still the point: make a failed build LOUD.** The morning's half-deployed state (Pi on `0.34.0`, Worker on `0.35.0`, announcement already mailed) was only visible from the served version, and this second failure was again found by a person watching, not by the tooling. **OUTCOME 2026-10-17, `0.36.0` shipped: MORE SWAP WAS RIGHT, and this item is now about writing it down.** The swap recommendation above is exactly what unblocked it, so record the evidence: the test clone was killed **four times running** (attempts 2-4 identical re-runs, two dying earlier than the first, during `Creating an optimized production build` rather than the typecheck), with **3.5-3.6 GB of the Pi's 4 GB free between attempts** and the largest processes on the box being the Next server at 74 MB and `cloudflared` at 30 MB. So it was never contention or a leak - the build's appetite exceeds the machine. **Lutan then increased swap from 2 GB to 6 GB** (a 4 GB file-backed `/swapfile2` beside the existing 2 GB of zram, in `swapon --show`); the next test build completed and the production build succeeded **first time**. **This is evidence the fault is headroom, not a runaway**, as the swap recommendation predicted - and note zram is compressed RAM and adds little real headroom, so it is the **file-backed** swap that did it. **A restart was asked about and correctly rejected**: it reclaims memory that is already free, the box had been up 15 days without leaking, and it briefly drops the Pi as production's origin for no gain. **WHAT IS LEFT, and it is urgent for a different reason than before:** the fix is **deployed by hand and undocumented**. `/swapfile2` is not in `scripts/pi/setup.sh` or `docs/pi-hosting.md`, so **a rebuilt Pi goes straight back to failing and nothing in the repo explains the number**. (1) Put the swapfile in `setup.sh` and document *why* that size. (2) Make `deploy-pi.sh` (or `guard-release.mjs`) **refuse or warn loudly below ~6 GB of swap** - that is the cheapest way to satisfy the standing "make a failed build LOUD" requirement, because the precondition is checkable before the build rather than after. (3) The `ignoreBuildErrors` route is still worth doing on its merits: swap only buys headroom and the app grows every release. See `docs/releases/2026-10-17-0-36-0.md` Defect 1, and note the `0.36.0` handover **withdraws "budget one retry"** as a remedy. **CONFIRMED 2026-10-17 evening: a temporary 4 GB swap file got the deploy through, first try, with nothing else changed.** Lutan: *"yes it made it through after we added the swap"*. **That is the strongest evidence on this item and it points at (c), not (a).** The reasoning, so nobody re-runs it: the Pi has **4 GB RAM + 2 GB swap = 6 GB**, and the build was killed **three times in a row** at that size, then succeeded once ~4 GB more swap was available. **So the build's peak is somewhere above 6 GB** — on a 4 GB machine. Consequences for the three options: **(a) capping V8's heap looks WRONG, or at least unproven** — a cap below what the typecheck genuinely needs converts a kernel kill into a clean heap-OOM, not a success, and nothing here suggests a runaway that would collect if pushed; **(b) enlarging swap permanently WORKS but means a 4 GB machine permanently carrying 4+ GB of disk-backed memory** for one stage of one command, slow and wearing on the disk; **(c) dropping the typecheck from the Pi build removes the demand instead of housing it**, and the same commit has already been typechecked twice (local `gates.mjs`, then CI) before it can be deployed. **(c) is now the recommendation, not merely "looks strongest".** **One measurement would settle it and nobody has taken it:** capture the actual peak on the next Pi build (`/usr/bin/time -v npm run build` reports *Maximum resident set size*, or sample `free -m` through the run) and write the number on this item. If the peak turns out to be only a little over 6 GB, (b) is defensible as a stopgap; if it is well over, (c) is the only honest answer. **Do the measurement before the fix, not after** — the morning's item already guessed at causes twice and was corrected twice. **PARTLY CLOSED 2026-10-18 (claude/pi-deploy-safety): (1) done - `/swapfile2` is in `setup.sh` step 2b and `docs/pi-hosting.md` "Swap" explains the size; (2) done - `deploy-pi.sh` refuses below ~5.5 GiB of swap, and refuses a production/uat commit not on `origin/main`. STILL OPEN: (3) `ignoreBuildErrors` waits on the peak-memory measurement, now a step in `docs/release-procedure.md`; threshold in `docs/decisions/2026-10-18-pi-deploy-safety.md`. Not run on a real Pi yet.** **CAUSE FOUND 2026-10-19 (Lutan, during `0.37.0`), and it supersedes the recommendation above: the Turbopack build cache was starving the machine, not the app’s appetite.** The production clone’s `.next/cache` had reached 4.4 GB on a 4 GB Pi while the test clone’s was 1.2 GB and built first time every attempt; clearing it took `.next` from 4.9 GB to 450 MB and the next build compiled in 52 s. The fix now belongs to **`deploy-pi.sh` lets the Turbopack build cache grow…** (moved to Next up, 2026-10-19). **Three conclusions on this item are WITHDRAWN, do not act on them:** (1) **the peak-memory measurement is no longer worth taking** — it would have measured a machine starved by a cache, not a build needing more than 6 GB, and the cache item withdraws it as a step from `docs/release-procedure.md`; (2) **option (c) `ignoreBuildErrors` is not the answer**, because the kills happened during *compilation*, before the typecheck ran at all — so it would not have saved a single one of them; (3) **“the build’s peak is somewhere above 6 GB” is wrong**: the extra swap that appeared to fix `0.36.0` bought headroom against the same growing cache, which is why more swap and a reboot both failed on 2026-10-19. **What this item keeps, and why it stays open:** the `/swapfile2` entry in `setup.sh` and the pre-build swap check in `deploy-pi.sh` are done, are cheap, and stay — but the standing **“make a failed build LOUD”** requirement is still unmet in the case that actually happened, since four kernel kills were again noticed by a person watching rather than by the tooling. That is all that is left here.

- [x] **`git show <rev>:<path>` silently returns an error instead of the file when the path starts with a dot, and the error reads exactly like "the content is not there".** Found 2026-10-13 while checking whether a merged change had survived on `main`. Git Bash's MSYS layer treats an argument containing `:` as a Windows path-list and rewrites it — `/` becomes `\`, `:` becomes `;` — so `git show origin/main:.claude/skills/plan-day/SKILL.md` reaches git as `origin\main;.claude\skills\plan-day\SKILL.md` and dies with *fatal: ambiguous argument*. **Measured, and the trigger is narrow:** `package.json`, `docs/backlog.md` and `src/lib/status/health.ts` all work; `.claude/skills/plan-day/SKILL.md` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` both break. It is the **leading dot** — which is exactly where the skills, the workflows and the settings live. **Why it is worth an item rather than a shrug:** the failure is *invisible* when piped. `git show <rev>:<path> | grep -c "something"` prints `0`, which is indistinguishable from the file genuinely not containing it, and `| grep ...` with no match prints nothing at all. On 2026-10-13 this had me conclude that PR #557's pre-push test-plan block had been reverted from `main` by `ecfa5da5` three hours after it merged. **It had not** — `git grep -c "pre-push" origin/main -- .claude/skills/plan-day/SKILL.md` returns `1`, and `ecfa5da5` changed nothing in that file except backslash paths. A session that did not double-check would have "found" a regression that never happened, and the obvious next move — restoring the block — would have been a real corruption of `main`. **Three fixes, all verified on the failing path 2026-10-13:** prefix the command with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`, or with `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`, or avoid the colon form altogether — `git grep <pattern> <rev> -- <path>` and `git ls-tree -r <rev> --name-only -- <path>` are both immune and are usually what you actually wanted. **Done when:** the rule is written where a session reads it before reaching for the colon form (`AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`), stated as "never trust an empty result from `git show <rev>:<path>` in this shell — use `git grep`/`git ls-tree`, or prefix `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`". This is the same family as the backslash-eating bug fixed by `ecfa5da5` on 2026-10-12: **the shell rewrites arguments before the program sees them**, and both bugs cost real time because the symptom pointed at the wrong thing. [done 2026-10-13: rule + reproduction in `CLAUDE.md` ("A trap in this shell"), `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` / `git grep` / `git ls-tree`.]

So `write-env.mjs:95` (`PI_OPTIONAL_SECRETS.filter((k) => env[k])`) has nothing to write, `src/lib/status/usage.ts:108-109` reads `undefined` for both, and the tile correctly renders its grey *Not set up* state. **The tile is behaving exactly as designed; the values are simply not there.** **The likely root cause** is that the pair was only ever set as **Cloudflare Worker secrets** (`wrangler secret put`), which `scripts/deploy.mjs` hands to the Worker directly. The Worker is the *fallback*; the **Pi serves the pages**, and the Pi cannot read a wrangler secret — it reads local env files. The decision note's phrase "with both values configured" means configured *as Worker secrets*, and that is the gap. **Fix:** (1) confirm whether the pair exists as Worker secrets at all (`npx.cmd wrangler secret list --env production`) and whether the token is still valid — it may never have been created, or may have expired; (2) put both into the Pi's `.env.deploy.production` (the production values file, mode 0600, gitignored) so `write-env.mjs` picks them up on the next `deploy-pi.sh`; (3) **add a check that fails loudly rather than rendering grey** — the whole failure mode here is that "not configured" and "configured but not reaching the reader" look identical on screen. `src/lib/status/run.ts:79` already knows the key name; the System status page should distinguish *no token set* from *token set but the API refused*. (4) re-run `scripts/pi/deploy-pi.sh` and confirm a number appears. **Also decide what to do about the note.** `0.25.0` is a major release, so its note *"Settings → System status: the Website visitors tile now shows how many people visited the website, instead of saying Not set up"* was **mailed to every admin and is false**. The mail cannot be unsent. Either fix this before anyone looks, or carry a correcting line in `0.26.0`'s notes. **Lesson for the release checklist:** a release note that asserts a *configuration-dependent* thing now works needs someone to look at the live screen before the cut, not after. `docs/test-plans/pi-visitor-count.md` left exactly that as `pending:` and it was shipped on the ship-and-record call. **[FIXED 2026-10-10, same day, configuration only — no code change, no release, no version bump.]** The diagnosis above was right: both values were present on the PC in `.env.deploy.production` (which is how the Worker had them) and absent from the Pi, which is what serves the pages. Before changing anything the token was verified against Cloudflare’s API — `user/tokens/verify` returned `status=active`, and the app’s own GraphQL query returned real numbers — so the fix could not land into the same grey state. The two lines were then copied to the production Pi’s `.env.deploy.production` (piped over ssh so no value was ever printed; the file was backed up first as `.env.deploy.production.bak-20261010` and its `0600` mode is unchanged), and `scripts/pi/deploy-pi.sh --ref 590a9d35` was re-run — **pinned to the `0.25.0` release commit, so no unreviewed code shipped with the config fix.** Verified three ways: the generated `.env.production.local` now carries both keys; the app’s exact query, run on the Pi itself against the Pi’s own generated env, returned **5364 page views and 663 uniques over 7 days**; and **Lutan confirmed in chat that the tile is live**. **`0.25.0`’s fifth note is therefore true and needs no correcting line in `0.26.0`.** **Two things deliberately NOT done, both still open and worth their own items:** (1) **test is still unfixed** — the test Pi has neither value and there is no `.env.deploy.test` on the PC, so `test.lannacare.org` still shows *Not set up*; the token is zone-wide so the same pair would work. (2) ~~**The screen still cannot distinguish “no key set” from “key set but the API refused”**~~ — **WRONG, corrected 2026-10-11. #522 already did this, in this same stream. Do not file it and do not build it.** `src/lib/status/usage.ts` now returns which of the two key names is missing, which machine answered (`worker` / `pi` / `local`, the Pi marked by `PHOTO_CACHE_DIR`, which `write-env.mjs` gives only a Pi) and the file to fix; **on production a missing value is red, not grey**, because the count was promised there, and **one of the pair without the other is red anywhere**. An API refusal was already red, carrying Cloudflare's own message. So the two states are distinguishable and carry different text. See `docs/decisions/2026-10-10-visitor-count-live.md`, §*The tile now says where the value is missing*, and the comment at `usage.ts:125-131`, which says it in as many words: *"not configured" and "configured on the wrong machine" must not look the same*. The sentence above was written by the configuration fix, which landed after #522 and did not re-read what #522 had changed. **Flagged rather than quietly deleted, because this is the phantom-backlog failure exactly:** a plausible "still open" note, written in good faith by a session that had just done real work, which would have cost a whole stream. **The test is whether the bad outcome can still happen — not whether someone recorded that it could.**

A bundle cannot have that gap, because the dependency is part of the definition. `0132`’s `permission_activities.requires` already carries prerequisites between activities; jobs are the same idea one level up, and a better home for it. **The firm constraint: jobs sit above activities and do not replace them.** Enforcement stays activity-level because that is what RLS and `can()` ask (`has_permission('stock.delivery', 'edit')`), and the Edit/Read distinction has to survive *inside* a job — Purchasing means *edit* the order and *read* the stock. **A role is given jobs; a job expands to activities; a role’s rights are the union.** The Director assigns jobs; nobody but a session needs to see the activity list, which is the point. **Two consequences to design for:** jobs **overlap** (Stocktake and Purchasing both read stock figures), so a role’s rights are a union and not a partition — removing a job does not cleanly undo granting it; and **the bundles must be written by a session, not the Director**, since knowing Purchasing needs the last count, the receipts since and `safety_stock` takes reading the code. **Deliberately NOT designed up front.** Designing a dozen bundles abstractly would fail exactly as the 37-cell table did, one level higher. Instead the first roles each build their tile as a named job with an explicit bundle, and the layer is formalised from three or four worked examples: **Administer Medication** — `medical.prescriptions` (Read), `resident.record` (Read, who and where); **Do Maintenance** — `maintenance.jobs`, `maintenance.progress`; then the 2IC’s **Do the Purchasing** and **Do Stocktaking**, which are the ones that genuinely need thought about what sits underneath. - [x] **DONE 2026-10-22 (timeout, one retry, registry failure is a warning).** **CI's `audit` job HANGS and is killed after ~5 minutes, so it reports red without ever finding a vulnerability — and each stream that meets it asks Lutan what to do (small; a timeout and a retry).** Found 2026-10-22 by `/plan-day` after Lutan asked why he was getting audit failures. **The evidence:** on PR #836 the `audit` job log shows `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` starting at 02:58:18 and the job reporting `Terminate orphan process: pid (2641) (npm audit)` at **03:03:23** — five minutes later — with **no advisory output and no `found N vulnerabilities` line at all.** On PR #831 the same job passed in **10 seconds**. Run locally against the same lockfile, twice, `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` returns **`found 0 vulnerabilities`**. **So this is not a finding being reported; it is `npm audit` hanging on the registry and being terminated.** That matters because the standing rule in `CLAUDE.md` tells everyone a red `audit` means *read the advisory and establish reachability* — and here **there is no advisory to read**, so a session following the rule correctly finds nothing and asks a person. **The likely trigger:** three streams pushing within minutes of each other, so several `npm audit` calls hit the registry at once; `npm audit` has no default timeout and the job has no retry. **Do:** give the step a timeout well under the job's and a single retry, and make a timeout report as *skipped/inconclusive* rather than red — a check that cannot distinguish "no vulnerabilities" from "could not reach the registry" is worse than no check, because it trains everyone to ignore it. **Keep `continue-on-error: true`** so it still cannot block a merge. **Do NOT** change the daily `advisories.yml` to match: `ci.yml` says *"Do not 'tidy' the two to match"*, they disagree about failing on purpose by design (`docs/decisions/2026-10-02-scheduled-audit-fails-on-purpose.md`), and that was proposed and rejected on 2026-10-06. **Do NOT run `npm audit fix --force`** — it is free to move a dependency backwards across a major version. **Done when:** a registry timeout no longer shows as a red check, and a genuine advisory still does. → *Documentation*

Every brief written from now on carries it; a stream meeting a red audit reads it before it reads anything else. Original item: Every brief must carry the red-`audit` rule, because streams keep meeting a red audit and asking Lutan instead of reading `CLAUDE.md` (planner process; one paragraph added to the brief blocks).** Filed 2026-10-22 by `/plan-day`, as its own gap. **What happened:** Lutan was asked about a failed audit check **five times in five minutes across three active streams**, and each stream's advice — ignore it — was *correct*, but he had to give the same answer repeatedly. **`CLAUDE.md` already documents this at length** (*"A red `audit` check is not a blocker, and never has been"*: `continue-on-error: true`, verified across 30 pull-request runs, cannot fail a run or block a merge). **The briefs do not repeat it, and the brief is what a fresh session actually reads first** — which is exactly the reasoning that put the test-plan checker block into every brief after Lutan's 2026-10-12 complaint about the same shape of waste. **Do:** add a short block to the brief template in `.claude/skills/plan-day/SKILL.md`, beside the existing test-plan block, saying: a red `audit` cannot block your merge; do not wait on it; read the advisory and say in the PR whether the flaw is reachable; **if there is no advisory in the log, say the job was inconclusive and carry on**; and **do not ask Lutan about it** unless `audit` is red *and* an advisory names something reachable. **The general lesson worth writing down with it:** a rule that lives only in `CLAUDE.md` gets re-derived or escalated by every stream that meets it. **The test is whether a fresh session hits the situation before it has read the relevant paragraph** — if so, the rule belongs in the brief. **Done when:** the brief template carries it and a stream meeting a red audit resolves it without asking. → *Documentation*

(2) **Exactly one clinic and one live resident per name match** → create the visit (status scheduled, a note *"Created from Google Calendar"*, the audit actor *via Google Calendar*), write the `visitId` into the event's private properties and retitle it to the app's standard form, so from then on it behaves like any synced visit (moves and deletions flow back). (4) **Scope and safety:** only the shelter's vet calendar is read, never her personal calendar; an event created before this is switched on is not imported unless someone confirms it; an all-day event, or one with no resident, goes to confirm; the same event is never imported twice (keyed on the event id). ## Security

- [ ] **Promote `scripts/check-wrapped-write-paths.mjs` to a BLOCKING CI check — but ONLY after the shared header’s writes are wrapped, because today it correctly reports the rule as broken and would fail every build (small once unblocked).** Added 2026-11-01 by `write-paths-admin` (`docs/decisions/2026-11-01-write-paths-admin-sweep.md` §5). It answers the whole-page rule per page — *does every write reachable at this address go through `runWriteAction()`?* — by walking the import graph from each `page.tsx` plus the layouts above it, and names any path on `WRAPPED_WRITE_PATHS` that fails. **It is the check that would have caught `/admin/units` being listed on the day it was listed, and nothing else can:** `scripts/check-worker-origin.mjs` tests the **Worker’s** rule (which is path-agnostic, so one representative entry is genuinely enough — do not “fix” it by looping over the list), while the whole-page rule is a property of the **app**. It always exits 0 and is deliberately out of CI for now, the same shape as `check-stale-titles.mjs`. **Do this in the change that closes the header, not separately** — switched on earlier it blocks everyone, and left off after the header is fixed the rule goes back to being enforced by reading, which is what missed the header in the first place. It is a reachability heuristic (module-granular, and an action imported by a never-rendered component still counts), so it over-reports rather than under-reports, which is the safe direction.

- [ ] **Re-list the action controls on the pages the Pi-failover sweep touched against `CLAUDE.md`’s “a button is shown only if the login’s cards let it do that action” — now TWO streams deep and still not done (medium).** `CLAUDE.md` says: before a page is finished, list its action controls and the activity each one’s action asks. Stream (C) admitted it did not do this for `src/app/admin/units/UnitsTable.tsx` (`docs/decisions/2026-10-31-write-request-wrapper.md` §7), and `write-paths-admin` did not do it for the thirteen files it converted on 2026-11-01 (`docs/decisions/2026-11-01-write-paths-admin-sweep.md` §8). **Neither stream changed whether any control is drawn — only how it calls — and every existing gate is untouched, so this is an unmade check rather than a known fault.** But it is now owed across `/admin/units`, `/admin/zones`, `/admin/blood-test-types`, `/admin/procedure-types`, `/admin/immunization-types`, `/admin/medications`, `/admin/enclosures`, `/admin/stocktaking`, `/admin/recent-changes`, `/admin/shop`, the four `/admin/diets` addresses, `/admin/who-does-what` (+ `features`) and `/admin/facility-map`, and doing it in one pass is cheaper than a note per stream. **Read the activity from the action’s own `can(perms, …)` or the RPC’s `has_permission(…)`, never from the control’s label.** A control found ungated is a finding, not a licence to name a role.

It is true *today* only because no card bundles that activity (`cards.ts` kept it out of Manage medical on purpose), which is a fact about the current card set, not a rule — so the sentence becomes false the moment a card is given it, and it names a role in user-facing copy, which `CLAUDE.md` forbids. **DO:** reword it in `src/lib/i18n/dictionaries/en.ts` and `th.ts` to name the activity ("Withdraw a death recorded in error") rather than Admin. **Sequence it with** the two strings below (`assistant.volunteerReadOnly`, `assistant.pageSubtitleReadOnly`): same file, same fault, one PR. **NOT this item:** the manual's own prose, which was fixed in #TBD.
- [ ] **Teach `translations-open` about label drafts — ITS TRIGGER HAS NOW FIRED, so nothing is left to decide and it is buildable now (small).** **TRIGGER MET, MEASURED BY THE PLANNER 2026-11-01:** production is 296 of 296, so `0293` and `0294` **are** applied, `label_drafts` exists there, and the planner re-ran `check-production.mjs translations-open --env production` after #1144 — it reports **94 missing, 1 out of date** and, for the first time, **_Every registered label pair is counted_**. So the old title's condition (*"ONLY once `0293` and `0294` are applied to production, and not before"*) is **SUPERSEDED 2026-11-01** and the exact edit recorded beside the check can be made. **Asked for by #1144's own deliverable 4**, which deliberately left it alone and said so. Filed 2026-10-31 by `claude/translations-labels-app` (`docs/decisions/2026-10-31-label-drafts-the-app-half.md`, §5), which was asked to decide this and decided *not yet*. **Why it is not already done, and why the obvious workarounds do not exist:** `buildQuery()` in `scripts/lib/readonly-checks.mjs` wraps a check's SQL in a `do $o$ … $o$` block, and `assertSelectOnly()` allows **one statement** starting with `select` or `with`. Every relation is therefore resolved when that block is planned, so a query naming `label_drafts` **stops** on a database that has no such table — which production is today. `to_regclass` cannot guard it (the guard still names the relation), and a probe-then-choose or dynamic SQL is outside what the harness accepts. A check that stops reports **nothing**; one that under-reports by a known amount is strictly better, and on production that amount is **zero**, because a database with no `label_drafts` can hold no drafts. **The trigger:** `node scripts/apply-migrations.mjs --status --env production` shows `0293` and `0294` applied. **The edit, already written out in a comment beside the check:** add `left join label_drafts d on d.table_name = a.table_name and d.row_id = a.row_id and d.column_name = a.column_name` to the `label_state` CTE, and give a row with no live Thai and a draft the state `proposed`, counted apart from `missing` — which is what `label_translations()` does and what the screen shows. **Measured on dev 2026-10-31, so the cost of waiting is a number:** the check says **383 missing labels** where the screen says **311 missing and 72 waiting**. **Not this item:** the `uncovered` empty-table fault (its own item), which is a different reason the check can mislead.

Fold them in. One schema PR; nothing a user sees. FILED 2026-10-30 by the planner.** **Why this is filed at all:** every instance of it was recorded only in a route comment, a decision file or the tail of a **ticked** backlog item, so there was nothing on the board to schedule and nothing to tick — the invisible-work fault, three times over. **What the function is:** `can_see_drive_file(p_drive_file_id)` (`0193`, touched by `0218` and `0276`) is the single access decision the file routes ask, **as the caller**, so RLS answers it; `/api/photos/[fileId]` and `/api/videos/[fileId]` call it before any disk read, and `/api/documents/[fileId]` (PR #1095) does too. It reads `attachments`, `community_outing_photos`, `maintenance_photos`, `medication`, `project_photos`, `shelter_friends` and `stock_medications`. **The three that are NOT in it, each checked in app code beside it instead:** (1) **memes**, since `docs/decisions/2026-10-18-meme-library-app.md`, because that app half carried no migration — the photo route's own comment says *"fold it into that function in the next schema PR"*; (2) **donation receipts** (`donation_receipts`, asked for `donation.receipt`) and (3) **the resident deceased summary and offline index** (a `residents` row), both added 2026-10-30 by PR #1095, whose decision file repeats the same *"fold into the function in the next schema PR"*. **This is NOT a hard-coded-security breach and `check-hard-coded-security.mjs` is clean** (verified 2026-10-30: *no coded security outside the Admin bypass*) — each app-code check is still asked as the caller, so RLS still decides and no role name is read. **The fault is that one access decision now lives in four places**, so a change to who may read a receipt has to be made in app code while the same question about an attachment is answered in SQL, and only one of the two is visible to a policy review or to a migration. **DO:** one migration extending `can_see_drive_file()` to answer for memes, `donation_receipts` and the `residents` summary/index rows with the same activities the app code asks today, then delete the app-code checks from `src/app/api/photos/[fileId]/route.ts` and `src/app/api/documents/[fileId]/route.ts` so the routes ask one question again. **Prove it per kind, both ways:** a login that can see each kind still gets 200, and one that cannot still gets the indistinguishable 404 — that 404 is deliberate, so a visitor cannot tell an internal file from a made-up id, and it must survive. **Watch out for:** `scripts/check-can-see-drive-file.mjs` **exceeded 100 s and has never been diagnosed** (on the harness item), so the check that would prove this is itself unproven — diagnose it first or say you could not. **Schema first, as its own PR** (`CLAUDE.md`), and **only one migration-carrying stream per batch**. → *Security*

- [x] **A REGISTER OF ALREADY-ASSESSED ADVISORY IDS, SO THE `audit` CHECK GOES RED ONLY FOR SOMETHING NEW. OFFERED TO LUTAN 2026-10-25 AND DECLINED FOR REASONS THAT NO LONGER HOLD — he asked for it again on 2026-10-28, so this is a genuine change of circumstances, NOT a settled question being re-raised.** **THE HISTORY, because without it this reads as a fresh idea he already said no to:** `docs/decisions/2026-10-25-audit-on-releases-not-every-pr.md` records it verbatim under *The residual risk* — *"Not included (offered, not chosen): a list of already-assessed advisory ids the job ignores until a review date."* He chose the other option instead: scope the PR `audit` job to run only on PRs that change `package.json` or `package-lock.json`. **That was sound at the time** — a job that rarely runs needs no register. **WHAT CHANGED:** the scoping never actually worked. `deps-changed` was never written out, so the job silently skipped **everything**, release cuts included — that is the bug `#1041` fixed on 2026-10-27. The first cut it genuinely ran on was `0.40.10` (2026-10-28), **which went red**. So the premise behind the refusal — "it hardly ever runs" — is gone, and the real state is: **a release cut always changes `package.json`, so `audit` now runs on every cut, and will be red on every cut** until the one open advisory is fixed upstream. **A permanently red check is the thing `CLAUDE.md` warns becomes noise people filter.** **WHAT TO BUILD, with the proven in-repo precedent:** the same shape as `docs/hard-coded-security-registry.json` — a register where each entry is a **named record** (advisory id, date assessed, why it is not reachable here, and the decision file), the check **passes** anything registered and **fails on any id not on it**, so a new advisory is the only thing a person ever sees. The seven existing decision files are the first entries, `docs/decisions/2026-10-28-glob-cli-advisory-not-reachable.md` and `2026-10-24-audit-body-parser-undici-not-reachable.md` among them. `npm audit` has no native ignore, so the register is read by a wrapper around `audit:prod`, not by npm. **THE CATCH, AND IT IS THE REASON TO DESIGN THIS CAREFULLY RATHER THAN QUICKLY:** a registered advisory stops being re-examined. `glob` is harmless today **only because nothing in this repo runs its CLI** — if code were later added that does, the register would keep saying "fine" and nobody would look again. The security registry handles the equivalent by failing when a record's recorded text disappears; the audit version needs each entry to record **why it is unreachable in checkable terms** (here: no invocation of the `glob` binary in `package.json`, `scripts/` or `worker/`, and absent from the built `worker.js`) and to be re-read when that area changes. **A register that only stores "we looked once" is worse than the red.** **THE RULE IT TOUCHES, named rather than worked around:** `CLAUDE.md` says not to change the PR job's `continue-on-error`, timeout or retry **to make the red go away**. A register is arguably a different thing — it demands a decision per advisory rather than hiding them, and it goes red for anything new — and **Lutan confirmed that distinction and said to schedule it, 2026-10-28** (*"Item B - schedule it"*), so **nothing is left to decide and nobody owes an answer** — build it.
