Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-check-harness-crashes.md`. → *Security* **DONE 2026-10-16:** `scripts/check-cards-count.mjs` plus a `cards-count` job in `ci.yml` (no `continue-on-error`; not a required check — Lutan's call). `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cards-count-in-ci-and-worktree-ports.md`.
- [x] **The three website tables (`site_content`, `site_pages`, `site_content_photos`) are readable by every login, not just the website editors — including the public-viewer and clinic logins, and including `clinic_visit_estimate`, which the public view hides.** From the 2026-10-13 database review (F2), ranked its second finding. `public_read_site_*` (`0018`, `0059`) are `using (true)`; `0122` only revoked `anon`, so every authenticated role still reads them. Replace them with `(select has_permission('website.content', 'read'))`; the `public_site_*` views keep the public read, so nothing a visitor sees changes. **Migration: yes, small. About an hour.** `scripts/check-public-views.mjs` and `scripts/check-app-access-gate.mjs` are the proof. **Filed 2026-10-14 on Lutan's instruction** — the review raised it without filing, by design, and he picked all three of F2, F4 and W1. **Note the exposure concretely:** `clinic_visit_estimate` is the vet-visit budget figure the public view deliberately omits, and a clinic login can read it today. → *Security* **Done: 0195 (claude/security-schema-fold). Read needs website.content Read or reports.cashflow Read, because the forecast reads the estimate.**
- [x] **Audit the moves, the role grants and the money: add `record_audit()` to `placement_history`, `user_roles`, `maintenance`, `maintenance_bills`, `bills_inbox`, `stock_receipts`, `blood_tests`, `procedures` and `resident_diets`, and let service-role scripts name an actor.** From the 2026-10-13 database review (F4): **18 tables are audited and 43 writable ones are not**, so there is no record of who moved a resident, who changed a login's role, or who entered a bill. Also **1,402 of dev's 1,529 audit rows have no actor**, because `auth.uid()` is null for the service role. Nine trigger lines; have `record_audit()` fall back to `current_setting('app.actor', true)`, which `scripts/correct-resident.mjs` and its siblings set. **Migration: yes, small. About an hour.** **Extends the 2026-10-01 audit-log decision rather than reversing it** — read that first. **Filed 2026-10-14 on Lutan's instruction.** → *Security* **Done: 0195. user_roles has no id, so record_audit() falls back to user_id. No script sets app.actor yet; the fallback is ready for them.**
- [x] **`maintenance_bills.bill_date` defaults to the UTC day, and two round-status views nobody reads filter on `CURRENT_DATE`.** From the 2026-10-13 database review (W1). `0189` wrote `default current_date` where `0073`'s `shelter_today()` is the rule; the forms send a date, so **only a direct insert is dated a day early, and only before 07:00 Thai**. `prescription_round_status`, `resident_diet_round_status` and `frequency_round_status` (`0137`/`0138`) **have no reader anywhere in `src/` or `worker/`**: drop them, or move them to `shelter_today()` if they are wanted — say which and why. **Migration: yes, about ten lines. Ten minutes.** **Filed 2026-10-14 on Lutan's instruction.** **Fold this into the same schema PR as F2 and F4** — all three are small migrations and only one may be in flight at a time. → *Security* **Done: 0195. Views kept and moved to shelter_today(): scripts read them.**

- [x] **CONFIRMED 2026-10-19 and CLOSED: the Pi refuses a keyless request.** #551 added the check to `src/proxy.ts` so the Pi refuses a request that reaches `pi.lannacare.org` without the shared secret, rather than trusting the Cloudflare WAF rule alone. `pi-token-off` then copied `ORIGIN_KEY` into the Pi's `.env.deploy.production` on 2026-10-12, so the value is in place. **But the Pi is serving `0.27.0`, which predates #551, so nothing on the Pi checks the header today.** It starts working at the next Pi deploy (`./scripts/pi/deploy-pi.sh`) and not before. **Why this is worth its own item:** the protection reads as shipped — the code is on `main`, the secret is on the Pi, the PR is merged and its test plan is signed — and the only record that it is not yet live is one row of that test plan's manual table, where no planner or release pass would ever see it. Until the deploy happens, an edited, disabled or displaced WAF rule still puts the Pi's `next start` in front of anyone who finds the hostname, which is precisely what #551 was for. **Done when** a Pi deploy carrying #551 has happened and a request to the Pi without the header is confirmed refused (the test clone uses the same key, so it can be checked there first). No code change expected. See `docs/decisions/2026-10-12-pi-checks-origin-key.md` and `docs/test-plans/pi-token-off.md` row 5. **Staleness sweep 2026-10-14:** the Pi deploy this waits for has happened: the Pi served `0.28.0` (`b5fd020d`) and then `0.29.0` (`9cb36eea`) on 2026-10-13 (`docs/releases/2026-10-13.md`), and both contain #551. So "the Pi is serving 0.27.0" is out of date. What remains is the confirmation: a request to the Pi without the header is refused. No release record or test plan shows that yet. **CONFIRMED 2026-10-19.** Production answered `Forbidden` to a direct origin request **without** the header - observed repeatedly while diagnosing the false `DEPLOY FAILED` banner, with and without a `Host:` header. That is exactly the refusal this item asked someone to confirm. #750 then made `deploy-pi.sh` send the key on its version probe, and `scripts/pi/build-lib.test.mjs` covers a fake origin that answers only with the right `x-origin-key` (7/7). **Lutan confirmed 2026-10-19 that he considered this done.**

**Moved above Deployment on 2026-09-30 (Lutan): severity governs here, not
file position.** The review appended this section at the end of the file,
which by this file's own convention ("ordered by suggested priority") read as
the lowest priority in the backlog while it held the only High finding and a
live open redirect. That was an artifact of how it was written, not a
judgement — so the section was moved rather than left to mislead the next
planner.

From the 2026-09-30 security assessment (`docs/security/security-assessment-2026-09-30.docx`, `.pdf`; commit d26103b, release 0.10.0). Finding IDs (DB-n, CODE-n, WEB-n) are the report's. No Critical finding; one High. Items are grouped so each is one stream; schema items are `claude/<name>-schema` PRs first, per the migrations rules. Effort is the report's. None of these makes the app harder for field staff.

- [x] **A vet login can read, rename, add and delete every project and maintenance photo record (Medium).** **Done 2026-10-09** (`0174_close_the_remaining_over_grants.sql`, `claude/close-the-remaining-over-grants`; `docs/decisions/2026-10-09-clinic-login-allow-lists.md`): the four `doctor_*_attachments` policies name only `resident`, `blood_test` and `procedure`, `doctor_can_write_attachment()` ends `else false`, and `doctor_read_translations` reads residents only. Proved under a doctor JWT by `scripts/check-clinic-allow-lists.mjs` (9 failures before, 18 of 18 after) and the surface probe (doctor attachments read 160 → 14, update/delete 158 → 12, translations 46 → 0). Found 2026-10-09 by the dynamic half of the security assessment (`permission-measure-and-probe`, `scripts/probe-role-surface.mjs`; `docs/security/security-assessment-2026-10-09-dynamic.md`, which has the evidence). The four `vet_*_attachments` policies (`0110`, carried unchanged by `0167`) let a clinic login through for any `owner_type` **not** in `('resident', 'blood_test', 'procedure')`, and `vet_can_write_attachment()` ends `else true`, so project and maintenance photos fall through. Under a vet's JWT on dev it read 144 project and 2 maintenance rows, renamed all 144, deleted all 146 and inserted a new project attachment. `vet_read_translations` has the same shape (`table_name <> 'residents'`), so the vet also reads the Thai text of maintenance jobs, recurring jobs, project folders, Shelter Friends and site pages. Not in the roles paper's C table, and not what the 2026-10-07 "leave vets as they are" decision was about: that kept the vet's clinical access, and project photos are the public site's pictures. **DECIDED 2026-10-09 by Lutan: no — lock it to clinical records only.** Turn the five policies into allow-lists naming only `resident`, `blood_test` and `procedure`, drop the `else true` from `vet_can_write_attachment()`, and close `vet_read_translations` the same way — a clinic login has no reason to read the Thai text of maintenance jobs, recurring jobs, project folders, Shelter Friends or site pages. Project photos are the public site's pictures. The original framing is kept below for the reasoning: should a clinic login see project and maintenance photos at all? If not, turn the five policies into allow-lists (name the three clinical types, drop the `else true`) in one small re-runnable migration with a harness under a vet's JWT; about an hour. Does not give the vet any cells. **Raised with Lutan 2026-10-09 by `close-the-over-grants`; not built, waiting for his answer** (the recommendation stands: no, allow-lists). **Names since 0172 (2026-10-09, vet-to-doctor-rename):** the vet login is the **doctor** login, the policies are `doctor_*_attachments` / `doctor_read_translations`, and the function is `doctor_can_write_attachment()`; the rename changed no behaviour here, so the finding stands.

- [x] **`reset_prescription_rounds()`, `reset_frequency_rounds()` and `reset_diet_rounds()` can be called by any signed-in login (Medium-low; silent).** Found 2026-10-09 by the dynamic half of the security assessment (`permission-measure-and-probe`, `scripts/probe-role-surface.mjs`; `docs/security/security-assessment-2026-10-09-dynamic.md`, which has the evidence). They run as their owner, ask nothing about the caller, and are granted to `authenticated` (`0137`, `0138`); only triggers call them, no app code does. As a login with **no role** (which reads 0 prescriptions) `reset_prescription_rounds(<id>)` replaced a prescription's custom rounds with its frequency's defaults: the medication list then shows a dose at the wrong round, and nothing says so. Needs the id (a UUID), so the realistic caller is an archived former volunteer or a vet who has seen one. `check-medication-rounds.mjs` asserts `norole` cannot write `prescription_rounds` through the table, which holds, and never looked through the function. **Fix:** `revoke execute … from authenticated` on the three (the triggers that call them also run as owner, so nothing in the app changes) plus a line in `check-medication-rounds.mjs`. Schema PR; ten minutes. **CLOSED 2026-10-09 (`close-the-over-grants`, `0170` §2, commit 4586418f):** execute revoked from `authenticated` (and `public`, `anon`) on all three; `service_role` keeps it. `check-medication-rounds.mjs` now calls each function under every login with a real id, before it replays `0137`/`0138` (the replay re-grants them inside its transaction): 18 red before, green after.

- [x] **The facility map tables answer every signed-in login, including the public viewer and archived people (Low).** Found 2026-10-09 by the dynamic half of the security assessment (`permission-measure-and-probe`, `scripts/probe-role-surface.mjs`; `docs/security/security-assessment-2026-10-09-dynamic.md`, which has the evidence). `facility_maps_read` (`0142`) and `map_rooms_read` (`0157`) are `to authenticated using (true)`, kept on purpose when the writes converted (`0150`, `0158`), but that reaches `public_viewer`, a login with no role and an archived person, which the app-access gate keeps out of every other internal table. It is the shelter's layout, not personal data. **Fix:** add `has_app_access()` (or `has_shelter_floor()`) to the two read policies, and the two tables to `check-app-access-gate.mjs`. (`rounds` is open the same way, but `check-medication-rounds.mjs` asserts it deliberately and it holds only round names: leave it.) **CLOSED 2026-10-09 (`close-the-over-grants`, `0170` §3, commit f08de41f):** both read policies ask `private.has_app_access()`; `check-app-access-gate.mjs` lists both tables (red before: archived, roleless and `public_viewer` each read 3 `facility_maps` rows; green after). `rounds` left open as the item says.

- [x] **A vet login lists every person with a login, with their role (Low).** **Done 2026-10-09** (`0174`, same PR): `private.app_users` shows a clinic login only itself and the doctors at its current clinics; the volunteer case is unchanged (the harness asserts the volunteer still sees every login an admin does, without emails). The role enum column stays for `perm-drop-enum`. Found 2026-10-09 by the dynamic half of the security assessment (`permission-measure-and-probe`, `scripts/probe-role-surface.mjs`; `docs/security/security-assessment-2026-10-09-dynamic.md`, which has the evidence). `app_users` (`0146`) blanks emails for vets and volunteers but not names, roles or `archived_at`, so an outside clinic sees all 57 logins and who is Admin. The volunteer sees the same, which the recurring-jobs pickers use; no vet screen reads it. **DECIDED 2026-10-09 by Lutan: narrow `private.app_users` for a clinic login to its own clinic's doctors only.** Emails are already blanked; names, roles and `archived_at` are not, and no clinic screen reads the list. **Volunteers read the same view for the recurring-jobs pickers, and that must keep working** — narrow the clinic case without changing the volunteer case. Note the view still names the role enum, so it is one of the views `perm-drop-enum` waits on anyway. **Raised with Lutan 2026-10-09 by `close-the-over-grants`; not decided.** **Since 0172 (2026-10-09):** the vet login is the doctor login; unchanged by the rename, so the finding stands.

- [x] **Next 16.3.5 carries a Critical RCE advisory; the fix is a patch bump that is "outside the stated dependency range" (Critical).** Surfaced 2026-10-01 by the new `audit` job on PR #265, which is — as far as the run history shows — the first PR to execute it: `next 16.2.0 - 16.3.5`, **critical**, *"Next.js: Remote Code Execution in next/og ImageResponse"*, [GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j), `fix available via npm audit fix --force`, `Will install next@16.3.8, which is outside the stated dependency range`. `package.json` pins `"next": "16.3.5"`, so **`main`, test and production are all affected equally** — this is not a property of the PR that found it. **Worth putting beside the 2026-09-30 assessment, which recorded "No Critical findings":** that was true of the code, and the first Critical to appear came from the supply chain instead, caught by a job the same security batch added. The chain is what the review could not see by reading the repo. **The mitigating fact, and it is a real one:** `next/og` and `ImageResponse` appear **nowhere** in `src/` or `worker/` (grepped 2026-10-01), so the vulnerable entry point is not reachable in this app — the dependency is vulnerable, the code path is unused. That is the difference between "patch on the next convenient day" and "stop and patch now", and it is why this is a backlog item rather than a hotfix. Do not treat it as safe indefinitely, though: a future feature that wants an Open Graph image would reach for exactly that API, and the person adding it will not know this. **Why it is not a one-line bump:** `AGENTS.md` opens by saying this is a modified Next whose APIs, conventions and file structure may differ from training data, and npm itself reports `16.3.8` as outside the declared range. So it needs its own PR: read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` and the upstream notes for 16.3.6–16.3.8, bump, run the full gates, and **check the two things this project has already been bitten by around builds** — that `strip-baked-env` still finds and empties `next-env.mjs` (its shape is an OpenNext implementation detail), and that `getSiteOrigin()`'s header reading still behaves on the Pi behind cloudflared, since a sign-in outage on 30 September came from exactly that area. **Also fix the reporting gap this exposed:** `audit` is `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, so a push to `main` skips it and nothing reports a new advisory between PRs — an advisory published on a quiet day is invisible until someone happens to open a PR. Its `continue-on-error: true` is correct and should stay (the job's own comment argues the case well, and contrasts it with `test-plan`), but "reported, not enforced" only works if it is actually reported: consider running it on a schedule as well, so a Critical lands somewhere a person sees without a PR to carry it. **Status 2026-10-02:** the bump landed (#268, Next 16.3.8) and the reporting gap is closed by `.github/workflows/advisories.yml` (daily, fails on purpose; docs/decisions/2026-10-02-scheduled-audit-fails-on-purpose.md). **Still open, so not ticked:** `getSiteOrigin()`/sign-in on the Pi behind cloudflared has not been confirmed on 16.3.8 (#268 verified sign-in on a local production build only, and was not deployed). **Status 2026-10-06 (verified by `/plan-day`, not ticked): the Critical is RESOLVED.** `48b1a27a` *"Bump next and eslint-config-next to 16.3.8 for GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j"* landed the fix, so `package.json` now pins **`next: 16.3.8`** — the version the advisory names — and `npm audit --audit-level=critical` reports **no critical vulnerabilities**. `next/og` and `ImageResponse` are still absent from `src/` and `worker/`, so the re-grep the item asked for still holds. **The 5 high-severity advisories that remain are dev-only:** `npm audit --omit=dev` finds **0 vulnerabilities**; the highs are `fast-glob` reached through `@next/eslint-plugin-next` → `eslint-config-next`, i.e. the lint toolchain, not anything shipped. **Left unticked deliberately** — the item also carries the standing warning that a future Open Graph feature would reach for exactly that API and the person adding it will not know this, so whoever owns Security should decide whether that warning belongs somewhere more durable than a closed backlog item before ticking. **Closed 2026-10-07 (claude/next-og-warning-durable):** the standing warning now has a durable home — `scripts/check-next-og.mjs`, run by `npm run lint`, fails if `next/og`/`ImageResponse`/an OG convention file appears while Next is below 16.3.8 (docs/decisions/2026-10-07-next-og-warning-lives-in-lint.md). Re-verified: `npm audit --omit=dev` 0 vulnerabilities, no `next/og` in `src/` or `worker/`. Not confirmed: `getSiteOrigin()` on the Pi behind cloudflared on 16.3.8 — file separately if still wanted.

- [x] **Encrypt the weekly backup and keep session tables out of it (DB-1, High).** **Done 2026-10-02** (rollout in `docs/decisions/2026-10-02-backup-encryption-rollout.md`, code in #243): key pair made by Lutan, private key in two places only; first encrypted production run on the Pi (`.dump.age`, link not logged); a decrypt rehearsal gave a valid archive with the session and MFA tables absent; old plaintext dumps deleted on the Pi and in Drive, `backup.log` truncated; `Backups/` moved to `Admin/Backups`, shared with Lutan only; every production session and refresh token rotated. Left over, split out as its own item below: clearing the MFA factors. The restore itself belongs to DB-2 and the Deployment restore item. `scripts/backup.mjs:44` dumps `public` and `auth` with `pg_dump` and uploads the file to the shelter's Drive as-is; `auth` holds password hashes, TOTP secrets in plain text and live refresh tokens, and line 104 logs the shareable link to `backup.log`. Encrypt before upload with a key kept only by the administrator (age, gpg or `openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2`; key in a password manager, never the repo or `.env`), add `--exclude-table=auth.refresh_tokens --exclude-table=auth.sessions --exclude-table='auth.mfa_*'`, put `Backups/` in a folder shared with the admin only rather than the application root, and stop logging the web link. Then rehearse a restore. Half a day. **Do first.** **Update 2026-09-30:** the weekly backup now runs on the Raspberry Pi as well as the laptop (`--local-copy`, cron Sundays 03:00), so **the Pi's SSD also holds plaintext dumps**, and its `~/backups/backup.log` collects the Drive link every week. Encrypt with `age` public-key encryption so the decrypting key never sits on the Pi, and encrypt before both the upload and the local copy. **Status 2026-09-30:** code done in PR #243 (age public key, exclusions, link no longer logged, tile reads `.dump.age`); **left open until Lutan** generates the key pair, installs the public key on the Pi and laptop, does the first run and the restore rehearsal, deletes the old plaintext dumps and the Pi's `backup.log`, re-shares `Backups/` and rotates (test plan manual table).
- [x] **Clear the production MFA factors left over from DB-1, and re-enrol.** From the DB-1 rollout (2026-10-02): Lutan's authenticator (TOTP) secret was in the plaintext dumps that were exposed before encryption, and the factors were not cleared when sessions were rotated. Lutan is the only person with one. **Done 2026-10-10:** Lutan ran `node scripts/bootstrap-admin.mjs --env production --reset-2step <his email>` from the main checkout ("removed 1 authenticator app(s) … on production (dbkodyyxxhtygxcxmfcu)"), set up a new app on Settings → Security and is back in at 2-step. **Do not use the SQL this item first suggested (`delete from auth.mfa_factors;`)**: since the 2026-10-01 rule (`docs/decisions/2026-10-01-first-authenticator-needs-an-admin-to-open-it.md`) a new app can only be set up inside a window opened from outside the session, and a bare delete leaves it shut. With no other admin that locks Security until `--allow-2step-setup` is run. The routes are Security's **Reset** (also allowed on your own login) or `--reset-2step`, both of which open the window.
- [x] **Backups from an always-on machine, and a rehearsed restore (DB-2).** **Always-on half done 2026-09-30, closed 2026-10-04:** the weekly backup runs from cron on the Pi (Sundays 03:00, `docs/decisions/2026-09-30-one-pi-hosting-and-backup.md`), and a red Weekly backup tile already emails admins (`src/lib/status/alerts.ts`). **The restore rehearsal was not done** and is carried by "Rehearse a restore from a production backup" (Deployment) rather than kept open in two places; retiring the laptop schedule is the "Confirm the Pi's first scheduled backup" item. The scheduled task runs only while the developer's Windows account is logged on (`scripts/backup-schedule.ps1:43-46`); `backup.log` shows two manual runs (21 and 26 Sep), and the restore procedure has never been tested. Move the schedule to a GitHub Actions workflow or the Pi in `docs/pi-hosting.md`, restore once into a scratch Supabase project and write the steps down, repeat quarterly, and have the "Weekly backup" status tile alert admins when it goes red. A day, including the rehearsal. Do together with the item above. **THE SUPABASE HALF IS DONE — 2026-10-19, and this item's "is now its own item" promise is hereby closed rather than left dangling** (`docs/decisions/2026-10-19-restore-drill-real-supabase.md`, README "Backups"). A fresh production backup was decrypted and restored into a **throwaway Supabase project** (`ffaqchioswdmloaclhxu`): **82 public base tables, 53 views including the `private` ones, 324 policies, 304 residents, `auth.users` 5**; RLS was checked per role (staff saw 304, anon 0, an archived role 0) and a **real password sign-in** returned 304 of 304. It answered the open privileges question — default privileges gave `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` access to all 82 tables with no manual grants — and corrected the README recipe (restore `auth.users` then `auth.identities` as separate data-only calls, because `postgres` cannot set `session_replication_role` on Supabase; ~493 `DROP … IF EXISTS` errors are noise; it is slow over the internet and a 120 s timeout cuts it off). **Lutan has since done it more than once.** So no item is owed here: `/plan-day` filed one on 2026-10-22 and withdrew it the same hour, having read this item's status note and the backlog but **not `docs/decisions/`** — the exact fault the plan-day skill's step 3 warns about.
- [x] **HTTP security headers and Secure cookies (WEB-2).** *Done in the Worker; the CSP is report-only, tightening owed (see docs/decisions/2026-09-30-security-headers-in-the-worker.md).* Nothing sets CSP, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or nosniff, and the Supabase cookie is created without `secure`. Add `headers()` in `next.config.ts` (or the Worker): `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self), geolocation=()`, HSTS if the Cloudflare zone does not already send it; CSP in report-only first (`default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; frame-src https://www.google.com`), tighten after a quiet week; `cookieOptions: { secure: true }` in production on both Supabase client factories. Camera must stay allowed for photos and QR scanning. Also covers CODE-7's proxy half (`nosniff` and `Content-Disposition` on `src/app/api/photos/[fileId]/route.ts`).
- [x] **Tighten the CSP (WEB-2 follow-up).** *Collection is done (2026-10-01, `claude/csp-tighten-and-collect`): the Worker answers `POST /api/csp-report` and logs a bounded one-line summary per violation, readable in Workers Logs (search `csp-report`); `docs/decisions/2026-10-01-csp-report-collection.md`. Enforcement is deliberately not on, because no reports existed before that change.* **Gate: after the collector has been deployed to production for a week**, read every `csp-report` line and explain or fix each distinct (directive, blocked) pair; if the week is thin or has unexplained hits, wait longer. Then: switch `content-security-policy-report-only` to `content-security-policy` in `worker/security-headers.mjs` (keep `frame-src https://www.google.com`, `img-src 'self' data: blob:` and `camera=(self)`); drop `'unsafe-inline'` from `script-src` with nonces only if they can reach every inline script on **both** render paths (the Pi's `next start` and the Worker's OpenNext render), otherwise leave it and say why; consider raising HSTS above six months once stable. A blocking CSP breaks public pages for visitors, so check `/`, `/adopt`, `/our-work`, a Shelter Friend page and the camera on a phone before merging. **CHECKED 2026-10-07 (staleness sweep) — built and merged today; not ticked because what is left is a person looking.** `59238341` (#431, `claude/csp-enforce`, 2026-10-07): `worker/security-headers.mjs` sends `content-security-policy` (line 46). The gate was read from the live logs: 190 reports in six days, every one Cloudflare's injected Web Analytics beacon, which `/privacy` says is not there, so blocking it is right. `'unsafe-inline'` stays, with the reason this item asked for (nonces cannot reach both render paths), and HSTS stays at six months: `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-csp-enforced.md`. **Still open:** the five checks in `docs/test-plans/csp-enforce.md` *Left for manual verification* (public pages, a Shelter Friend page, a staff page and the camera on a phone, after the production deploy). **DONE 2026-10-08:** live since `0.21.0` (both sites send `content-security-policy`); all five checks recorded in `docs/test-plans/csp-enforce.md` and the plan signed (Lutan: the pages he looked at and the phone camera; Claude: the header and the browser pass on production, where the only thing blocked was the Cloudflare beacon). - [x] **A high advisory in `sharp` reaches the production tree through the Cloudflare build chain, and the only fix npm offers is a breaking `wrangler` change.** Found 2026-10-07 on PR #405's `audit` job, one day after the `source-map-js` high was closed by #398. **The advisory:** `sharp <0.35.5`, **high**, [GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w) — *Vulnerability in librsvg dependency*, CVE-2026-96889. **How it reaches production:** `@opennextjs/cloudflare@1.20.6` is a **`dependencies`** entry (wrangler itself is only a devDependency, which is why this is easy to misread) → `wrangler@4.135.0` → `miniflare@5.x-alpha` → `sharp@0.35.4`; **`next` also pulls `sharp@0.35.4` directly**. So `npm audit --omit=dev` sees it and `npm run audit:prod` fails. **Why it is not a one-liner:** `npm audit fix --force` reports *"Will install wrangler@4.15.2, which is a breaking change"* — a major move of the Cloudflare build chain, which is how the app is built and deployed. **Do not take that fix inside an unrelated PR**, and weigh a narrower route first: a newer `@opennextjs/cloudflare` that depends on a patched wrangler, a `sharp` bump on its own, or an `overrides` entry pinning `sharp >= 0.35.5` (noting an override pins a transitive dependency behind the maintainer's back and needs removing when upstream catches up). **Reachability is worth establishing before urgency:** the flaw is in **librsvg**, i.e. SVG rendering inside `sharp`. Next only processes SVGs through its image optimiser when `dangerouslyAllowSVG` is set — **check whether it is** — and `miniflare` is the local Worker simulator, which does not run in production. If no untrusted SVG reaches `sharp`, this is *"patch on the next convenient day"* rather than a hotfix, which is exactly the judgement the Next RCE item recorded for `next/og`. **Expect `advisories.yml` to be red daily until it is settled** — that is the design (it fails on purpose so a human is emailed), and **the PR `audit` job will be red on every open PR meanwhile, which does not block merging** (`continue-on-error: true`, deliberate; `ci.yml` says *"Do not 'tidy' the two to match"*). **Say so on any PR that meets it**, so nobody re-derives it. **DONE 2026-10-07 (`claude/sharp-override`):** the narrower route this item asked to weigh first was the right one — `"overrides": { "sharp": "^0.35.5" }` in `package.json` plus the lockfile, and `npm run audit:prod` goes from **4 high to 0 vulnerabilities**. The breaking `wrangler` downgrade was **not** taken, and the reason is worth keeping: there is no newer release to move to — `miniflare` pins `sharp` at exactly `0.35.4` and every current `wrangler` pins that `miniflare` — so npm's only route was backwards, and a major regression of the chain that builds and deploys the app is the larger risk by a wide margin. **Reachability was established before urgency, and it is nil:** `next.config.ts` sets `images: { unoptimized: true }` and `dangerouslyAllowSVG` appears nowhere in the repo, so the `sharp`-backed image optimiser is never invoked, and `miniflare` is the local Worker simulator, which does not run in production. Hygiene, on the same reading the `next/og` item recorded. `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-sharp-override.md` has the argument and the condition under which it expires. Verified with `npm run opennext:build` as well as the three gates, because `next build` never loads `wrangler` or `miniflare` and so cannot exercise the pin that was overridden. **What the red cost, now addressed in CLAUDE.md:** it stalled the production release manager for about 45 minutes on 2026-10-07 working out whether the release could proceed, and it had been red on every PR for two days with nobody asking why. CLAUDE.md said nothing about the `audit` job while documenting a red `test-plan` at length, so it now carries a section stating that a red `audit` cannot fail a run or block a merge (measured across the last 30 pull-request runs: not one concluded failure because of `audit`), what a red does ask for, and the two standing do-nots. **Follow-up on the `backlog` branch, not here:** delete the override once `wrangler` and `miniflare` ship a `sharp` past 0.35.5. → *Security*

Waits on a wrangler/miniflare release. Added 2026-10-07 by `claude/sharp-override`, which put `"overrides": { "sharp": "^0.35.5" }` in `package.json` to clear [GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w) (`sharp <0.35.5`, high, a flaw in the librsvg copy `sharp` bundles) out of the production tree. **Why it is a follow-up and not a defect:** an `overrides` entry pins a transitive dependency behind its maintainer's back — `miniflare` asked for exactly `0.35.4` and is getting `0.35.5` anyway. That is sound for a patch bump and nothing more, and it is not a licence to hold the pin for good: left in place it will one day silently hold `sharp` *back* from a version the chain actually wants, and that failure is much harder to read than the advisory it fixed. **The check:** when `npm ls sharp --omit=dev` shows the chain resolving to 0.35.5 or later on its own, delete the `overrides` block, run `npm install`, and confirm `npm run audit:prod` is still clean. `npm run opennext:build` is the gate that matters, not just `npm run build` — `next build` never loads `wrangler` or `miniflare`, so it cannot exercise the pin. **Not urgent, and do not chase it:** the advisory is not reachable in this app (`images: { unoptimized: true }`, no `dangerouslyAllowSVG`, and `miniflare` is the local simulator), so nothing is at risk either way; this is tidying a deliberate temporary measure. `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-sharp-override.md` has the full argument. → *Security*

The original text follows. The RPC is `security definer` and accepts `p_issuer jsonb` as a parameter; the app passes `receiptIssuer(country)` (`src/app/management/donations/actions.ts:74`), but anyone with `donation.receipt` can call `/rest/v1/rpc/issue_donation_receipt` directly with any name and address. That gets round the deliberate hard-coding in `src/lib/donations/issuer.ts` (Lutan: a receipt must not read a field anyone can edit), and the forged issuer is stored on the receipt. Fix: the RPC builds the issuer itself (a `receipt_issuers` lookup, or a SQL function mirroring `issuer.ts`) and ignores or drops the parameter. At multi-tenancy this becomes the per-shelter issuer anyway (`docs/decisions/2026-10-09-multi-tenancy-spike.md`, *What fought back* §6), so doing it now is the same work done once.
- [x] **`issue_donation_receipt` also takes what the receipt says (`p_content`: donor name, lines, total) from the caller, so the API can issue a receipt for an amount nobody gave (found by `receipt-issuer-server-side`, 2026-10-10).** **DONE 2026-10-10 (`claude/receipt-content-server-side`, migration `0177`):** the RPC now stores `receipt_content(donation)`, a SQL copy of `receiptContentFor()` beside `0176`'s `receipt_issuer()`, and ignores `p_content` (kept in the signature so the deploy order does not matter). `check-donation-receipts-schema.mjs` issues every receipt with forged content and compares the stored content, as text, with what `receiptContentFor()` builds, on seven probe donations and every real dev donation; it was 22 red before the migration and 64 green after. With `0176` and `0177` the issuer and the content no longer come from the caller, but **the date still does**: `p_issued_on` is stored as given, so the API can backdate a receipt (its own item, filed on the backlog branch the same day). `docs/decisions/2026-10-10-receipt-content-server-side.md`. Same shape as the issuer hole closed in `0176`: the RPC is `security definer` and stores `p_content` as given, and the app builds it with `receiptContentFor(donation.donor_name, lines)` (`src/app/management/donations/actions.ts`). Anyone holding `donation.receipt` can call `/rest/v1/rpc/issue_donation_receipt` directly and get a correctly numbered receipt saying 1,000,000 baht for a 100-baht gift, stored in the register as though printed from the donation. Smaller than the issuer hole because the same login can already edit the donation's lines before issuing, so the forged figure at least has to match nothing; but a receipt whose stored content disagrees with its donation is exactly what a tax check would find. Fix: the RPC builds `content` from `donations` and `donation_lines` itself, mirroring `receiptContentFor()`, keeps `p_content` accepted and ignored as `0176` did with `p_issuer`, and the receipts harness passes forged content. Needs a migration, so it is a schema slot.
- [x] **`issue_donation_receipt` still takes the receipt date (`p_issued_on`) from the caller, so the API can backdate a receipt into another tax year (found by `receipt-content-server-side`, 2026-10-10).** **DONE 2026-10-12 (`claude/receipt-backdate-rule`, migration `0186`):** the RPC now validates `received_on <= p_issued_on <= shelter_today()` (22023 otherwise, before the counter moves). `check-donation-receipts-schema.mjs` passes a date before the donation, a future date and null (all refused) and one receipt backdated three days (accepted). `docs/decisions/2026-10-12-receipt-date-rule.md`. The original text follows. Third of the same shape after `0176` (issuer) and `0177` (content): the RPC is `security definer` and stores `p_issued_on` as given, with no check against today, the donation’s `received_on`, or anything else. The app always sends `todayIso()`, so no screen does it, but anyone holding `donation.receipt` can call `/rest/v1/rpc/issue_donation_receipt` directly and get the next number dated, say, last December, which is the one field a tax check reads first. Numbers are gapless and in order, so a backdated receipt would sit out of date order in the register, which is how it would be spotted, not prevented. Fix: the RPC uses the shelter’s today (Asia/Bangkok) itself, keeps `p_issued_on` accepted and ignored as `0176`/`0177` did, and the receipts harness passes a forged date. ~~Decide first whether the Director ever needs to issue a receipt dated earlier than today (a gift recorded late); if so, the rule is `received_on <= issued_on <= today`, not today only.~~ **ANSWERED 2026-10-11 (Lutan, in the `/plan-day` chat): YES, a backdated receipt is fine for the Director to issue.** His reason, in his words: *"It is not uncommon for someone to donate and then ask for a receipt a week later."* **So the rule is `received_on <= issued_on <= today` — not today only.** Three things that follow, and none of them is a judgement left to the stream: (1) **a receipt may never be dated before the donation it is for**, because that is not a late receipt, it is a wrong one; (2) **it may never be dated in the future**, which is the whole point of the item — a receipt dated into next tax year is the thing a tax check reads first; (3) **"today" is the shelter's today, Asia/Bangkok** (`shelter_date()`, `0073`), not UTC, or a receipt issued in the Thai evening is refused as being in the future. Keep `p_issued_on` **accepted and validated**, not ignored — this differs from `0176` and `0177`, which accepted and ignored their parameters, because here the caller's value is now legitimate input rather than something only the server should decide. The receipts harness should pass a date before `received_on` and a date after today and expect both refused, plus one legitimately backdated receipt and expect it accepted. **Do not narrow this to today-only on the grounds that it is safer**: it would refuse the ordinary case Lutan has just described, and the Director would have no way to issue the receipt she was asked for. Needs a migration, so it is a schema slot.

Both files are mode `0600`, owned by `lutan`. **The running app never reads it**, so step (2) cannot break the site: the only reference under `src/` is the `SECRET_ENV_NAMES` redaction list in `src/lib/status/run.ts`, which exists to scrub the value *out* of status-tile error text. **But something live does read it, and the order of the steps below now matters more than the item implied.** The Pi's crontab holds `0 3 * * 0 cd $HOME/Animal_Shelter_App && node scripts/backup.mjs --env production --local-copy $HOME/backups/lannacare` — **the weekly production backup runs from the Pi, as that user, with that token.** It is working: the newest dump is `lannacare-production-2026-10-10T2000Z.dump.age` (1.06 MB, encrypted, uploaded to Drive, 3 local copies), written at 03:00 on 2026-10-11. So **(2) must not be done before (1)** — delete the token first and the Sunday backup fails into `~/backups/backup.log`, which nobody reads, and the first anyone would know is the next time a backup was wanted. That makes this a *silent* failure mode, which is the project's standing concern. **Two things that got cheaper:** the **test clone's** copy is pure excess — nothing on the Pi backs up the dev project — so it can be deleted now, ahead of the rest; and step (3)'s guard should refuse the token in **either** clone, not just the production one. **Severity stands as written:** the token runs arbitrary SQL against both projects through the Management API, and the app service and the backup run as the same Pi user. Do, in order: (1) put `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://<pooler user>@<pooler host>:5432/postgres` in the Pi's `.env.deploy.production` and run the backup once by hand; (2) delete `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` from every file on the Pi; (3) make `scripts/pi/write-env.mjs` and `setup.sh` refuse to run when any env file on the Pi holds `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` (the same shape as `deploy-pi.sh` refusing a production file in the test clone); (4) move the Drive values the Pi needs into `.env.deploy.production` so `.env.local` is never copied to the Pi again, and say so in `docs/pi-hosting.md`; (5) rotate the token. Half a day. Cheaper than *Run the app on its own user on the Pi* and worth doing first. `docs/architecture-review-2026-09-22.md` §2.1 S1.
  **Closed 2026-10-12 by `claude/pi-token-off`:** guard and docs in the PR (`scripts/pi/check-no-forbidden.mjs`), and the Pi steps done by Lutan the same day: `SUPABASE_DB_URL` set and backup proven, token deleted from both clones, `.env.local` removed from the production clone, token rotated (old `CL-Both` deleted).

- [x] **DONE 2026-10-25 — migration `0263`, PR from `claude/doors-need-a-card`; record in `docs/decisions/2026-10-25-doors-need-a-card.md`. Everything below is the brief it was built from. EVERY VIEW AND EVERY TABLE MUST REQUIRE A CARD — RULED 2026-10-25 by Lutan, in his words: *"all views / doors need to require a card"*. The principle is SETTLED and this is buildable now; the ONLY thing still to agree is the card set — which role holds each new card — and that comes to him as a proposal, not as a question about whether to do it.** Found 2026-10-25 by the inventory (`docs/decisions/2026-10-25-no-coded-security-inventory.md`, B3). **He asked first where the access came from, since there is no coded security left, and the answer is worth keeping because it is not a breach of his rule:** there are two locks, and these surfaces only ever got the first. `has_app_access()` is the **front door** ("is this login in the app at all?") and it asks only *"does this role hold at least one card?"* — no role name, no role column, which is why the zero-asserting check is right not to flag it. `has_permission()` is the **room door** ("does this role hold the card for *this*?"), and it is on nearly everything else. These surfaces have **no room door at all**, so any one card walks in. That is an activity with no card, which `CLAUDE.md` already answers: *"No card for the activity? Create one. Never write 'but there is no card for this' and add a fallback."* **`has_app_access()` itself STAYS as the front door** — it is what keeps `public_viewer` out (it holds no cards), and `docs/decisions/2026-10-25-security-database-half.md` explains why it cannot simply answer `true` or `false`. `has_app_access()` is true for Admin or any role holding one cell, and it is the only gate on: the facility maps, map rooms and room placements; `translatable_fields` and approved map-room translations; and the views `app_users` (**every login's email, name and role key**), `current_placement`, `resident_current_state` (resident names, status, date of death), `immunization_compliance`, `immunization_duplicate_check` and `translation_queue`. So a login holding only `do_stocktaking` reads all of them. Two reference tables, `rounds` and `units`, are readable by **any signed-in login with no card at all**. Derived from cards, so not a coded rule and not red in the check, but not that card's grant either, which is what a "this card gives exactly X" test measures. This is the same set the 0.40.3 release record calls the six views with no card gate; **fold the two together**. **SUPERSEDED 2026-10-25 — do not read the next sentence as current:** *"Each surface either gets a card (schema first) or is recorded as deliberately shared."* That was the open question and **it is answered: every one of them gets a card.** Nothing is recorded as deliberately shared. **`rounds` and `units` are IN SCOPE too** — Lutan's ruling was "all", asked directly after being told those two were the ones proposed to stay open. **THE HAZARD, and it has already bitten this project twice, so design for it rather than discovering it:** a reference table put behind a card breaks the forms that need it **silently** — the field renders empty and the save is refused with nothing to explain it. That is exactly `clinics.list` (`fault-clinic-visit-save`: *"the clinic list is empty and the field is required"*) and `facility.enclosures` (`fault-residents-lifecycle`), both still LIVE rows in `docs/card-access-faults.md`. So **every card that opens a form must also grant the reference reads that form needs**, and the test plan must drive each affected form, not merely assert the policy exists. - [x] **DONE 2026-10-31 (`claude/check-scripts-not-blind`, `docs/decisions/2026-10-31-sql-readers-know-string-literals.md`): shared `scripts/lib/sql-code-only.mjs`; and YES, the blocking check COULD report a false green (five fixtures proved it, now regression tests); nothing real was hiding.** Original: **`check-migration-grants.mjs` reads a `;` or `--` inside a SQL string literal as code, so it reports a real security finding that is not real — and the next author will hit it again.** Found 2026-10-31 by `pi-failover-schema` while writing `0292_write_requests.sql`. `statements()` is `sql.split(";")` and `stripSql()` is `replace(/--[^\n]*/g, " ")`, neither of which tracks string literals. So a `comment on … is '… in_flight (never replay it -- a success). …'` swallows the rest of its own line **including the closing quote and semicolon**, the following statement is absorbed into it, and that statement's `revoke all on function … from public, anon;` is read as missing. The script then printed `function claim_write_request() is created without revoke all … — Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC, so anon could call it through /rest/v1/rpc/`, which is the shape of a genuine exposure and was not one. **Why it matters more than a cosmetic parser bug:** `lint` runs this script, so `gates.mjs` and CI both do, and the finding it prints is the most alarming kind — a reader has no way to tell it from a real missing revoke without reading the parser. The 2026-10-31 workaround was to write the migration's comment strings with no `;` and no `--` in them, with a comment in the file saying why; **that is a convention nobody can be expected to know, and it is now load-bearing in `0292`.** **The fix:** make `stripSql()` and `statements()` quote-aware (single quotes with `''` doubling, `"` identifiers, and `$tag$` bodies, which `stripSql` already handles), then delete the convention note from `0292`'s header. **Check it is still real before building:** add a fixture with a `;` and a `--` inside a `comment on` literal followed by a `revoke`, and confirm the current script reports a false finding on it — that fixture is the regression test. **Also worth one grep while in there:** `check-hard-coded-security.mjs` has its own `stripSqlComment` with the same blindness (it already carries a CRLF guard for a related fault), so the same literal could hide a policy or a grant from the blocking security check — **that direction is a false GREEN, not a false red, which is the worse of the two.** Establish whether it can, and say so either way.

## Deployment (before go-live)
- [x] **A Pi build fails whenever a release DELETES a page, because its type check reads the live build's stale route types.** Found 2026-10-30 by `0.40.12`, which removed `/admin/frequencies`: `deploy-pi.sh` builds into `.next.new` (`NEXT_DIST_DIR`), but `tsconfig.json` includes `.next/types/**/*.ts`, so `next build` type-checks the *previous* build's `.next/types/validator.ts`, which still imports the deleted page (`TS2307: Cannot find module '../../src/app/admin/frequencies/page.js'`). The build is refused safely (the old version keeps serving), but production users stayed on `0.40.11` against a database `0288` had already changed, so the medication list errored until it was cleared. Cleared by hand that release: Lutan moved `.next/types` aside on both clones (to `~/stale-next-types-{prod,test}-0.40.11`; the auto-mode classifier refuses Claude remote writes outside `deploy-pi.sh`). The Worker deploy is not affected (it builds in place, so its types are regenerated). **Fix:** have `deploy-pi.sh` move `.next/types` aside (or point the typecheck at `.next.new/types`) before the build, and put it back on a failed build; check `tsconfig.json`'s includes for the same reason. The `~/stale-next-types-*` folders can be deleted once a later Pi deploy has succeeded. **DONE 2026-10-31 (`claude/pi-build-stale-types`):** the typecheck now points at `.next.new/types` — `next.config.ts` picks `tsconfig.next-new.json` for `NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next.new`, which never reads `.next`, so a failed build has nothing to put back; reproduced locally before and after (`docs/decisions/2026-10-31-pi-build-checks-its-own-types.md`). `tsconfig.json`'s `.next/types` include stays: it is how in-place builds (Worker, gates) check the route validator. Deleting the two `~/stale-next-types-*-0.40.11` folders on the Pi is Lutan's and is its own item under this section.

- [x] **The release-time home-icon sync re-uploads all 344 files every release whether or not anything changed, and hit a Drive 403 rate limit mid-release (found 2026-10-21 during `0.38.2`). NOTHING LEFT TO DECIDE; buildable now. Fix (a) only — upload just what changed, plus retry with backoff and a resumable run.** `scripts/sync-home-icons.mjs` draws **8 files per card** — dark/light × 180/1024 px × with-name/icon-only (`sync-home-icons.mjs:49`) — so 43 cards is 344 images. **The upload loop has no "unchanged" case** (`sync-home-icons.mjs:97`-`104`): for each of the 344 it does a `files.list` lookup and then *always* uploads, `files.update` when the name exists and `files.create` when it does not. Nothing compares the PNG just drawn against the one in Drive. **So every release costs ~688 Drive requests** — 344 lookups and 344 uploads — to replace files that are almost all byte-identical to what is already there. On `0.38.2` it drew all 344, uploaded 40, died on `userRateLimitExceeded` (403) leaving the folder **part-updated**, and a straight retry got through slowly. **It will recur every release until this changes.** **Not an auth fault** — the token was fine, and a 403 here reads deceptively like the Drive connection having broken. **Two fixes, independent, in value order:** (a) **upload only what changed.** The `files.list` call it already makes can return `size` and `md5Checksum`, so comparing against the drawn buffer turns a normal release into a few uploads instead of 344 — this is the fix Lutan asked for and it removes the rate limit as a side effect. (b) **is all eight wanted?** Most people will use one, the 180 px icon in their phone's own appearance; trimming the set cuts the count again. Keep **retry with backoff** and make a partial run **resumable** either way, so a failure is never a silently mixed folder. **Do not** solve it by dropping the Drive copy: the `0.38.2` release note promises "every card's icon is also kept in a shared Google Drive folder", so the folder is a user-visible promise. Context in `docs/decisions/2026-10-21-home-screen-icons.md` and `docs/releases/2026-10-21.md` (Defect 1). **ANSWERED 2026-10-21 by Lutan on fix (b): KEEP ALL EIGHT files per card.** His call, asked directly: the count stays 344 drawn, but once (a) lands a normal release uploads only the few that changed, so the rate limit goes either way and nobody loses a size or a naming variant they were using. **Do not trim the set, and do not ask (b) again.** **DONE 2026-10-22: md5 comparison, backoff, resumable re-run; second run uploads 0, one changed card uploads 1.**

- [x] **Make the assistant-retention job report on itself — a database job that fails silently is the one kind of failure nothing here can see (found 2026-10-20 by the `0.37.2` release; small-to-medium, code + a little schema).** `purge-assistant-actions` (`0227`) is **the only pg_cron job in the entire schema** — `grep -r "cron.schedule" supabase/migrations/` returns exactly one hit — so there is **no existing pattern for watching one**, and this item is as much about establishing that pattern as about this job. **The problem:** pg_cron runs inside the database. It needs no key, no deploy and no Worker, which is why it was the right shape for retention — and it is also why **nothing anywhere knows whether it ran.** There is no email, no alert, no tile and no log anyone reads. Every other scheduled thing in this system reports: the Worker's quarter-hourly sweep writes `status_alert_runs`, the backup writes its own state, and both surface on `/admin/status` with alert mail behind them. This one writes nothing. **Both failure directions are silent and neither is cheap.** If the job never installed or is `active = false`, `assistant_actions.request_text` is kept **forever**, against the sentence `0227`'s sibling PR added to `/privacy` — so the page makes a promise to users that the database is quietly not keeping, and a privacy promise that is untrue is worse than one never made. If the job runs but errors every night (a permission change, a renamed column, a `search_path` surprise), the same thing happens, and the only trace is in `cron.job_run_details`, which nobody opens. **What makes this tractable:** the function already returns the row count it deleted, and pg_cron already records every run in `cron.job_run_details` with status, start, end and return message. **Do:** (1) read the last run for `purge-assistant-actions` from `cron.job_run_details` — status, when, and the count returned; (2) add a tile to `/admin/status` beside the existing ones, green when the job succeeded within the last ~48 hours (not 24: one missed night is not an incident, two is), **amber when the job exists but has not run**, and **red when it does not exist or is `active = false`**, which is the install failure this is really for; (3) hang it off the **existing** alert machinery (`worker/index.mjs`'s quarter-hourly route and `status_alert_runs`) rather than inventing a second one — the plumbing, the mail and the test-alert button all exist already and were extended in `0.37.2`; (4) write the check so it **distinguishes "has never run" from "ran and deleted zero rows"**, because on a quiet shelter zero deletions is a perfectly normal night and must not read as a fault. **Deliberately out of scope:** changing the retention periods, which are Lutan's decisions of 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-19 (2 days, 90 for `unmatched` and `refused`) and are not in question. **Worth generalising while in there, but only if it stays small:** the tile should key off a *list* of expected jobs rather than this one name, so the second pg_cron job ever added is watched by construction instead of repeating this gap. Needs a decision file (why pg_cron rather than the Worker for retention, and why the signal lives in the Worker's sweep) and a test plan covering all four tile states, including the one that matters most — **the job absent entirely**, which is the state production may be in right now and which the sibling item above exists to find out. → *Deployment (before go-live)* **Done 2026-10-21 (`claude/retention-job-report`, migration 0238):** `cronJobs` health check + tile + alert mail on red; list-driven via `EXPECTED_CRON_JOBS`; production read showed the job active. The website never faltered (the tunnel is outbound, so it never touches the broken path) and the Pi was healthy throughout. **Cause:** with port isolation on, every port reaches the UPLINK but no port reaches another port; the PC and the Pi were in adjacent ports. One toggle on the switch fixed it immediately, with the Pi's Wi-Fi back on. **The check that names it in one minute:** from the suspect machine, ping the gateway, then ping any other device on the same wire — reaching ONLY the gateway is the signature. **Bind the ping** (`ping -S <that interface's address> <target>` on Windows): an unbound ping on a dual-homed PC silently leaves by the other interface and reports a success that means nothing; that mistake was made twice on the night and both times inverted the conclusion. **The measurement that proves WHERE packets die, needing no `sudo`:** `ss -tnH state syn-recv` on the Pi while the other machine connects — the SYNs arrived and sat half-open, so the loss was on the return path; - [x] **A schema branch that adds a public view turns CI red on every OTHER stream, for as long as it stays unmerged.** Found 2026-10-16 by the `0.33.0` release, whose record PR went red having touched nothing but three Markdown files. **Mechanism:** `public-views` (`scripts/check-public-views.mjs`) runs against the **shared dev database**, while its `PUBLIC_VIEWS` allow-list is read from **the branch under test**. The schema-first rule (CLAUDE.md) requires a migration to be applied to dev *before* its PR merges. In that window the new view exists in dev and is absent from `PUBLIC_VIEWS` on `main`, so every branch cut from `main` fails with `FAIL public_<thing>: anon SELECT is refused - HTTP 200 (a new public view? add it to PUBLIC_VIEWS)`. **Observed:** `0210_appeals.sql` (#667) created `public_appeals` and `public_appeal_photos` and was applied to dev about a minute after #667's own CI had passed - so #667 was green and #668 (and anything else branched from `main`) was red, with no fault of their own and no fix available on their branch. **Why it matters beyond the nuisance:** the check is doing its job - an unlisted public view is exactly the silent-exposure risk it exists to catch - so it must not simply be softened. But a red that nobody can act on is the kind people learn to wave through, which is how a real one gets missed. It also stalls the merge train, since a red check is never merged past. **Options to weigh in the PR:** (a) have the check treat a view that exists in dev but is created by a migration **not on `origin/main`** as `skip` with a loud note naming the branch, rather than `FAIL` - it can tell, by reading `supabase/migrations` on `origin/main`; (b) run the check against a throwaway database built from the branch's own migrations instead of shared dev, which removes the coupling entirely but costs build time; (c) leave the behaviour and document it, which is what `0.33.0` did as a stopgap in `docs/release-handover.md`. (a) looks cheapest and keeps the signal. **Whichever is chosen, say explicitly what happens to a genuinely unlisted view on a branch that DOES own the migration** - that case must stay red. Needs a test plan that exercises both: a view from an unmerged foreign branch (should not fail you) and a view your own branch adds without listing it (must fail you). No schema. -> *Developer experience* **Done 2026-10-16 (`claude/ci-script-fixes-fold`): option (a). `check-public-views.mjs` skips an unlisted `public_*` view only with positive proof that another unmerged `origin/*` branch's migration creates it (loud WARN naming the branch), and fails every other case; proved by `scripts/check-public-view-owner.mjs`. See `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-public-views-foreign-branch-skip.md`.**

- [x] **Let Claude run production deploys with fewer hand-offs: SSH from the laptop to the Pi, and a permission decision for the Worker — a guided session.** Lutan, 2026-10-02; facts from the release manager session the same day, which has run every release from 0.9.0 to 0.13.0. **Where each step of a production deploy stands:** (a) **Migrations** (`node scripts/apply-migrations.mjs --env production`) already run from a Claude session with no hand-off, using `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` from the gitignored `.env.deploy.production`. Leave them alone. (b) **The Worker** (`node scripts/deploy.mjs --env production >> deploy.log 2>&1`) is **not** blocked by credentials: wrangler is logged in through `npx wrangler login` (its own stored auth, `~/.wrangler/config/default.toml`), and the command would work. It is refused by Claude Code's auto-mode safety check (reason "Production Deploy"), consistently. **A token changes nothing here**; if Lutan wants Claude to run it, that is a Claude Code permission rule (an allow rule for that exact command in `.claude/settings.json`, via the `update-config` skill), and it is Lutan's decision, made in his own session, never at another session's request. Until then Lutan runs that one command himself. (c) **The Pi**, which is what users are served from (the Worker is the fallback, and both must be deployed or `/releases` shows the old version while the release mail announces the new one): `./scripts/pi/deploy-pi.sh` must **run** on the Pi but can be **started** from the laptop over SSH, which is not set up. Tested 2026-10-02: `lanna-pi` / `lanna-pi.local` answer and are in `known_hosts`, but authentication fails because **there is no private key on this laptop** (`~/.ssh` holds only `known_hosts`) and no ssh-agent running. `pi.lannacare.org` cannot be used for SSH: it is the cloudflared HTTP ingress, so SSH has to go to the LAN name. **This is the part the session fixes:** Lutan runs `ssh-keygen -t ed25519` and then `ssh-copy-id lutan@lanna-pi.local` (it asks for his Pi password, so it is his to run), add a `Host pi` entry in `~/.ssh/config`, and decide whether to restrict that key on the Pi to the deploy script only (`command=` in `authorized_keys`). Then a laptop-side wrapper, e.g. `node scripts/deploy-pi-remote.mjs --ref <sha>`, runs the deploy over SSH and appends its output to `deploy.log`, so a Pi deploy is one command from any session. **A Cloudflare API token is optional, not the fix:** nothing in the repo uses `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` today, and swapping the OAuth login for a scoped, long-lived token kept in a file is a different risk, not simply an upgrade; ask Lutan whether he wants it (its only gain is not having to repeat `wrangler login` when that lapses). **Things to write down while there:** on this laptop PowerShell's execution policy blocks plain `npm`, so every command must be `node scripts/…` or `npm.cmd`; keep the `>> deploy.log 2>&1` redirect on deploy commands (release records depend on it) and warn that the terminal looks empty while it runs; and the 90-day token set on 2026-09-22 is still unlocated, so if auth fails around 2026-12-21 check that first. Record each credential's name, location, scope and expiry (never its value) in a `docs/decisions/` file and the README deploy section. **Done when:** from a fresh Claude session, a Pi deploy of a named SHA runs over SSH without a password prompt and lands in `deploy.log`, and Lutan has decided, in writing, whether Claude may run the Worker deploy. **CHECKED 2026-10-07 (staleness sweep) — the SSH half is in daily use; not ticked because the written decision on the Worker is not in a decision file.** Release records show Claude running the Pi build over SSH from 2026-10-02 (`docs/releases/2026-10-02.md`, *"Pi build over SSH"*), and the ticked *Confirm the new Pi allow rule* item (`852b80c3`, 2026-10-07) records the 0.20.1 release running it under `Bash(ssh lutan@lanna-pi.local *)` past `[Production Deploy]`. The Worker production deploy stays Lutan's by choice (same item: *"deliberately Lutan's own job"*), but this item's done-when asks for that **in writing** with each credential's name, location, scope and expiry in `docs/decisions/` and the README — no such file exists. It has no trigger of its own, so it happens only when whoever deploys hands the output to whoever writes records - which held for `0.5.0`, `0.6.1` and `0.7.0` because the session was in the conversation at the time, and did not here. It is the only release artifact with no automated trigger and the only one that cannot be reconstructed later. Two options are in the record, neither built: a nudge at the end of `deploy.mjs` naming the record now owed (the better trade - it fires while the output is still on screen), or a script comparing `latestRelease.version` against `docs/releases/`. - [x] **`apply-migrations.mjs --drift <env>` crashes every time, on every environment (found 2026-10-13, during the `0.28.0` release).** `ReferenceError: unapplied is not defined` at `scripts/apply-migrations.mjs:226`. Introduced by `e6df8b2b` — the `--upto` PR (#570), **in the `0.28.0` release itself**. `driftReport()` destructures `{ unapplied, missingFile }` into its own scope and returns a count; the new explanatory block at the call site then reads `unapplied` and `missingFile` as if they were in scope, and they are not. The condition is evaluated unconditionally, so **every** `--drift` run dies, whatever the state of the database. **What still works, and why this was not caught:** the crash happens *after* `driftReport()` has printed the whole comparison, so the substance — file count, applied-row count, and the two gap lists — is on screen and correct; only the `No drift: <env> matches origin/main` verdict line and the exit code are lost. It exits non-zero through the crash, so it fails loudly rather than silently, and a reader skimming the output sees a correct comparison. Nothing in CI runs `--drift`. **Why it matters:** the release runbook requires the named drift check on **both** databases and says to quote its verdict, precisely because that line is what reads as a drift check to whoever reads the record afterwards. `0.28.0`'s record therefore quotes the comparison (`192 file(s), 192 applied row(s)`, 0 on either side, both databases) and states that the verdict line could not be printed. **The fix is two lines:** have `driftReport()` return the two arrays rather than only their total, and read them from that at the call site. **While there:** add a case to whatever covers this — `check-release-guards.mjs` is the nearest harness — because a release gate that cannot run is worth one assertion. Also note `--drift dev` is not a thing: the dev database is `--env test`. *Done on `claude/release-tooling-fixes`: `driftReport()` returns the arrays; a case in `check-release-guards.mjs`; verified with `--drift --env test` printing the verdict and exiting 0.*

It genuinely works on this box: the Pi was first flashed to SD and `rpi-clone`d to the NVMe (`docs/pi-hosting.md:152-158`), and `BOOT_ORDER=0xf146` already reads 6 NVMe, 4 USB, 1 SD, so SD needs no eeprom change. **Three caveats.** (1) **Use a USB card reader, not the built-in slot.** `spare-clone.sh:102` tests `lsblk -dno TRAN` for `usb`, so `mmcblk0` is refused outright; a card in a reader reports `usb`, passes unchanged, and is tried earlier in the boot order too. No code change needed, and the check should stay as it is. (2) **Size.** `init` writes 512 MB boot plus `ROOT_SIZE`, default **64G**, so a 16-32 GB card needs `ROOT_SIZE` lowered to fit the NVMe’s *used* space — read `df -h /` on the Pi first. (3) **Still `f3probe` it.** SD is the most counterfeited storage there is and the drive tried on 2026-10-02 was a fake. Endurance is a moderate worry rather than a blocker, because `spare-clone.timer` runs `rpi-clone -u` incrementally and not a full weekly rewrite — but SD has no SMART and tends to fail silently or go read-only, on the one device you only reach for on the worst day. So **re-run the boot test periodically** and treat the card as interim, not as the answer. A branded SSD is still wanted: for the archive half (the item below) and for speed. **Note 2026-10-19 (Lutan): he has found a 1 TB Seagate USB drive** (it reports as USB-attached SCSI, i.e. UAS, which is normal for a USB drive and not a SCSI disk). **Check before using it:** whether it is a **spinning portable hard disk or an SSD** (most 1 TB Seagate portables are hard disks): a hard disk is fine for the **backup and archive copy** (one job, written nightly, LUKS-encrypted), and works but is slow as a **bootable spare**, which is the SSD's job in this item; that it is genuine and full size (`f3probe`, as the item asks, since the first drive tried was a counterfeit); its SMART health (`smartctl -a`, many USB bridges pass it through with `-d sat`); and that the Pi 5 powers it from USB alongside the NVMe on the 27 W supply (a portable hard disk draws most at spin-up). Then decide with Lutan which of the two jobs it takes: recommended, **the backup and archive copy** (the item below), leaving the bootable spare for a branded SSD later. **ANSWERED 2026-10-19 (Lutan), BOTH HALVES.** (1) **Leave the bootable spare UNENCRYPTED — "YES"** to the written proposal: the bootable copy stays unencrypted so the Pi comes back by itself after a power cut, with the drive kept physically secure; the separate archive copy is still encrypted, because it holds medical history and names carers and adopters. (2) **A drive has been found** — his words: *"1TB SSD Drive has been found, this should do."* So the purchase step is done and what remains is the probe, the clone and the boot test with the main drive disabled. **Do not re-ask either question.**

- [x] **`apply-migrations.mjs` does not guard `--env test`, so a stale worktree can silently undo a merged migration's effect.** Found 2026-10-15 during the `0.32.1` release. `GUARDED` is `envName === "uat" || envName === "production"` (`scripts/apply-migrations.mjs:94`), so the check that a checkout's `supabase/migrations/` matches `origin/main` is skipped for dev. Consequence, observed rather than reasoned: `0203_clear_stale_ledger_row_0201_map_rooms.sql` deleted the phantom `0201_map_rooms_drop_map_id_shape.sql` ledger row from dev, is recorded as applied, **and the row is back** — dev reads `208 applied` against 207 files and `--drift test` is red, while production is clean because the row was never there. The cause is that three merged-but-not-cleared worktrees (`facility-map-with-enclosures`, `map-rooms-column-drop`, `mobile-44px-finish`) still hold the file under its **old** name, and an unguarded `--env test` run from any of them re-inserts it. The effect is quiet: the migration reports success, CI is green, and only the drift check notices. **Do:** (1) decide whether `GUARDED` should cover `test` too — the argument against is that dev is where schema-first work is applied *before* merge, which the guard would forbid, so the fix is probably a narrower check (refuse a file that is not on `origin/main` **and** not in the current branch's diff) rather than full guarding; (2) a new migration to delete the row again, since an applied file is never edited; (3) clear the three leftover worktrees, which removes today's source. Note (2) alone is not a fix — it is re-runnable by hand and will come back the next time an old worktree applies to dev. **Not a release blocker:** production is unaffected and dev's actual schema is correct, both columns being dropped under either filename. Recorded as a stated gap in `0.32.1`'s release record. **UPDATE later the same day: part (3) is DONE, which changes part (2).** A `/clean-streams` round cleared all three worktrees, and a sweep of every `Animal_Shelter_*` checkout now finds **no copy of `0201_map_rooms_drop_map_id_shape.sql` anywhere**, so nothing can re-insert the row. That removes the reason (2) was not a fix on its own: **a single new migration deleting the row would now close this permanently**, where before it would have come straight back. (1) is still the real question and is unchanged — the guard gap is a live hazard for the *next* renamed migration even though today's source is gone, so do not close this item on the strength of (2) alone. Dev still reads `208 applied` against 207 files and `--drift test` is still red. **PART (1) DONE 2026-10-16 (`claude/migration-test-guard`, `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-migration-guard-for-test.md`): `--env test` now refuses a file absent from `origin/main` but present in the merge-base. Part (2), the cleanup migration deleting the phantom `0201` row, is DONE 2026-10-16: `0208_clear_phantom_ledger_row_0201_again.sql` (`claude/ledger-labels-schema`, `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-ledger-row-and-resident-labels.md`); `--drift test` no longer lists the 0201 row, checked after two applies. Closes the `0.32.1` stated gap.** → *Deployment*

- [x] **`setup.sh` adds the Pi's swapfile to `fstab` with no priority, so it comes back *below* zram — and on the live Pi it was not in `fstab` at all.** Found 2026-10-19. `/swapfile2` was created by hand during `0.36.0` and `/etc/fstab` had **no swap entry whatsoever**, so the swap fix that `0.36.1` depended on **would have vanished at the next reboot**, silently, taking the Pi back to the state where builds were killed three times running. Fixed on the live machine (`swapon -p 200`, plus `/swapfile2 none swap sw,pri=200 0 0`) and **proved by an actual reboot** — it came back at priority 200. Still to do in the repo: `scripts/pi/setup.sh` line 77 writes `sw` with no `pri=`, so a rebuilt Pi gets the file swap at a *lower* priority than zram, which is the wrong way round — zram is compressed RAM and spends RAM to save it. Add `pri=200` there and explain the ordering in `docs/pi-hosting.md`. Note the priority change was **not** what fixed the `0.37.0` build (see the Turbopack cache item) — it was a real misconfiguration found on the way past.
- [x] **`eslint` walks into `.claude/worktrees/`, so `gates.mjs` reports a five-figure lint failure in the main checkout that CI never sees.** Found 2026-10-19 while running the gates for the `0.37.0` release.
