## Quick wins

- [x] **`CLAUDE.md` DOCUMENTS THE `dev-signin.mjs` CARD FORM WRONGLY, AND THE SCRIPT REFUSES WHAT IT TELLS YOU TO TYPE. One-line fix to `CLAUDE.md`; the script is correct and must not be changed.** **WHAT HAPPENS:** `CLAUDE.md` → *Getting a signed-in dev session* says *"A login's cards can be set with `dev-signin.mjs <role> --cards <card>`"*. Typing that gives **`Error: give a role or --cards, not both`** (`scripts/dev-signin.mjs:145`). Hit by the planner on 2026-10-28 while driving the cashflow card check. **THE CORRECT FORM IS `--cards` ALONE, and it is better than the documented one:** `node scripts/dev-signin.mjs --cards <a,b> --port <N>`. Given `--cards` with no role, the script **creates its own throwaway role** named after the cards (`cardRoleKey(cardKeys)`, `kind: "custom"`) and puts exactly those cards on it. **So it models *a login holding exactly that card and nothing else* — which is precisely what the card rule asks for — without touching any real role.** The documented `<role> --cards` form would have re-keyed a shared role and could have broken another stream's live session; the script refusing it is the script being right. **DO:** correct that sentence in `CLAUDE.md` to the `--cards`-alone form, say that it makes a disposable role of its own so no real role is disturbed, and keep the existing warnings (the snippet holds a live token; cookies belong to `localhost`, not a port). **DO NOT** change `dev-signin.mjs` to accept both. **AND A SECOND WARNING WORTH ADDING WHILE THERE, measured the same day:** `node scripts/dev-signin.mjs --remove` deletes **every** login the script has ever made, including ones other live streams are signed in with. With two or three streams running that is a shared-resource hazard, and nothing in `CLAUDE.md` says so. **Say: do not `--remove` while other streams are running.** **Size:** XS, one paragraph of `CLAUDE.md`. **It needs a PR like any other change** — `CLAUDE.md` is never edited on `main` directly, and never via this branch. → *Documentation* **DONE 2026-10-28 by #1058 (`claude/instruments-last-two-and-docs`), ticked by the planner 2026-10-29 — the stream fixed it and did not tick its own item.** `CLAUDE.md` now carries the correct form in **both** places it appears: the all-analysis-by-card section (*"a login holding exactly that card and nothing else — `node scripts/dev-signin.mjs --cards <card> --port <yours>`"*) and the dev-session section, which now also states outright that **the script refuses a role and `--cards` together**, and warns that `--remove` deletes every login the script has made, so it must not be run while other streams are live. **The script was not changed**, as this item required. **Verified by reading both lines, not by trusting the PR title.**

- [x] **THREE RELEASE NOTES IN A ROW WENT MISSING, AND THE GUARD THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT THEM COULD NOT FIRE. ESTABLISHED 2026-10-28, NOT GUESSED: the step EXISTS and is NOT simply skipped — its TRIGGER IS TOO NARROW. Nothing left to decide; buildable now, one small PR, no schema.** **WHAT WENT MISSING:** `0275`'s note (rescued later as #1024), `0276`'s (rescued as #1038), and `0279`'s (written by #1047/#1048 after the fact). **Three in a row is a mechanism, not bad luck.** **THE FIX THAT WAS TRIED AND FAILED:** nominating a carrier in prose. `0279`'s carrier was named in FOUR places — the backlog item, the stream's brief, its decision file and its PR body, all saying *"carried by the next release cut PR"* — **and the cut still did not pick it up.** So the planner's own remedy was itself the failed intervention, and the replacement must be MECHANICAL rather than another note telling someone to remember. **WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, read 2026-10-28 in `docs/release-procedure.md` (the section ending *"Expect this shape again while the security rebuild runs"*):** the procedure DOES carry the right instruction — *"when `unreleased` is empty, do not conclude 'nothing visible'. Check whether any PR in the range wrote `n/a` on its release-notes line for a step this release closes; grepping the range's test plans for that line is a minute's work."* **THE HOLE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE FINDING: that instruction is conditional on `unreleased` BEING EMPTY.** At `0.40.10`'s cut `unreleased` was NOT empty — it carried two notes (the Upcoming visits Edit gate and `0276`'s medical-photos read) and was missing a third. **So the trigger was false and the check was never going to run.** A release missing SOME of its notes looks exactly like a release with nothing deferred, and that is the shape all three misses had. **This is neither "no step exists" nor "someone skipped a step": it is a guard whose condition excludes the commonest case.** **DO:** (1) make the check UNCONDITIONAL at every cut — run it whether or not `unreleased` is empty; (2) make it a SCRIPT rather than prose, since prose is what failed: over the release range, list every PR whose test plan answered the release-notes line `n/a:` together with the step it cited, so the cutter is shown which deferred notes this release now closes and must decide on each; (3) wire it into the cut so it cannot be passed over silently — a refusal or a printed list the cutter has to answer, in the same place the gates already run. **WHY A SCRIPT AND NOT A RULE:** every one of the three misses happened with the rule already written down. **CAVEAT, STATED HONESTLY:** it is NOT established whether any note beyond these three was lost the same way; nobody has swept earlier releases for it, and this item does not claim they were. → *Quick wins* **DONE (release-note-guard): `scripts/check-deferred-notes.mjs`, run unconditionally by `cut-release.mjs`, which refuses until each candidate is answered (`docs/decisions/2026-10-28-release-note-guard.md`). No sweep of earlier releases was done.**

- [x] **EACH STREAM RECORDS ITS OWN USAGE AT MERGE, instead of the planner gathering it afterwards (process change: `CLAUDE.md`'s merge train and the `/plan-day` skill, one small PR; nothing left to decide; buildable now).** Lutan, 2026-10-28: *"Can we get the individual stream to record their actual usage at merge rather than relying on the planning stream to gather them"*. **WHY, from the skill itself (`.claude/skills/plan-day/SKILL.md` ~74–135):** today the planner reads each merged stream with `get_usage` + `get_session` at the next `/plan-day`, and that loses figures three ways the skill already documents: `get_usage` returns `unavailable` once the stream's process has exited or been archived (batch 3 was auto-archived on merge and all three figures were lost); passing `sessionId` instead of `session_id` silently returns the PLANNER's own window (nearly three fabricated actuals, 2026-10-24); and a session that compacted reports a remainder, not what it spent. A stream reading ITSELF at merge removes the first two outright: its process is alive by definition, and "self" is exactly what it wants. **THE CHANGE:** (1) **`CLAUDE.md`, merge train step 4:** immediately before `gh pr merge`, the stream calls `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__get_usage` and `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__get_session` with no `session_id` (self), and posts ONE comment on its own PR in a fixed, parseable form, e.g. `stream-usage: slug=<feature> tokens=<context.tokensUsed> messages=<the Messages category> model=<model> effort=<effort> started=<session start> merged=<now UTC> compacted=<yes/no/unknown> finished=<yes/blocked>`, with `unmeasured` for any field it cannot read, never a guess. **A PR comment, not a commit:** a commit after green CI would re-run CI, and the backlog branch may only touch `docs/backlog.md`; the comment is durable, tied to the PR, and costs nothing (token counts are not sensitive; the repo is public). (2) **The `/plan-day` skill, "Capture the actuals":** read the figure from the PR first (`gh pr view <n> --json comments`, the `stream-usage:` line) and fall back to today's `get_usage` reading only when there is none (a stream that never merged, or a PR someone merged by hand), saying which source each figure came from in `.plan-day.md`. Every existing rule about WHICH figures count (a blocked stream is not a band reading; a reset window is `not a reading`, judged from `messages` against elapsed time and the diff) stays exactly as it is: the stream reports, the planner still judges. (3) Release-manager and handover PRs are not streams and do not post one. **Done when** the next batch's three streams each leave a `stream-usage:` comment and the planner fills `.plan-day.md` from them without a `get_usage` call.
- [x] **`check-test-plan.mjs` DOES NOT LOOK INSIDE FENCED CODE BLOCKS, so a test plan can ship with an unfilled placeholder where its evidence should be — and one already has. Small, one script, nothing to decide.** **FOUND 2026-10-28** while writing handover `420`'s test plan from `411`'s as a template: **`411`'s plan shipped with the literal string `GATES_OUTPUT_PLACEHOLDER`** sitting in the fenced block under *Paste its closing `gates:` lines below exactly as printed*, **and the checker passed it** (PR #1010, merged). The gates themselves were genuinely run — the tick is not false — **but the evidence the line exists to capture is absent**, which is precisely the failure the template warns about two lines away: *"Evidence pasted into this plan is the tool's actual output, unedited. A hand-maintained table of results is prose about a measurement rather than the measurement."* **An empty evidence block is weaker than a hand-maintained one.** **WHY THE CHECKER MISSES IT:** it validates ticks, `n/a:`/`pending:` reasons, the two signature lines and `Result:`, all of which are line-level tests on checklist lines. **A fenced block is not a checklist line**, so nothing reads it. **THE FIX:** fail when a fenced block that follows a **ticked** line contains an obvious placeholder — `PLACEHOLDER`, `TODO`, `<paste`, `xxx`, or an empty block — and say which line it belongs to. **Keep it narrow and keep it strict:** `CLAUDE.md` is explicit that this script's strictness is deliberate, that it must never get `continue-on-error`, and that **a red `test-plan` is always someone's mistake to fix**, so a check that fires on anything legitimate would be worse than the gap. **Prove it both ways:** `411`'s merged plan must fail the new check, and every other plan in `docs/test-plans/` must still pass — run it across all of them and say how many were read. **AND DO NOT RETROFIT `411`'s PLAN:** it is a record of what happened, the gates were run, and editing it now would put evidence into history that nobody actually pasted. → *Quick wins*

- [x] **A gate script can print its verdict and then exit non-zero from a teardown crash, so its exit code contradicts its own answer — and for a gate, it contradicts it in the dangerous direction.** Found 2026-10-16 during the `0.34.0` release. `node scripts/facility-map-holders.mjs --env production` is the gate Lutan asked for before `0212_retire_facility_map_activity.sql` was applied to production: it exits 1 when a role would be stranded, so **non-zero means "DO NOT APPLY"**. It printed its table and `Without facility.enclosures at Read: 0 (safe to retire)`, then died with `Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 94` and exited **127** — reproduced twice before the apply and again after it. The script's own `process.exit(stranded.length ? 1 : 0)` had already decided `0`; the 127 is libuv tearing down with the `fetch` keep-alive socket still open on Windows, and says nothing about the check. **So a session reading only the exit code would conclude the gate had failed when it passed**, and would refuse to apply a migration that was provably safe — or, worse, would learn to wave away a non-zero exit from this family of scripts and one day wave away a real one. **The shape is not specific to this script:** any one-shot `scripts/*.mjs` that `fetch`es the Supabase Management API and then calls `process.exit()` can do it, which is most of the `check-*` and reporting scripts, including ones whose exit code CI reads. **Fix (small, one place):** add a shared exit helper in `scripts/lib/` beside `env.mjs` that flushes stdout and lets the event loop drain before exiting — `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` after the last write, or close the keep-alive agent / pass `{ keepalive: false }` — and use it from the scripts that currently exit straight after a `fetch`. **Then prove it:** run the fixed `facility-map-holders.mjs` against test and read `echo $?` as `0`, twice. **While there, check whether CI is exposed:** any job whose step is a bare `node scripts/check-*.mjs` inherits the same ambiguity, and a flaky 127 there would read as a real failure and block a merge for nothing — `grep -n "node scripts/check-" .github/workflows/ci.yml`, and say in the PR which jobs were and were not affected. No schema and no user-visible surface, so `n/a` on the release-notes line. Worth doing because the cost is asymmetric: the bug makes a passing safety gate look like a failing one, and gates exist precisely for the moments when nobody has spare attention to debug them. Interim note for anyone who meets it before the fix: a non-zero exit **accompanied by an `async.c` assertion line** is noise; a non-zero exit **without** one is a real verdict. **Done 2026-10-16 (`claude/ci-script-fixes-fold`): `scripts/lib/exit.mjs` `exitWith()` replaces a bare `process.exit()` after `fetch` in 15 scripts (exit code now 0/1 as decided, reproduced 127 before and 0 twice after on `facility-map-holders.mjs`). CI runs on Linux where the libuv assertion is Windows-only, so no CI job was exposed. See `docs/decisions/2026-10-16-shared-exit-helper.md`.**

It has not bitten yet only because that timer is not installed (see the spare-clone item). **Fix:** `git update-index --chmod=+x scripts/pi/setup-test.sh scripts/pi/spare-clone.sh` and commit; two mode changes, no content. **Worth pairing with a guard**, since this is the second thing this week to reach `main` because nothing checks `scripts/` — a syntax error in `deploy.mjs` did the same on 2026-10-02 and CI was green on it (see that item). It states what it does not cover. Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-10-02-script-integrity-reads-the-index.md`.

The migration is fine — the harness predates `0108`. Fix: have it assert against the live views instead of replaying `0073`, or replay only the functions it tests.

- [x] **Bug: on Record a donation, "Choose resident" finds nobody when you search.** Lutan, 2026-10-09: choosing "For a resident" and searching in the picker does not work. **Almost certainly the cause (read 2026-10-09, not yet reproduced):** `src/app/management/donations/new/page.tsx` loads the picker's list with `supabase.from("residents").select("id, name, thai_name, current_status")`, but **`residents` has no `current_status` column** (0001 keeps status out of the table on purpose; it is worked out in `resident_list_view` / `resident_current_state`). The query therefore errors, the page ignores the error (`residents.data ?? []`), and the picker opens on an **empty list**, so every search shows "no residents". **Fix:** load from `resident_list_view` as the other pickers do (`src/app/immunizations/new/page.tsx`: `resident_id, name, thai_name, current_status`, mapped to `id`), probably leaving out deceased residents (`NOT_DECEASED`) unless a gift in memory of one should be recordable; ask Lutan. And **stop the silence:** check `error` on this query and show a message on the form instead of an empty picker, since an empty list that looks like "no matches" is what hid this. Worth a quick grep for other `.from("residents").select(...current_status...)` reads, which would fail the same way. Check on the donation's page and receipt that the chosen resident shows (`residents:designation_resident_id(name)`). Small, no schema. A `releases.ts` line (the Director will notice it working) and a test: search by English name, Thai name, pick one, save, the donation page names the resident. **Done 2026-10-10 (`claude/donation-picker-and-map-zoom`):** reproduced first on dev (PostgREST 42703, *column residents.current_status does not exist*), so the read cause was the real one. The picker now loads from `resident_list_view`, **deceased included** (Lutan, 2026-10-10: a gift in memory of an animal must be recordable; the row shows Deceased). A failed load is logged and shown on the form. The donation's own page now throws on a failed read instead of showing *not found* or *no receipts yet*. Grep found no other `current_status` read off `residents`; the wider `?? []`-without-`error` pattern is filed separately. Tested: English search, Thai search, a deceased resident, save, and the donation page reads *A resident: Summer*. The receipt PDF carries no designation, by design.

- [x] **`check-phone-width.mjs --clean` sweeps other runs, not just its own (tooling; found by the `0.24.0` release, 2026-10-10).** The sweep matches everything a run makes by pattern — `name like 'ZZ Width %'` and `phonewidth-` logins (line 597) — so it deletes **another session's in-flight** seed rows and throwaway logins as readily as a killed run's. Seen on 2026-10-10: a `--clean` during the release removed `phonewidth-admin / management / second-in-command-d45ea577@example.invalid`, a role set this checkout's script could not even produce, so another stream was evidently mid-run; it also cleared a stale login from 2026-10-03. Dev data is disposable so nothing was lost that matters, but with three streams running the sweep is a trap for whoever is in the middle of a run. **Fix:** scope it to the current run id, or to rows older than an hour, and print what it removed. **Not closed by PR #509**, which fixed the Staff principal (the ticked item above) and did not touch the sweep.

Previously released entries stay as they are — they are history, and untagged reads as everyone. Worth doing in the same PR as any future note that needs one of the three.

- [x] **DONE 2026-10-28 (`claude/release-tooling-and-audit-trigger`): `release-prs.mjs` now asks GitHub for any commit it cannot place and labels each PR `[from git]` or `[from github]`; offline it behaves as before. Proven on the 0.40.9 range: 29 PRs, #1008 and #1009 from GitHub.** Original: `release-prs.mjs` CANNOT SEE A SQUASH-MERGED PR AND HAS NOW COST THE RELEASE MANAGER A BY-HAND FIX IN THREE CONSECUTIVE RELEASES: let it ask GitHub which PR a commit belongs to, instead of exiting 1 and asking a person. Small, one script; nothing to decide.** **RAISED 2026-10-28 by the Production release manager** while cutting `0.40.9`, in its words: *"29 PRs in the range once the two squash-merged ones are added by hand — #1008 and #1009, both confirmed MERGED via `gh pr view`, which `release-prs.mjs` again missed with exit 1. That is the third consecutive release the squash-merge gap has fired; it may be worth a backlog item against the script rather than another by-hand fix."* **THE SCRIPT IS NOT WRONG TODAY, and that matters for how it is fixed.** Read 2026-10-28 by the planner: it builds the PR list from merge commits and their subjects, so a **squash** or rebase merge leaves no merge commit to read. The files that PR added then belong to no PR in the list, and it prints `DISAGREEMENT — N file(s) added in this range belong to no PR above`, names the file and the commit, tells you to find the PR on GitHub and add it by hand, and **exits 1** (`scripts/release-prs.mjs:97-105`). **It is refusing to guess, which is correct** — the one thing the fix must not do is silently invent a PR number. **THE FIX:** when an orphan file is found, ask GitHub which merged PR contains that commit (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/pulls`, or `gh pr list --search <sha> --state merged`), add it to the list, and **print that it was resolved from GitHub rather than from git**, so the release record says where each PR came from. **Keep the exit-1 refusal for any orphan `gh` cannot resolve**, and behave exactly as today when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated — the script must still work offline, which is presumably why it is git-only now. **Prove it** against the `0.40.9` range, where the answer is known: #1008 and #1009 must appear without a by-hand step, and the count must come to 29. **Why it is worth a slot rather than another manual fix:** the by-hand step lands in the middle of a release, which is the most expensive place to spend attention, and the release manager has to notice the exit code rather than the count — a release whose PR list is quietly two short is one whose pre-deploy test-plan check was run against the wrong set. → *Quick wins*
- [ ] **Six throwaway `harness_cards_*` roles are sitting on the dev database, left behind by check harnesses that did not run their `cleanup()`.** Found 2026-11-01 by `claude/label-thai-generator`, which counted them before and after its own run to prove none was its: `harness_cards_y4x44tz9`, `nm0arpqg`, `634vrkno`, `wel5ngx9` (29-30 October), `odut6h5q`, `ytzh0kg0`. `giveCards()` in `scripts/lib/user-role.mjs` returns a `cleanup()` its own comment says must be awaited in a `finally` block, so a harness that throws before reaching it, or is interrupted, leaves the role and its cards behind. They are harmless in themselves but they pad every per-role reading taken on dev, and `role-cells` / `role-cards` print them as if they were real roles. **Two parts:** delete these six, and find which harness leaks (the names say which cards, so `grep` for the card sets). **Do NOT delete them while other streams are running** -- a role another harness is mid-way through using disappears as an unexplained failure.

So the review formats the day-first text as if it were ISO, and `formatDate()` turns it into NaN. **What is saved is right:** the form submits the hidden input's ISO value by name, so the resident gets the correct intake date; only the review line is wrong. Confirm that on dev before closing. **Fix:** read the date by its submitted value (the `name`, through `FormData` or the hidden input), not the visible box, or have `DateInput` expose the ISO value; then **sweep for the same pattern**: any other review or summary step that reads a `DateInput` by id (grep `querySelector` and `getElementById` against fields rendered with `DateInput`, and every `formatDate(` fed from a form element). - [x] **Recurring jobs for staff, feeding My dashboard.** [done 2026-09-26: schema `0095` (#155), then Management → Recurring jobs (`src/app/management/recurring-jobs`) and the Recurring jobs section of My tasks (`src/lib/my-tasks/recurring.ts`), including the sick-week hand-over form; see docs/decisions.md 2026-09-26.] Lutan, 2026-09-25. Let management set up jobs that repeat on a calendar and are assigned to a person (or a team, like maintenance, 0063). Examples: "stocktake of on-hand medication, every Monday morning, staff member X", then "order and buy medication, every Monday after the stocktake is done, staff member Y". **Templates vs occurrences:** a `recurring_jobs` template (title, description, assignee(s), recurrence rule, time of day such as morning/afternoon, optional link to the screen the job is done on, active flag) produces *occurrences* that are transient. Each one shows on the assignee's My dashboard (the item above) for its day and is marked done or skipped, and only that result is kept (who, when, a note), so there is a record that the stocktake happened. Decide whether occurrences are generated ahead (a cron in `worker/`, or on first read of the day) or computed from the rule and stored only when acted on; the second avoids a job table filling with future rows. **Recurrence:** a small, explicit subset rather than full iCal RRULE: every N weeks on chosen weekday(s) (weekly, fortnightly with a start date as the anchor), monthly on day N, monthly on the Nth weekday ("first Monday"), with a start date and an optional end date. Dates are in Asia/Bangkok. **Order between jobs:** "after the stocktake" means an occurrence can depend on another template's occurrence the same day, and shows as "waiting for stocktake" until that one is done. **Missed jobs:** decide whether an undone occurrence stays overdue on the dashboard until done or skipped (suggest yes, with how many days late) or quietly expires. **Admin:** a Management page to create, edit, pause and reassign templates, with a preview of the next few dates, and reassignment when a login is archived. The stocktake example links naturally to the "Stock on hand" item below; the job can deep-link to its count screen, `/stocktake` (`?tab=diets` opens the Diets tab), which staff and volunteers can use (0091). Needs its own schema PR first. **Reassigning one week** (Lutan, 2026-09-26): if someone is sick, management can hand that date's occurrence to someone else without changing the job, and the next week goes back to the usual person; the schema for it is in `0095` (cover team per date, `reassign_recurring_job()`, docs/decisions.md 2026-09-26), and the admin page needs the form, including "all of X's jobs for these dates → Y". Manual topic in `src/lib/manual/en.ts` / `th.ts`.

- [x] **Microchip number on a resident, searchable from a chip scanner.** Done 2026-09-30 across 0113, PR 221, 0116 and `claude/microchip-vet-feature` (0117); see the second-half item below and `docs/decisions/2026-09-30-microchip-second-half-vet-form-public-boolean.md`. Two reasons: overseas adoptions need it (a microchip is the first thing an export permit and the destination country ask for, and `/adopt/international` already lists it), and the app should encourage shelters to chip their animals rather than treat it as optional. **Why now, when it isn't standard practice:** `0060_adoption_recommendation.sql` and `docs/decisions.md` (2026-09-21) left the field out because microchipping isn't done as a matter of course in Thailand. Add a `docs/decisions.md` entry saying so, which extends rather than contradicts the 0060 one. "Microchipping" already exists as a procedure type (0031), so the act of chipping can already be logged, just not the number. **Schema PR first:** `residents.microchip_number text` (nullable), stored as digits only (strip spaces and dashes on save), **unique** across residents where set (a partial unique index, so a mistyped duplicate is caught), with a check that allows the ISO 11784/11785 standard 15 digits and, if the shelter has older chips, 9/10-digit ones too (ask Lutan whether any exist before tightening it). Optional `microchip_implanted_on date`. Locked with the rest of the record on death (the 0026 trigger's column list). **Where it is entered:** Edit resident and the intake wizard (Health step), and offered straight after a "Microchipping" procedure is logged ("Record the chip number?"). Show it on the hub's details card, in the deceased archive PDF and index, and on the vet-visit and procedure views where a vet needs it. **Scanner search:** handheld and USB/Bluetooth microchip readers act as a keyboard: they type the 15 digits and press Enter. So (1) the `/residents` search and the header search match `microchip_number` exactly (after stripping non-digits), alongside name and R-code; an exact chip match jumps straight to that resident's hub, whatever the place/zone filters or deceased toggle say; (2) a small **Scan a chip** box (autofocused input, e.g. on `/residents` and the intake wizard's first step) so a staff member can scan a stray at the gate: a known chip opens the resident, an unknown one offers "New resident with this chip" prefilled. Phones cannot read the common 134.2 kHz (FDX-B) chips over NFC, so do not promise phone scanning; test with a real reader Lutan has, or by typing into the box. **Privacy and public site:** the number stays staff-only. Do not add it to any `public_*` view; the public resident page may show "Microchipped: yes" (a boolean derived from the column), which is the flag 0060's "Desexed / Vaccinated" ticks were meant to have. Vets see it for residents in their scope. **Encouraging chipping:** a count on the management dashboard (residents without a chip), a filter on `/residents` ("No microchip"), and a gentle prompt on the hub for a resident marked ready for adoption with no chip. It is a MISSING CHIP, and the machinery to add it already exists.** **WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, so nobody rewrites it:** `STATUS_CHIPS` in `src/lib/residents/list-view.ts:16` is `["Adopted", "Fostered", "Hospitalised"]`, and `applyFilters` applies a picked chip as `eq("current_status", status)` (line ~84) — **already exclusive, already "that status and nothing else", exactly the behaviour he asked for on the vet visits page.** **THE GAP: "Deceased" IS NOT IN THAT LIST**, so no chip can ask for it, and the only control that reveals the deceased at all is **Show all** (`?all=1`, `showAll`, line 165), which adds them to the living (`listQuery` applies `NOT_DECEASED` unless `showAll`, line 231). **So the deceased can only ever be seen MIXED IN with everyone else — which is precisely why finding one is difficult.** **THE FIX, and it is two small pieces:** (1) add `"Deceased"` to `STATUS_CHIPS`; the value is already the live `current_status` string (`DECEASED = "Deceased"`, `src/lib/residents/status.ts:14`) so `eq("current_status", "Deceased")` needs no new predicate; and (2) in `listQuery`, **skip the `NOT_DECEASED` clause when that chip is the one picked** — otherwise the chip asks for the deceased and the surrounding query removes them again, and the list comes back empty. **(2) IS THE WHOLE TRAP; a stream that does (1) alone ships a chip that always shows nothing.** Then the chip in the UI and the string in **both** dictionaries. **DELIBERATELY NOT IN SCOPE, each for a reason:** **Show all** stays as it is — its label says *all* and that is what it does, so it is not the mislabelled-additive fault, and it is the useful "search across everything" escape hatch that the deceased-name-match banner (`deceasedMatches`, `src/app/residents/page.tsx:229`) already leans on. **The zone chips** are a genuine multi-select — two zones picked means both zones (`in("zone_id", zoneIds)`) — which is normal and is not additive-in-the-bad-sense; **the Unallocated chip** adds to the zones **by design and is documented as doing so** (`list-view.ts`, the `unallocated` comment). **Do not convert any of those three.** **RELATED BUT A DIFFERENT PAGE AND A DIFFERENT FAULT:** the vet-visits chip item in *Next up*, where two chips really are mislabelled and additive. **Same batch is sensible; same stream only if one session can prove both pages in the browser.** **PROOF:** with a deceased resident present, pick the chip and see only the deceased; unpick it and see the living; confirm **Show all** still behaves as before and the deceased-hidden count and name-match banner still read correctly. **A release note is owed** — he asked for this himself. Filed by the planner 2026-10-27. **>>> AND A SECOND HALF, FOUND 2026-10-27 WHILE CHECKING A QUESTION OF HIS, AND IT IS IN SCOPE RATHER THAN A NICETY.** He asked *"And hospitalised as well is needed"*, then *"That's fine I just didn't see it listed above"* — **Hospitalised DOES exist as a chip and nothing needs adding for it.** But looking for it found why he could not see it: **`src/app/residents/page.tsx:387` renders the status chips only as `zoneIds.length === 0 && !unallocated && !enclosureId`, so ALL THREE CHIPS VANISH FROM THE PAGE the moment a zone chip, Unallocated or an enclosure filter is set.** They are offered only on an otherwise unfiltered list. **WHY IT WAS BUILT THAT WAY, so nobody calls it a bug and rips the gate out:** `applyFilters` **ANDs** status with zone (`eq("current_status", status)` at line ~84, then `in("zone_id", zoneIds)` further down — the zone clause is NOT skipped when a status is picked), and adopted, fostered and hospitalised animals sit in the **Lifecycle pseudo-zone** rather than a real one, so **status + zone returns nothing.** Hiding the chips avoids offering a combination that always comes back empty. **It is a defensible fix to the wrong problem: it protects the user from an empty list by removing the control instead of making the control work.** **WHY IT BLOCKS THIS ITEM: a Deceased chip added without touching that gate WILL VANISH under a zone filter too**, so he would still be unable to find the deceased exactly when he is looking at a zone — **the new chip would be useless in the case he reported.** **THE FIX: show the status chips ALWAYS, and make picking one CLEAR the zone, Unallocated and enclosure filters in its `href` so it takes over the list** (the code comment at line 387 already reaches for this — *"One at a time; tapping the one that is on takes it off"*). **Do NOT instead make `applyFilters` drop the zone clause when a status is set** — that would leave the zone chip drawn and visibly active while silently doing nothing, which is the same disagree-with-the-screen fault as the vet-visits chips. **CHECK while in there:** `hiddenStatuses` (line ~152) counts silently-hidden statuses **only when there is a search term (`q`)**, so browsing by zone with no search hides these animals with no notice at all; say in the PR whether that is still needed once the chips always show. **>>> DECIDED 2026-10-27 (Lutan): "Yes all of those chips below need to clear the zone chip selections."** **THE RULE: every chip in the row below the Filter button takes over the list — picking one CLEARS the zone chips, Unallocated and the enclosure select in its `href`.** That is FIVE controls, not three: the **deceased toggle** (`toggleHref`, `src/app/residents/page.tsx:382`) **and** Adopted, Fostered, Hospitalised **and** the new Deceased chip. **THE DECEASED TOGGLE IS IN SCOPE AND THE PLANNER CONFIRMED WHY, 2026-10-27:** `src/lib/residents/place.ts:16` says outright that **'Adopted' and 'Deceased' are history, not a place** — *"These show only under Everywhere"* — and `list-view.ts` says the three status chips sit in the **Lifecycle pseudo-zone, not a real one, the Off-site chip included** (see the `narrowed` comment, `page.tsx:145-151`: *"Any zone chip (Off-site too: they sit in the Lifecycle zone, not an off-site one), Unallocated or enclosure hides all three"*). **So ANY zone chip hides all four history statuses, and "Show all deceased" with a zone picked shows NO deceased and says nothing about it.** That is the same silent miss, reached through the toggle instead of the chips. **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE:** once every chip clears the zone picks, the `zoneIds.length === 0 && !unallocated && !enclosureId` condition at `page.tsx:387` **has nothing left to protect and comes out** — the chips are always drawn. **That is the whole reason the gate existed** (it stopped an always-empty status+zone combination), so removing it and adding the clearing in the same change is correct; **removing it WITHOUT the clearing would ship exactly the empty list it was guarding against.** **STILL DO NOT make `applyFilters` silently drop the zone clause when a status is set** — that leaves a zone chip drawn and visibly active while doing nothing, which is the screen-disagrees-with-behaviour fault this whole round came from. **Clear the selections in the URL so the screen and the list always agree.** **PROOF, and it is the deliverable:** with a zone chip active, tap each of the five in turn and confirm the zone chip comes off, the list shows that status, and the chip row still reads correctly; then confirm the `hiddenStatuses` notice and the deceased-hidden count are either still right or no longer needed, and say which in the PR. **DONE 2026-10-27 (`claude/filters-say-what-they-do`).**

Lutan, 2026-10-05: on `/medical/photos` (Add Medical Photos, the Head of Medical's job) staff may struggle to find the right dog in the picker without help. **The cards (Lutan, 2026-10-05):** every resident has its **own name card**: credit-card-sized plastic with the dog's photo and name on the front and an **NTAG215, 13.56 MHz NFC** chip inside, which every NFC phone can read without an app (iPhone XS or later, Android with NFC on). Each card is encoded with the resident's link, **`/r/<R-code>`** (`src/lib/tags/links.ts`, from 2026-09-22's "Copyable links for enclosure QR codes and resident RFID cards"), which normally opens the resident's page. The card belongs to the resident, not the enclosure, so it stays right when a resident moves. **The ask: take the resident out of the card's URL and use it in this search.** The medical jobs already accept a chosen resident (`/medical/photos?resident=<id>`; check `/medical/weight` and `/medical/diets` the same way), so the whole job is turning a scan into that parameter: (1) **Android, Chrome:** a *Scan card* button in the resident picker uses Web NFC (`NDEFReader`) to read the card's URL record, takes the R-code after `/r/`, looks it up (the same lookup `/r/[code]` does, `loadResidentCard`; an older card may hold a raw UUID, which `/r/` already accepts) and opens the form for that resident, without leaving the page. (2) **iPhone, Safari:** there is **no Web NFC**, and holding the phone to a card always opens its link in a new Safari tab, which the page cannot intercept. So make the link do the work: *Scan card* stores a short-lived "waiting for a card" marker (a cookie naming the job, e.g. medical photos, for about five minutes) and tells the user to hold the phone to the card; when `/r/<code>` opens with that marker present and the user signed in and allowed that job, it **redirects straight to `/medical/photos?resident=<id>`** and clears the marker. Without the marker, a tap behaves as it does today. (3) **Both:** the picker's search box also accepts the **R-code** printed on the card, or a pasted card link, and pulls the code out. **Make it work signed in (Lutan, 2026-10-05: a card normally takes a person to the *public* page):** `/r/<code>` goes on into the app only when the browser the card opened has a signed-in staff session; on an iPhone that browser is always **Safari**, on Android the default browser, so staff signed in elsewhere land on the public card (its *Sign in* link is small). So: make *I work here: sign in* a large button at the top of the public card, returning to the scan afterwards (and keeping the waiting marker); tell staff to sign in once in the browser the cards open and stay signed in (sessions are long-lived, 60-day inactivity timeout); and check a phone kept on site stays signed in there. A home-screen app would not help on iOS, since cards open Safari, not the app. **Also fix where a signed-in tap lands with no job waiting:** today it is the resident hub, which a Head of Medical, Head of Maintenance or volunteer may not be allowed to open (`resident.record`), so a tap can end on the no-access page. Instead show "Panda (R-0042), Enclosure 5" with the photo and big buttons for the jobs this person can do for that resident (*Add medical photos*, *Record weight*, *Diet*, *Open record* only for roles that hold it), drawn from their permissions; with one job, go straight to it. **Safety:** before anything is saved the form shows the resident's photo and name large enough to check against the dog, so a card picked up from the wrong kennel is caught before a photo lands on the wrong record. Never use the card to *write* anything by itself: it only chooses the resident. **Scope:** the medical jobs first (photos, weight, diets), then the same scan in any other per-resident form. Phone-only by definition (no PCs on site). Manual (a "Scanning a name card" topic, both phones), both dictionaries, a releases line, and a test plan with a real card on an iPhone and an Android phone: scan from the form on each, a scan when not signed in, a card for a resident the person may not open, a deceased resident, an unknown code, and a waiting marker that has expired. **Staleness sweep 2026-10-14:** the "where a signed-in tap lands with no job waiting" part is done: `a3b44750`, `src/lib/residents/card-landing.ts`, `docs/decisions/2026-10-07-name-card-taps.md`. The scanning itself (Web NFC, the iPhone waiting marker, the R-code in the picker) is not built. **Built 2026-10-16 (`claude/name-card-scanning`, docs/decisions/2026-10-16-name-card-scanning.md):** the R-code or pasted link in the picker search, Scan card by Web NFC on Android, and the iPhone waiting marker (`/scan/arrive`) for Add Medical Photos and Record Weight; real-card checks on both phones still pending. **Built 2026-10-20 (`claude/nfc-medical-jobs`):** the public card's large *I work here: sign in* button. **Still open:** (built 2026-10-21, PR 798, scan on the immunizations form; every other picker is desk work or has none, list in docs/decisions/2026-10-21-scan-card-everywhere.md.) views (`vet_contacts` from 0126 and anything else with `vet` in it). **The `vet` role becomes `doctor`** (confirmed by Lutan, 2026-10-03: the vet login is the doctor's login): `alter type app_role rename value 'vet' to 'doctor'` keeps existing policies working, because they store the enum value, not the text, but every literal `'vet'` in `src/`, `worker/` and the check scripts has to change in the same release. - [x] **Units of measure: buy and count in one unit, feed or dose in another, with a conversion per item.** [done 2026-10-01 as `claude/units-of-measure-feature`: Units panel on Management → Medications / Diets, units on Record a delivery and the stocktake with the factor stamped server-side into `entered`, stock shown in the purchase unit, price per purchase unit; see docs/decisions/2026-10-01-units-of-measure-feature.md. The 2-decimal cost column refuses sub-1% precision, e.g. per-gram prices: follow-up on the backlog branch] From the backlog page's suggestion box (2026-09-26), confirmed by Lutan 2026-09-29. Dry kibble is bought in 20 kg bags but given to dogs by the cup; medicines arrive by the box or bottle but are given by the tablet or ml. **Today each item has exactly one unit**, used for everything: `diet_types.unit` (0051: "daily_qty_* and cost_per_unit are in this unit") and `medication.dose_unit` (0027). Stock on hand (0083), stock counts (0093) and deliveries (`stock_receipts`, 0096, which records the unit at receipt and expects "2 boxes of 50" to be converted by hand before saving) all use that same unit. So staff either count kibble in cups or feed in kilograms, and the forecast, stock and cost figures are only as right as that mental arithmetic. **Shape:** keep the item's existing unit as its **base unit** (the one feeding or dosing is recorded in, and what the forecasts already compute), and add a small per-item **conversion table**: other units it is bought, received or counted in, each with how many base units one of it holds (e.g. kibble: base `cup`; `kg` = 10 cups, `bag (20 kg)` = 200 cups; a tablet medicine: `box` = 50 tablets, `strip` = 10). Per item, not global, because a cup of one kibble weighs differently from another. Mark one conversion as the **purchase unit** and one as the **count unit** (can be the same) so forms default sensibly. **Where it is used:** "Record a delivery" takes a quantity in any of the item's units and stores both what was entered (quantity + unit) and the base-unit equivalent. The stocktake sheet (and the phone cards in the item above) counts in the count unit, e.g. "3 bags and 4 kg" if mixed entry is worth it, and saves base units through `record_stocktake()`. Stock on hand and days-of-stock can be shown in the purchase unit ("2.4 bags, about 11 days"). Cost moves to a **price per purchase unit** (what the receipt says: 850 baht a bag), with cost per base unit derived for the diet and medication forecasts and Cashflow. Doses, prescriptions, diets and forecasts stay in the base unit, so nothing there changes. **History must not shift:** existing counts and receipts are in today's single unit, which becomes the base unit, so they need no rewrite. Editing a conversion factor later must not silently re-value past rows, so each row keeps the base-unit amount it was saved with (0096 already snapshots the unit for the same reason). **Schema PR first** (a conversions table keyed on medication or diet type, like `stock_counts`' item-kind pair, plus the entered quantity/unit columns on `stock_receipts` and `stock_counts`); admin and management edit conversions on Management → Medications / Diets. Decide while building: whether a conversion factor can be approximate (a cup of kibble) and whether the page should say so; mixed-unit entry on the stocktake or one unit per line; and whether this settles the related open item "A single-cell stock edit writes no history". Check Stock between counts and Cashflow arithmetic end to end with a real kibble example. Manual (Medications, Diets, Stocktake, Deliveries topics), both dictionaries, a releases line and a `docs/decisions.md` entry for the base-unit rule. **Schema half done 2026-09-30 as `claude/schema-units-of-measure` (0118; see `docs/decisions/2026-09-30-units-of-measure-schema.md`) — the feature half builds against this:** table `item_unit_conversions` (`item_kind` + `medication_id` / `diet_type_id` as in `stock_counts`; `unit`, `base_units_per` > 0, `is_purchase_unit`, `is_count_unit` with at most one of each per item, `note`; unique per item by lower-cased unit; admin and management write, admin / management / staff / volunteer read). The base unit is the item's existing `dose_unit` / `unit`, unchanged. **The point-in-time factor** is `entered jsonb` on both `stock_receipts` and `stock_counts`: `[{"quantity","unit","factor"}]`, a copy of the factors in force when the row was saved, so editing a conversion never re-values history; `quantity` / `counted_quantity` stay the base-unit total and a CHECK requires sum(quantity × factor) to equal it. Null `entered` = entered in the base unit (all existing rows). `record_stocktake(jsonb, jsonb)` keeps its signature and now accepts an optional `entered` per element beside `id` and `count` (count in base units). Deliveries are written straight to `stock_receipts`: set `quantity` (base) and `entered` together. No cost column: price per purchase unit ÷ `base_units_per`. Still to do in the feature half: the forms and pages, refusing a conversion named like the base unit, stamping `factor` from the live conversion at save time, and the open decisions above.

- [x] **Doctors belong to a vet: investigate a managed list rather than free text.** Lutan, 2026-09-27, during Pass 0 of the role walkthrough. A clinic has many doctors — Novel has around 20 on staff — and the concern raised was that the relationship is modelled the wrong way round. It is not: `doctor_name` sits on `vet_appointments`, not on `vets`, so one vet already has many doctors. What is missing is anywhere to **manage** them. The column is free text by Lutan's own call on 2026-09-24 (`0074`, `docs/decisions.md`), with the cost written down at the time — "Dr Somchai" and "Somchai" stay two strings, so counting visits per doctor means grouping by hand — and that migration closed with "Promoting it to a lookup is its own item if that is ever wanted". This is that item. Today the only affordance is `loadDoctorNamesByVet` (`src/lib/vets/doctors.ts`), which harvests the distinct names already typed against each vet and offers them as a `datalist` on the vet-visit form. That stops a name being typed three ways, but a doctor nobody has recorded yet is not suggested, a typo becomes a permanent suggestion, and there is no screen where a clinic's roster can be seen or corrected. **To investigate:** whether a `vet_doctors` table (vet_id, name, active) with a nullable `vet_appointments.doctor_id` beside the existing text column earns its keep; how the names already recorded would be reconciled into it; and whether the shelter will actually maintain a 20-name roster per clinic or would rather keep typing with better suggestions. Note for whoever picks this up: the walkthrough's Pass 0 line "Management → Vets has at least one vet, and at least one has a doctor name" was wrong — the vet record has no doctor field — and has been corrected in `docs/role-walkthrough.md`. **Decided 2026-09-27 (Lutan): build both.** Schema half is #176 (`0102_vet_doctors_and_vet_accounts.sql`, applied to dev): a `vet_doctors` list per clinic that fills itself from typed names by trigger, `doctor_name` kept and following the list, `merge_vet_doctors`, `p_doctor_name` on `schedule_bulk_appointments`, and `user_roles.vet_id` + `current_user_vet_id()` for the vet-account→clinic link items 4 and 8 need. **Feature half still to do:** the list on the clinic hub (view, rename, deactivate, merge), the booking form passing `p_doctor_name` instead of its second write, suggestions from the list instead of `loadDoctorNamesByVet`, choosing a vet account's clinic in `/admin/security`, manual and release-notes line; tick this item then. **Done 2026-09-28** (`claude/vet-doctors-roster-screen`): Management → Vets → Doctors lists each clinic's doctors with their visit counts, and renames (saying how many visits the new spelling reaches), merges (pointing out look-alike spellings such as "Somchai" / "Dr Somchai"), marks a doctor as left, and adds or deletes an unused one; the clinic hub shows the list read-only; booking passes `p_doctor_name` in the one RPC call; the visit forms suggest the clinic's active doctors. The `/admin/security` clinic choice had already shipped with the vet-scope work.

- [x] **A single-cell stock edit writes no history, but the `0093` back-fill treated past ones as counts.** [done 2026-09-29 as `claude/stock-edit-history`, migration `0112`: Lutan chose one way in — `record_stock_correction()` writes a `source = correction` row, kept out of usage intervals; see docs/decisions.md 2026-09-29] Found 2026-09-27 while clearing UAT's stock figures. `record_stocktake()` writes a `stock_counts` row per item (`0093`), and the stocktake sheet goes through it. `updateMedicationStock` and its diet twin (`src/app/management/medications/actions.ts`) do not: they `update` the column directly, so `0083`'s trigger stamps `stock_counted_at` and nothing lands in the history. The result is that **Stock between counts cannot see a figure typed on the Management page** — four such edits on UAT this morning left no trace in `stock_counts` at all. What makes it more than a design choice is that `0093`'s back-fill *did* capture exactly those edits, one synthetic stocktake each, because all it had to go on was `stock_on_hand` and `stock_counted_at`. So a cell edit made before `0093` is history and the same edit made after it is not, which is the kind of split nobody will reconstruct later from the data. **To decide:** either route the single-cell edit through `record_stocktake()` so there is one way in, or leave it out of history on purpose and say so on the page — and either way `0093`'s comment should stop implying the two agree. Worth settling before the first real count, since that is when the history starts being worth something. **The display half is now done too (2026-10-01, `claude/stock-count-source`):** Lutan chose Stock between counts only, so a row there says when a figure was typed by hand during the dates being compared, in the table and in the CSV. No figure changes — a correction is still never paired into an interval. Labelling back-fill rows so they stop passing as real stocktakes was considered and declined for now, and is noted as still open in `docs/decisions/2026-10-01-corrections-on-stock-between-counts.md`.

Enforce it on the server too, not only in the form: the upload route is the thing that has to refuse.

Today a person belongs to exactly one clinic in two places, and both need to allow several. **(1) The doctor roster:** `vet_doctors` (0102) has a single `vet_id`, so a doctor who also works at a second clinic has to be entered twice, as two unrelated rows, and nothing shows they are the same person. Existing duplicate rows for the same person at two clinics can be merged afterwards from the clinic page (a "same person as…" merge), not guessed by name in the migration. **(2) Vet logins:** a vet account has one clinic, `user_roles.vet_id`, read through `current_user_vet_id()` by 18 places across `0102`, `0108` (which residents a vet sees) and `0110` (which clinic a vet may write for), plus `src/lib/vets/scope.ts`. A vet then sees the union of the residents their clinics treat; the vet-visit form's clinic, today fixed to their one clinic, becomes a choice among theirs (preselected when there is only one); Settings → Security gets a multi-select for a vet's clinics. Keep `current_user_vet_id()` working until nothing calls it, or replace all callers in the same PR. **Decided by Lutan, 2026-10-01: both,** the roster doctor and the vet login, **and a vet login is linked to its own doctor entry.** So: (3) a nullable, unique `user_id` on the doctor (one login is one doctor, and one doctor has at most one login), set in Settings → Security beside the vet's clinics (pick an existing doctor, or create one from the user's name). When a linked vet records a visit, the Doctor field is themselves, prefilled and locked to their own entry; staff and admins still choose any doctor at the visit's clinic. A doctor removed from a clinic keeps their past visits there. **Most doctors will have no login (Lutan, 2026-10-01):** many of the vets residents are taken to never use the system, so adding a doctor must need only a name and their clinic(s), with **no email, account or invitation**. That stays possible from the clinic page and from the vet-visit form (typing a new name, as today). A login is linked to a doctor afterwards, only if that doctor is ever given one, and unlinking or archiving the login leaves the doctor and their visits untouched. **Schema PR first,** then the feature; test with a vet login on two clinics that it sees both clinics' residents and no others, can record for either, and is refused for a third (`scripts/` check like the 0108 / 0110 harnesses). Manual (Vets, Security), both dictionaries, a releases line and a decision file in `docs/decisions/`. **Schema half done on `claude/schema-doctor-multi-clinic` (migration 0125, 2026-10-02); the feature half remains. Nothing left to decide.** Lutan, 2026-10-15, for the Director: once a visit is in her calendar, she would like to "move it in her calendar and push the change back to the system so she can manage her calendar as normal and the system polls for changes made to the calendar item in Google. This would also work for cancellations where a deletion from the calendar cancels the appointment in the system." **Possible, and free.** **How:** (1) every event the app creates carries the visit's id in the event's private properties (`extendedProperties.private.visitId`), so the app only ever looks at its own events and ignores everything else in her calendar (her other appointments, her hand-made entries); (2) the Worker's existing 15-minute cron asks Google for **only what changed since last time** (`events.list` with a `syncToken`, stored per calendar), so it is one small call per run; Google's push notifications (a `watch` channel) would be faster but need renewing about weekly and a public endpoint, so poll first and add push only if 15 minutes proves too slow; (3) **a moved event** sets the visit's date and time to the event's new start (in Asia/Bangkok); a change to the end time, title or description is ignored and put back on the next app-side sync, since the visit has no end and the title is generated; (4) **a deleted event** cancels the visit. **Safeguards to agree with Lutan, because a calendar delete is easy to do by accident on a phone:** the visit is marked cancelled with the reason *"Cancelled from Google Calendar"*, never deleted, so it can be restored; System status or the Upcoming visits page lists anything changed from the calendar in the last week; and (recommended) an email or in-app note to the Director saying "Novel - Blackie on 20 Oct was cancelled in your calendar; it is cancelled in Lanna Care too", so a mistaken delete is noticed. **Loops and conflicts:** the app records the event's `updated` time and etag after each write and ignores a change that is its own; if a visit was changed in the app **and** in the calendar since the last sync, the **app wins** and the calendar is put back, and the clash is listed for someone to look at (rare: one person, two places). A visit already completed is not changed by a calendar edit. **Who did it:** Google does not reliably say which person moved an event, so the audit row records the change as made *via Google Calendar* (the calendar's owner), not a named login. **Scope:** the same `calendar.events` token as the calendar item already reads as well as writes, so no new consent. **Limits to tell her:** a change shows in the app within about 15 minutes, not instantly; only entries the app created are synced back (if she drags a hand-made entry, nothing happens); a new entry she types in the calendar does **not** create a visit (booking stays in the app, where the resident and clinic are chosen). Schema: a `calendar_sync_state` row (calendar id, sync token, last run) and the visit's `calendar_etag`; one schema PR, or fold into the calendar item's if both are built together. Manual (moving and cancelling from your calendar), releases line, decision file, test plan: drag an event to another time and see the visit move within 15 minutes; delete one and see the visit cancelled with the reason and the note sent; change it in both places and see the app's version win and the clash listed; edit an unrelated event and see nothing change. **STATUS 2026-10-20:** SUPERSEDED: "build phase 1 first" and "Not started" — phase 1 is shipped. Schema half is `0232`: table `calendar_sync_state` (calendar_id, sync_token, last_run_at, last_ok_at, last_error; service role only) and `clinic_visits.calendar_etag` + `calendar_event_updated_at`. App half must: write the etag and updated time after every app-side event write, poll `events.list` with the syncToken from the 15-minute cron, and apply move/cancel/clash rules above. Nothing else left to decide beyond the safeguards already listed.

Raised while asking whether removing `frequency_id` could lose *twice weekly*: it cannot, because the form today offers only *times a day*, *every N days/weeks/months* and *as needed*, so a twice-weekly dose (say Monday and Thursday) **cannot be stored at all** and is entered as *every 3 days* or in the notes. This item adds what is missing rather than preserving something that exists. **The shape:** like a calendar's repeat setting. (a) **Which days:** every day; every N days; every N weeks on chosen weekdays (twice weekly = Mon + Thu); every N months on chosen days of the month (or the start date's day); as needed (no schedule). (b) **Which times on those days:** Morning, Lunch, Evening, **Night**, each with its own amount (the per-round amount already exists: `prescription_rounds.dose_quantity`, `0234`). (c) Start and end date, as now. **The schedule is then the only truth:** doses due on a day = the times ticked on that day, and the medication list, the medicine forecast (`medication_forecast()` / `prescription_doses_between()`, `0044`), stock usage against plan and the dose-due state all read it. **TWO EARLIER DECISIONS THIS DELIBERATELY REVERSES — say so in the decision file, quoting both:** (1) *"THREE rounds stay, there is NO fourth round, and an extra dose is written in a free-text note"* (Lutan, 2026-10-20, the prescription schedule item): Night is now a fourth round. (2) *"the tick count must NEVER become `doses_per_day`"* (`docs/decisions/2026-10-20-prescription-round-dose-schema.md`): under this design the ticked times ARE the count. **That rule existed to stop medicine silently vanishing from the forecast, and the reason survives even though the rule does not:** a prescription saved today as 4× daily with three ticks plus a note must NOT become 3× daily in the back-fill. **Back-fill rule: every existing prescription whose dose count differs from its ticks is listed for a person to fix, never guessed**, and the forecast is not switched over until that list is empty. **Done when, besides the build:** for the same date range, the medicine forecast totals before and after the switch-over agree for every prescription that was not on the fix list; every prescription's schedule reads the same before and after on the medication list; and a twice-weekly prescription (Mon + Thu) shows on exactly those days and forecasts exactly two doses a week. **ANSWERED 2026-10-30 (Lutan, in chat), all four; do not re-ask:** (1) **Four times a day is the most.** *"keep it to 4 with additional notes if something needs to be given hourly - this will be very rare so would be managed by the staff anyway if they had to keep hourly vigil on an animal"*. So: one dose amount per time slot, four slots, anything more frequent goes in the notes. **Consequence to state in the decision file:** doses written only in notes are not in the forecast, so the rare hourly case is under-counted there by design; existing prescriptions with more than four doses a day go on the back-fill fix list like any other mismatch. (2) **Night is about 10 pm, and it is for medication only:** *"Night rounds will probably be around 10pm, it is only for medication"*. (3) **Diets** have the same Morning/Lunch/Evening rounds (`reset_diet_rounds()`): does Night come to diets too, or medication only? - [ ] **A RELEASE NOTE CANNOT BE ADDRESSED TO ADMIN, SO EVERY ADMIN-ONLY FEATURE ANNOUNCES ITSELF TO EVERYONE. Found and reported by PR #1106 2026-10-30; filed by the planner, because it was in a PR body and on a ticked item. Nothing to decide about Admin itself — this is about the notes.** **THE MECHANISM, read 2026-10-30:** `src/lib/releases.ts` tags a note by **CARD** — `{ text, cards: CardKey[] }`, and its own comment says a note *"plainly not for everyone is tagged by CARD"*. An untagged note is a plain string and reads as everyone's, which is the deliberate widen-never-narrow default (`CLAUDE.md`, the no-named-role-fallback rule). **But Admin holds no cards and never will** — it sits outside the card system by Lutan's decision of 2026-10-25 — **so there is no tag that means "admins only", and an Admin-only feature can only be announced as a plain string to every login.** #1106 hit this with the new Assistant log screen and said so: *"a note cannot be tagged Admin-only, so every login will see it."* **WHY IT IS NOT A SECURITY FAULT:** a note grants nobody anything, so `check-hard-coded-security.mjs` is right to pass it. The cost is that volunteers read about screens they cannot open, which is exactly the confusion the card tagging exists to prevent. **OPTIONS, none chosen — this wants a decision before a build:** (a) an explicit `admin: true` on a note, read through the same `perms.isAdmin` short-circuit `can.ts` uses, which keeps Admin outside the card system and adds no card; (b) leave it and write Admin-only notes so they read harmlessly to everyone; (c) suppress untagged notes for non-Admin logins, which would change every existing untagged note's audience and is probably wrong. **(a) is the planner's reading of the least-surprise option, but it is NOT established that Lutan wants notes to carry an Admin flag at all** — ask before building. **Small either way, app only, no schema.** → *Admin*

- [x] **DONE 2026-10-26 by `small-fixes-bills-worktree` (#968), commit `89fa9eb1` "worktree list survives an unreadable process table" — filed and fixed the same day, and never ticked. Verified by the planner 2026-10-27 by reading the code, not the commit title: `parseProcessTable()` blanks control characters and returns `null` rather than throwing, so `list` can no longer be taken out by a process outside the repo. **The sibling check the item asked for is done too:** `holders()` sets `holdersUnreadable` and warns when the table will not parse, and the comment records that `held()` stays the authority on whether a folder is in use — so `done` cannot read an unreadable table as a false "free". The other `JSON.parse` sites are guarded as well (`gh` output at :164 returns a verdict, session files are skipped in a catch). ORIGINALLY FILED AS: **`worktree.mjs list` dies on a `JSON.parse` of the process table, so the worktree registry cannot be read at all while some unrelated process is running (script fix, small; seen 2026-10-26 by the planner, twice in one session — once crashing, once fine).** **What happened:** `node scripts/worktree.mjs list` printed a wall of raw process JSON and then `SyntaxError: Bad control character in string literal in JSON at position 184196`, thrown from `holders()` at `scripts/worktree.mjs:250` via `cmdList` at `:565`. **Ten minutes later the identical command worked.** So it is not the repo state — it is **whatever happened to be running**: `holders()` shells out for the process list (`ProcessId`, `Name`, `CommandLine`, `ExecutablePath`) and `JSON.parse`s it, and **one process whose command line contains a raw control character makes the whole parse throw.** **Why it matters more than a cosmetic crash:** `CLAUDE.md` makes `git worktree list` / `worktree.mjs list` **the registry** — *"every `claude/*` branch has a worktree and every worktree has a live session or a PR waiting"* — and it is the first command `/plan-day` step 2 runs and the one that reports `dirty`, `ahead`, `unpushed` and `held`. **When it throws, the planner is blind to every stream at once**, including the `ahead`-with-no-PR column that distinguishes unsubmitted work from a leftover. The failure is also **intermittent and depends on unrelated software**, which is the worst shape: it will come back on a different day with no change to the repo. **Do:** make `holders()` tolerate a process table it cannot parse. Parse defensively (strip control characters before `JSON.parse`, or ask for a narrower, quoted field set, or parse per-row and skip rows that fail), and **degrade rather than throw** — a `held` column reading `unknown` for one row is fine; losing the whole table is not. **Wrap the call in a try/catch that reports `held: '?'` and carries on**, so `list` can never be taken out by something outside the repo. **Check the siblings in the same pass:** anything else that `JSON.parse`es shelled-out process or `gh` output (`worktree.mjs` `done`, which refuses while a folder is held, is the one that matters — a false "free" or a crash there is worse than in `list`). **Nothing to decide.** It is not urgent: the command works most of the time, and the workaround is to run it again.

Find out which six visits it counts and why they never clear, then make the tile say only what is true and name the visits (investigate first; cause NOT yet established; small).** **Reported by Lutan 2026-10-25:** *"all vet visits are sync'd between google calendar and the app so I don't understand why this is showing as an error"*. **What the tile counts (read 2026-10-25):** `checkCalendar()` in `src/lib/clinics/calendar-sync.ts` counts every `clinic_visits` row whose `calendar_out_of_date_at` is set and either has no `calendar_synced_at` or is out of date AFTER its last sync (`isPending()`), with no date limit, so past and cancelled visits count too. `calendar_out_of_date_at` is stamped by the database trigger of `0207` (`clinic_visits_calendar_dirty`, using the database clock) whenever a visit's date, clinic, resident, status or archive changes; `calendar_synced_at` is stamped by the app (the Worker's clock, taken when the sync STARTED). The 15-minute sweep (`worker/index.mjs` → `/api/calendar/sweep`, cron in `wrangler.jsonc`) retries every such row, 40 per run, and a failure is written to the visit's `calendar_error` — **which the tile never shows**, so "waiting" and "failing every 15 minutes" look identical. **Dev has none (0 rows, 2026-10-25), so it is production only, and there is no read-only production check for it yet** — ad-hoc production reads are refused in this setup, so the first step is to add one. **Candidates, none proved:** (a) the six fail on every sweep (`calendar_error` set) — e.g. a visit whose event was made by the Director and imported (`calendar-import.ts`), deleted by hand, or on a past date where the delete or update is refused; (b) the Worker cron is not running the sweep on production (then new bookings would also wait — the tile would show it growing); (c) a visit is re-marked out of date after each sync, e.g. the Google→app poll (`calendar-poll.ts`) moving or cancelling it so the trigger stamps a newer time than the sync's start time; (d) visits already correct in Google that the app still holds as "out of date" because nothing re-synced them (a status change on a past visit: the sweep should clear these by writing `calendar_synced_at`, so if they stay, it points back to (a) or (b)). **Do:** (1) add a `calendar-pending` read-only check to `scripts/lib/readonly-checks.mjs` (run by `node scripts/check-production.mjs calendar-pending`) listing, for each counted visit, its date, status, archived or not, whether it has an event id, `calendar_synced_at`, `calendar_out_of_date_at` and `calendar_error` — no resident names in the output (the repo is public; ids and dates only); (2) run it on production and establish the cause from those rows — write down which candidate it was, or the real one; (3) fix the cause; (4) **make the tile honest:** say "failing" with the error when visits carry `calendar_error`, and list the visits (date and resident, linked to each visit) so Lutan can see which ones, rather than a bare count; decide in the decision file whether past visits should count at all — a past visit's calendar state matters to nobody, and counting them is what lets a harmless leftover read as an error. **Test plan:** the check's output before and after on production; the tile on dev with a visit forced into each state (pending, failing, past) via a rolled-back or disposable dev row. **DONE 2026-10-26 (`claude/calendar-pending-tile`):** cause established from production rows: the Worker's 15-minute cron stopped on 2026-10-23 at 10:00 UTC (the status-alert run and the calendar poll both last ran then), so the six visits are ones edited since, never retried; none carries an error and the gaps are about 26 hours, which rules out (a) failing, (c) re-dirtying and (e) clock skew. The tile now lists the visits with their last error, calls errored ones failing, and says when the sweep has gone quiet. `node scripts/check-production.mjs calendar-pending` and `calendar-cron` are the checks. **Left, and Lutan's: restore the production cron (filed as its own item).** → *Admin*

(2) **Levels that flow down:** a card may include another: **Residents** includes **View residents** (who and where, read) and adds the full record, edit, move, and add photos; **Medical** includes **View residents**; so giving the higher card gives everything below it, and the page shows "includes View residents". Lutan's example is the target: View residents vs Residents, with photo upload following the edit card. Cards are built from the existing activities, so `has_permission()`, every policy and `can()` are untouched. (3) **Enforcement stays where it is:** `role_permissions` remains the table the database checks; it becomes the **union of the role's cards' bundles**, recomputed when a role's cards change (one function, audited like a cell change today). Overlaps are fine (Stocktaking and Purchasing both read stock): removing one card keeps whatever another card still gives. (4) **Exceptions:** a role may still hold a single extra activity no card gives (today's cells that fit no card); keep them as **extras**, listed under the role's cards with why, so moving to cards changes nothing for anyone on the day it lands; the migration reports every cell that became an extra. - [x] **Bug: Settings → Security shows "Minified React error #441" instead of saying what went wrong.** Reported by Lutan 2026-09-26 with a screenshot on the dev-coloured site: an action on the archived `manager@gmail.com` row (Restore or Delete) failed and the row showed only "Minified React error #441; visit https://react.dev/errors/441…". **What #441 is:** React's production stand-in for *any* error thrown from a Server Action (`resolveErrorProd` in `react-server-dom-*-client.browser.production.js`). In a production build the real message is stripped before it reaches the browser, so `throw new Error(...)` in a `"use server"` file never shows its text to the user, **not even the friendly translated ones** (`t.admin.security.errors.cantDeleteOwnAccount` and the like). **So it is two fixes. (1) This page:** `src/app/admin/security/actions.ts` throws in every action (create, approve, change role, temporary password, archive, restore, delete). Make each return a result (`{ ok: true } | { ok: false, error: string }`) and have `UsersTable.tsx` / `AccessRequests.tsx` / `CreateUserForm.tsx` show `error`. Map known failures to plain words in both languages. Log the raw error server-side. **The failure in the screenshot is confirmed** (Lutan, 2026-09-26): it was **Delete** on a login with records against it. About 20 foreign keys to `auth.users` have no delete rule, so a delete is refused as soon as the person created anything: `created_by` on ten tables (from 0001 on), `uploaded_by`, `updated_by`, `user_id` on `assistant_actions` (0070), and others. **Don't fix it by changing them to `on delete set null`:** that would erase who recorded what, and that history is the point. Archive (0063) is the right tool for someone who has left. Instead, Delete is for accounts with no history (a typo, a test login). Before deleting, check the references (a small `security definer` function that counts them, or catch the error), and either hide Delete for such users or answer "This person has records in the system, so they can't be deleted. Archive them instead." **(2) The same pattern across the app:** at planning time 13 `"use server"` files under `src/app` held 98 `throw new Error` lines. Every one that can happen in normal use (validation, "not allowed", a clash) shows #441 in production. Sweep them to the return-a-result shape (the `upload-worker-error` fix already did this for uploads). Keep `throw` only for genuinely unexpected failures, and give those a generic "Something went wrong, please try again" plus the error's digest so it can be looked up in the Worker logs. Do the Security page first as its own small PR, then the sweep. The manual needs no change. Add a releases line (people will see real messages).
