The capacity was never checked, only assumed, and the whole concern was invented by that assumption.** **Do not reinstate it.** Capacity is ample for everything in this plan — the sensors add nothing measurable. **Still add a disk-space tile for the Green itself** alongside the Pi’s, but as ordinary monitoring rather than because anything is wrong: the box doing the monitoring should be monitored too. **THE WHOLE-OF-HOUSE DASHBOARD IS A SEPARATE PIECE OF WORK AND DOES NOT BELONG IN THIS REPO.** He wants help designing one in the same sitting, which is sensible — same tool, and the shelter tiles should sit beside the house ones rather than in a silo. **But this repository is PUBLIC**, and a house design names his rooms, devices, cameras, presence and alarm setup: his home’s layout and occupancy, published. **Do not commit it, do not attach it to a PR, and keep house entity names out of `docs/home-assistant-monitoring.md`,** which covers the shelter monitoring only, with placeholders. **The house design is a deliverable for `C:\Users\Leidos\OneDrive\Desktop`, and it is a conversation with him rather than a workstream** — it is his house and his preferences. **Keep the two outputs physically separate from the start.** One design note already worth carrying over: he runs **five different switch-and-plug ecosystems plus Matter and Thread**, so the same kind of device arrives under several naming conventions — **naming and grouping is where the house work actually is**, not integration. And **nothing is measuring electricity**, which in a house with air-conditioning is usually the most useful thing a dashboard can show; **some of his existing smart plugs may already report power** — check before designing around it. **THE SHELTER DELIVERABLE IS UNCHANGED** — the read-only `GET /api/status/health` endpoint with its own bearer token, the HA sensors that read it, the independent uptime checks, Pi health via Glances, the Cloudflare traffic figures and the phone alerts, all as set out below. **ADDED 2026-10-19 (Lutan): a wall-mounted touchscreen for the dashboard.** *"Sourcing an appropriate touchscreen for me to have the dashboard displayed and mounted in the house to support things like opening the front gate, viewing cameras, seeing status of the network and website."* **Part of the same guided session, ending in a short buying guide on his Desktop** (options, prices seen on Lazada or Shopee in Thailand on the day, and the recommendation), plus setting it up once bought. This is a **one-off purchase of Lutan's own hardware**, not an ongoing cost, so the zero-ongoing-cost rule is not touched; still prefer options with **no subscription or licence that renews**. **Options to compare:** (a) **a tablet as a wall panel** (an 8-10" Android tablet, or an Amazon Fire HD 10 if sold locally) running the **Home Assistant Companion app** in kiosk mode (free) or **Fully Kiosk Browser** (one-off licence, adds wake-on-motion and screen dimming), on a wall bracket with a USB power line to the wall; cheapest and easiest; (b) **a Raspberry Pi with the official Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2** in a wall frame, running a Chromium kiosk pointed at the dashboard; fits the kit he already runs, no battery to swell, but more to build; (c) **a dedicated smart-home wall panel** (PoE or in-wall, 7-10"); neatest, most expensive. Weigh: screen size and brightness for a hallway, **always-on power without a swelling battery** (a tablet kept at 100% for years is the known risk: use a charge limit, or a model or setup that runs without the battery), wake on approach, viewing angle, and Wi-Fi vs a cable. **What it needs from Home Assistant, to check before buying:** (1) **the front gate**: what opens it today (a remote, a button, a smart relay?); opening it from HA needs a **relay or gate controller HA can drive** (e.g. a Shelly relay on the gate motor's push-button input, wired by an electrician if mains is involved); list it as its own purchase; (2) **cameras**: which cameras are installed and whether they offer **RTSP or ONVIF** (or a native HA integration) so the panel can show live views; (3) **network and website status**: the tiles from this item's monitoring part (System status, Pi health, Cloudflare traffic), and the network from the home-network review item. **Safety, because a panel in the house can open the gate:** the panel signs in to HA as **its own limited user** that can see the dashboard and press the gate, not administer HA; the gate button asks for a **PIN or a long press**, and a gate opening is logged and notified to Lutan's phone; the panel sits on the network segment the home-network review decides (with Home Assistant, not on the guest network). **Done when** the panel is mounted, shows the dashboard, opens the gate (if the relay is fitted), shows the cameras, and its HA user cannot change settings. **ANSWERED 2026-10-19 (Lutan):** (1) **the gate already has a relay and is already in Home Assistant**, and also in **Alexa** for voice control in the house, so no gate purchase is needed; (2) the **Reolink doorbell** should give a live feed (Home Assistant has a Reolink integration, and the doorbell offers RTSP); (3) the **TP-Link PoE cameras** need investigating: find the model (TP-Link's **VIGI** business range generally offers RTSP and ONVIF; some **Tapo** models offer RTSP once a camera account is set in the app), then add them through ONVIF or the generic camera integration, and if they cannot, say so with the model; (4) **he prefers a smart wall panel, about 20", for the screen space**, so the buying guide centres on that: compare (i) a **21.5" wall-mount Android touch panel** (the kind sold for meeting rooms and smart homes, often PoE-powered, runs the HA app or a kiosk browser), (ii) a **21.5" touchscreen monitor with a small computer behind it** (a Raspberry Pi 5 in kiosk mode, or a mini PC), flush-mounted, and (iii) a **large tablet** only as the budget fallback; weigh power (PoE if a cable can reach, else a mains point behind the screen), mounting depth, brightness, a screen that dims or sleeps when nobody is near (burn-in on an always-on panel), and whether it can show **two or three camera feeds at once** smoothly (the computer behind option (ii) usually handles video better than a cheap Android panel). **One safety point to check while there, about Alexa:** a gate exposed to Alexa as a plain switch can usually be opened by voice **with no PIN**, by anyone within earshot of an Echo, and some setups also allow it from the Alexa app away from home. Check how the gate is exposed (a switch, or a lock or garage-door type, which lets Alexa ask for a voice PIN to open) and set a **voice PIN** if Alexa offers one; the wall panel's own gate button keeps its PIN or long press as above. **And (Lutan, same day): compare ALL the options, not only the wall panel**, the 20" wall panel, a touchscreen monitor with a computer behind it, and the tablet options, side by side with prices, so he can pick the one that fits the budget available at the time. The 20" panel is his preference, not a fixed choice; the buying guide ends with a recommendation **per budget** (e.g. best under a lower figure, best overall). **ADDED 2026-10-19 (Lutan): UPS options in the same buying guide, for the Pi, the Home Assistant, the routers and the switch.** This is the *keep the power on* option (3) of the Pi failover item under Next up (*Rethink Pi failover*), which names a power cut as the likeliest outage; do it here once rather than twice. **What must stay up together:** the **ISP router** and the **Deco main node** (the Cloudflare tunnel needs both), the **FR205** and the **switch** if the home-network review puts them in the Pi's path, the **Pi 5** (on its 27 W supply) and the **Home Assistant Green**; optionally the **PoE camera switch** and the **wall panel**, which add a lot of load for less benefit, so price them as a separate step. **Work out first:** the total draw (measure with a plug-in power meter if Lutan has one, else estimate from each power supply, and say which), and the **runtime wanted**: ask how long power cuts usually last at the house, then size for that plus a margin. **Compare:** (a) **one line-interactive UPS** (e.g. 650-1000 VA, pure sine wave preferred) under the desk feeding all of them, from brands sold in Thailand (APC, CyberPower and local brands such as Syndome or Cleanline); simplest; (b) **a DC mini UPS** (12 V / 9 V / 5 V outputs) for the routers and switch plus a **UPS HAT or USB-C power bank with pass-through** for the Pi; small, efficient, long runtime for low-power gear, but more pieces; (c) a mix. **Must have, whichever is chosen:** a **USB or network link** so the UPS can tell the Pi and Home Assistant when the battery is low (**NUT**, *Network UPS Tools*, which Home Assistant supports and the Pi can run), so the Pi **shuts down cleanly** before the battery runs out (an unclean power-off is what damages the NVMe and the database cache), and starts again when power returns (check the Pi boots by itself on power-up; Home Assistant Green does); a UPS status tile and a *power is out* phone alert on the dashboard; the replaceable battery noted with its rough life (3-5 years) and price, as the one cost that comes back. Recommendations per budget, like the screens. Record the chosen setup in `docs/pi-hosting.md` (in words, no home details) and tick option (3) of the failover item when it is in. **DECIDED 2026-10-19 (Lutan): the gate is not a security concern.** It is the property gate and gives no access to the house, so **no PIN, long press or voice PIN** is wanted for it, on the panel or in Alexa; drop the gate safety steps above (the Alexa voice-PIN check and the panel gate PIN). The panel's **own limited HA user** (it cannot change Home Assistant's settings) is about the panel, not the gate, and still stands. Do not raise gate security again.
- [x] **A logo or photo upload that exhausts the Worker shows the user a minified React error.** Done 2026-09-25: it was not the Worker. Next caps a Server Action body at 1 MB and rejects a larger one before the action runs, so every logo or Website photo between 1 and 15 MB failed where no app code could catch it (reproduced on dev: HTTP 500, `E394 Body exceeded 1 MB limit`). `next.config.ts` now lets the app's one limit through (`src/lib/uploads/limits.ts`, 15 MB, also used by every upload route), the clients pre-check the size and turn any thrown failure into words (`runUploadAction`), and `proxy.ts`'s 10 MB body cap was raised with it. What a Worker can really process is still unmeasured — see the follow-up item. Found 2026-09-24 on production, uploading a Shelter Friend logo: the page printed `Minified React error #441` and a link to react.dev, which decodes to "An error occurred in the Server Components render" — the message itself is stripped in production builds. The same image failed twice and a smaller one succeeded, so it is size- or format-dependent. It is **not** the app's own validation: `MAX_FILE_BYTES` (15 MB) and `ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES` both `return { error }` with readable text before Drive is touched, and the Drive calls themselves sit in a `try/catch` that returns a friendly message. So a file that passes validation is breaking *during* the upload, where nothing catches it. The likely mechanism: `drive.uploadFile` (`src/lib/google/drive.ts`) builds a multipart `Blob` holding the whole file in memory inside the Worker, and on the free plan that can exhaust memory or the 10 ms CPU budget — the same `1102` family as the render pressure the Pi origin is meant to fix. **Two things to do, and they are independent.** (a) Catch it: wrap the action so a resource failure reaches the user as "that image is too large to process — try one under about 2 MB" rather than a React error code. A user cannot act on `#441`, and it reads as the app being broken. (b) Decide the real limit: 15 MB is inherited from `admin/website/actions.ts` and is almost certainly higher than a Worker can actually process, so the number should reflect what works rather than what the form accepts. **The same limits and upload path are used by `/admin/website` photos and blood-test attachments** (`src/app/api/blood-tests/[id]/attachments/route.ts`), so whatever is wrong is wrong in three places. Worth re-testing after the Pi origin lands, since rendering and uploads move to real CPU and memory then and the failure may simply go away — but the error message should be fixed regardless, because the next resource limit will produce the same unreadable page.
- [x] **Measure the largest upload a Worker actually completes, and set the limit from it.** Follow-up to the #441 fix (claude/upload-worker-error, 2026-09-25), which found the reported failure was Next's 1 MB Server Action body cap, not the Worker, and raised the framework limits to the app's 15 MB (`src/lib/uploads/limits.ts`). Whether a free-plan Worker can buffer, parse and re-send a 15 MB file inside its CPU and memory budget was never measured. On test.lannacare.org, upload real photos of about 3, 6, 10 and 14 MB through a Shelter Friend logo and a resident photo, and read each request's CPU time and outcome in the Worker's observability logs. If anything below 15 MB hits 1102, lower `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` to what works (the `fileTooLarge` strings name the number, in en and th). The user now sees a readable message either way, so this sets the right number rather than fixing a broken page. Moot for requests the Pi origin serves once it is live. **Done 2026-10-07 without a measurement campaign: the Pi is live, and on the Pi path (test, production) the Worker streams the body to it and never parses or re-sends it, holding at most one 16 MB copy for the 530 fallback; the one Worker-rendered environment (uat) is not deployed. `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` stays 15 MB. Unmeasured and named: an upload while the Pi is off the network (docs/decisions/2026-10-07-worker-upload-limit.md).**

The dev hero had already been reset to a real photo by then; production's `hero_drive_file_id` was not checked from the worktree (handed to Lutan). Lutan, 2026-09-26. The dev (and test.lannacare.org) home page lost its hero photo: the hero is now `mid3.jpg` (Drive `1NAFh8O_pR5RBYTVjditj4nWo8qW1NL-2`), 3 MiB of zero bytes, uploaded on 2026-09-25 while testing the 15 MB upload limit (`docs/test-plans/upload-worker-error.md`, §4). It was accepted because every upload path trusts the browser's MIME type (`ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES`) and never looks at the bytes. Replacing the hero also permanently deleted the previous hero file from Drive, so the old photo can't be restored. **Fix:** check the file's leading bytes against the formats accepted (JPEG `FF D8 FF`, PNG `89 50 4E 47`, WebP `RIFF….WEBP`, GIF, HEIC `ftyp` box) in one helper beside `src/lib/uploads/limits.ts`. Call it from every image upload: Website hero and gallery, Shelter Friend logo, resident, project and maintenance photos. Refuse a mismatch with a readable en/th message before Drive is touched. Attachments that may be PDFs check `%PDF` the same way. **Also consider** not deleting the previous hero or gallery file until the new one is saved and confirmed readable, and moving it to Drive's trash rather than deleting it, so a bad upload can be undone. **Meanwhile:** set a real hero photo on dev under Settings → Website. If lannacare.org shows a broken hero too, check its `site_content.hero_drive_file_id` separately: that is the production database, which the upload test did not touch.

Still `2026-10-23T10:00:13Z` = not taken, and it becomes a Cloudflare SUPPORT question**, because everything on our side is eliminated. **ONE UNRESOLVED INCONSISTENCY, recorded rather than smoothed over:** our last run of 23 Oct **is inside** the week Cloudflare's Cron events page covers, yet that page reports no events at all. deleting and re-creating it changes nothing; **no commit touched `worker/` or `wrangler.jsonc` between the last working deploy and the breaking one** (`git log --since=2026-10-22 --until=2026-10-24 -- worker/ wrangler.jsonc` is EMPTY); **no dependency changed either** — the only `package.json` edits in that window are the release cuts' own version bumps, and the Next 16.4.2 advisory bump mentioned in a commit that morning is a BACKLOG NOTE, not an applied upgrade; The only thing that works is typing a street address, and **in Thailand Google often places a typed address at the wrong spot, or on a different business**. **Reproduce first, with real rows** (dev, and read-only on production when Lutan asks): note the exact address text and the URL the tap opens, for each failing contact and friend. **How it works today:** the address field holds either typed text or a pasted maps link, sometimes with text after it. The thumbnail is a keyless Google embed built from it (`addressMapEmbedSrc()`, `src/lib/contacts/map-preview.ts`, which follows `maps.app.goo.gl` short links server-side to find a place or coordinates). The tap opens `mapHref()` (`src/lib/contacts/contacts.ts`), which returns a pasted link **unchanged, including anything after it**, and `FriendCard` uses `map_location ?? address` the same way. **Likely causes to check, not conclusions:** (a) the tap opens the whole field (link plus trailing text, or a link with a space in it), which is not a valid URL; (b) **old-style `goo.gl/maps/…` short links stopped working in August 2025**, when Google shut down the Firebase Dynamic Links service behind `goo.gl`, so any contact saved with one now 404s at Google; `maps.app.goo.gl` links still work; (c) a short link that could not be resolved, so the thumbnail and the tap point at different things. **The fix:** (1) **Store a location, not just text.** Add `latitude` / `longitude` (or a place, e.g. Google's place ID plus coordinates) to contacts, and to Shelter Friends if they don't use the contact's (schema PR first). Get it **once, when the address is saved**, not on every view: from a pasted `maps.app.goo.gl` link (resolve it then, and refuse with a plain message if it cannot be resolved or is a dead `goo.gl/maps` link), from a pasted full Google Maps URL, from a **Plus Code** (common in Thai rural addresses), or from typed coordinates. Show **"Is this the right place?"** with a small map of the pin before saving, so a wrong location is caught when it is entered. (2) **Both the thumbnail and the tap use the stored coordinates** (`https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=<lat>,<lng>`, which opens the Maps app on a phone at that exact spot), never the address text. The typed address stays as the written address, for reading and for post. (3) **Guidance on the form,** in English and Thai: "In Google Maps, find the place, tap Share, copy the link and paste it here." That is what works for Thai addresses. (4) **Fix the existing rows:** a script that lists every contact and friend with an address that is a dead `goo.gl/maps` link, a link that does not resolve, or plain text, so Lutan or the Director can re-share the right link for each; the map is hidden for those (not a 404) until fixed. (5) **The website's contact map** (`site_content.contact_map_url`, Settings → Website) uses a similar link: check it the same way. Manual (Contacts, Shelter Friends: how to paste a location), both dictionaries, a releases line, and a test plan with a `maps.app.goo.gl` link, a dead `goo.gl/maps` link, a full Maps URL, a Plus Code, typed coordinates and a plain Thai address, each tapped on an iPhone and an Android phone. **Status 2026-10-08 (`contacts-map-404`): parts (3) and (5) done, and the 404 itself fixed; (1), (2) and (4) still open — they need a column, so schema first.** Reproduced: the one failing production row, I Blue Paw, holds a clean, working `maps.app.goo.gl` link, so none of (a)–(c) caused it — the 404 came from a tap *inside* Google's keyless embed, which goes wherever Google's embed decides. The thumbnail is now covered by our own link (`MapThumbnail`), and `addressMap()` gives the thumbnail and the tap from one lookup, so they can't disagree; a link plus trailing text opens only the link, a link that leads nowhere shows no map (the hub says so), and the contacts list's Map button uses the checked link too. (b) is weaker than written: Google kept active `goo.gl` links working after August 2025, so a `goo.gl/maps` link must be followed to be judged, not refused by its shape. Settings → Website (Management → Website) now refuses a map link Google answers 404 for. Related, and probably to be done together with (1): the separate Address / Map link fields item below. **Status 2026-10-08 (`contacts-address-map-schema`, `0164_contacts_map_url.sql`): schema half done, and the shape is `contacts.map_url`, a stored link — not latitude/longitude.** With no paid Maps API a pin can only be read out of a pasted link, and the link is already the exact place (it opens the Maps app on it, name and all); typed coordinates and Plus Codes fit as a `maps/search/?api=1&query=` link (`docs/decisions/2026-10-08-contacts-map-url-not-pin.md`). The column holds one link and nothing else (no spaces, http(s)); `public_shelter_friends.map_location` is now `coalesce(map_url, address)`, still under `show_map`. No rows moved yet — today's code reads the map from `address`, so the move goes with the feature. Still open: the forms, the hub/`FriendCard`/list reading `map_url`, the row move, and part (4)'s list of bad rows (done, next note). **Status 2026-10-08 (`contacts-link-audit`): part (4) done.** `node scripts/audit-contact-map-links.mjs` (read-only, dev by default, `--env production` when Lutan asks) lists every live contact — Shelter Friends included, since a friend's map is its contact's address — whose map link leads to no place, that is written words with no link, or that has words after a working link, each with what to do in plain words. - [x] **Management → Purchasing: how much of each medicine and food to buy, for a period you choose, with a safety stock.** Lutan, 2026-09-28. A Management page listing, per medication, a **recommended purchase quantity** so whoever does the ordering does not have to work it out. **The sum, per item, in its own unit:** *expected stock now* = last counted quantity (`stock_counts` / `medication.stock_on_hand`, 0093) − scheduled usage since that count (the prescription forecast, `doses_per_day` × `dose_quantity`) + receipts since that count (`stock_receipts`, 0096); *needed* = scheduled usage over the chosen period (from today) + **safety stock**; *recommended purchase* = needed − expected stock now, **never below 0**, rounded up to a whole pack if a pack size is known. **Period picker:** 1 week / 2 weeks (and perhaps 1 month / custom), reusing `src/lib/management/forecast-window.ts` as the forecasts already do. **Safety stock:** a new optional `medication.safety_stock` (numeric, the item's unit, null = none), set on the add/edit form in Management → Medications when an item is created or later, for items that are always in use whatever is prescribed today — IV/sub-Q fluids and the common antibiotics are Lutan's examples. It is a floor kept on the shelf, so it is added to *needed* on every period. Consider also adding the supplier lead time already stored (`reorder_lead_days`, 0083) to the period, so stock ordered today still covers the period once it arrives — say which in decisions.md. **Build on what exists, do not fork it:** `src/lib/management/stock.ts` already takes forecast usage off the last count to give days of stock; move the "expected stock now" part into one helper both pages call (and check whether it adds receipts since the count yet — if not, fix it there, so Medications' days-of-stock and this page agree). **Show the working** in each row (counted X on <date>, used ~Y since, received Z, need W for the period + S safety) so nobody has to trust a bare number, flag items **never counted** rather than guessing, and flag a count older than a few weeks as unreliable. A CSV / printable list of just the items to buy, grouped by supplier (the receipts' `supplier_contact_id` gives the usual supplier), is the thing someone takes to the vet wholesaler. **Cover food too (Lutan, 2026-09-28):** `diet_types` carry the same stock columns, counts and receipts, so the page covers every diet as well as every medicine — a Medicines / Food switch or two sections. **Special diets matter most**, so list them before the standard diet (the standard-diet flag from the Facility diet item tells them apart) and make the safety stock available on `diet_types` too. Diet usage comes from the residents on each diet (the diet forecast the Diets page already shows), not prescriptions. **Schema first:** `safety_stock` on both `medication` and `diet_types` (and pack size, if wanted) as a small `-schema` PR. Home: Management (or Shelter Operations if the Settings/Management review moves stock there). Manual topic en/th; a releases line. **Schema half done 2026-10-02 as `claude/schema-purchasing` (0128; see `docs/decisions/2026-10-02-safety-stock-schema.md`) — the feature half builds against this:** `safety_stock numeric` (nullable, `>= 0`, null = none; zero is a real value, distinct from null) on **both** `medication` and `diet_types`, stored in the item's **base unit** (`dose_unit` / `unit`) like `stock_on_hand`, counts and receipts. The form may take it in the purchase unit but must convert to base on save, as deliveries do. **No unit column and no pack-size column:** the pack is the item's purchase unit in `item_unit_conversions` (0118), so round up to its `base_units_per`. Nothing reads the column yet; write access is whoever already edits those tables. The item stays open for the page, the forms and the shared expected-stock helper.

- [x] **Saving a Shelter Friend does not publish it, and nothing says so.** Found 2026-09-24 on production, and it cost a round of "the release did not deploy properly" before the cause was clear. Making a Shelter Friend is two steps — **Save** the details, then **Publish** — implemented as two separate actions (`updateFriend` and `setFriendPublished` in `src/app/management/shelter-friends/actions.ts`). After Save the profile is a draft: `published` stays `false`, `public_shelter_friends` correctly filters it out (the view is `where sf.published and c.archived_at is null`, 0076), and so the public `/friends` page shows its empty state, the nav entry stays hidden and the home-page thank-you strip does not appear. All of that is correct behaviour, and from the outside it is indistinguishable from the feature being broken or not deployed. The card gives no indication after saving that the profile is still a draft. Options, cheapest first: a line on the card after Save — "Saved as a draft. Publish to show this on the website." — or a visible Draft badge on an unpublished profile, or a prompt on Save offering to publish straight away. Worth doing before anyone other than Lutan uses the feature, because the failure mode is silent: nothing errors, nothing is missing, the page simply looks empty. Related: the public page's empty state ("We're just getting started on thanking the businesses that help us") is written for a visitor and reads as intentional, which is right for the public but gives staff no hint that their own unpublished draft is the reason they cannot see it.

- [x] **Base the vet forecast on recent visit frequency, not a flat per-visit estimate.** Asked for by Lutan 2026-09-23 while testing PR #60: "can we set it to look at an average rolling number of visits recorded per week in the last quarter x the cost per vet visit, or number booked for that week if it's more." Today the vet line is a flat typical-visit estimate edited on `/admin/website` — it does not know how often the shelter actually goes. The proposed rule is, per week, `max(rolling average visits/week over the last quarter, visits actually booked that week) x cost per visit`, so a quiet week still carries the historical rate and a busy one is not understated. Decisions to make before building: (a) the page forecasts by **month**, so either the weekly figure is aggregated up or the rule is restated monthly; (b) whether "cost per vet visit" stays the flat estimate or becomes the mean of actual `vet_appointments.cost` over the same quarter, which would make the whole line self-maintaining; (c) what a booked visit with a **known** cost does — it should surely use its own cost rather than the estimate, which means the rule is really `max(estimated visits, booked visits)` for the *count* and actual cost where known; (d) the empty case, where a shelter with no history gets an average of zero and the line silently reads nothing rather than "unknown". Note this interacts with the defect PR #60 already fixed, where `coalesce(va.cost, estimate)` over a LEFT JOIN charged the estimate to months with no visits at all — any frequency-based rule needs the same care about distinguishing "no visits" from "no data". **Looked at 2026-09-24 and left as the flat figure on Lutan's call:** dev held 71 completed visits, none with a `cost`, and 20 in the last quarter (about 1.5 a week) — so the frequency half has data but the cost half does not, and the change needs a migration while 0073 was in flight. See `docs/decisions.md` (2026-09-24). The dev query and the proposed rule are recorded there, so this is ready to pick up once invoices are being recorded.

- [ ] **Machine-drafted translations: worker built; Lutan's deploy, the managers' model choice, then a machine-tier schema PR are left.** **STATUS 2026-10-21:** Left: Lutan deploys and confirms Workers AI; two bilingual managers compare models; then the schema PR. Shape: a Cloudflare Worker on a cron trigger in the same account the app deploys to (Workers AI binding, so no API key; Llama 3.x / Qwen / M2M100 all cover Thai and the free daily allowance dwarfs shelter volume), polling `translations where status = 'pending'` through Supabase REST with the service key as a Wrangler secret, writing back `text`, `engine` and `status = 'draft'`; a translate() function with one implementation per engine so a local Ollama box can replace it if one appears. Prompts differ by tier ("translate this adoption bio naturally; keep breed names" vs "translate this clinical note literally; keep drug names, doses, units and dates as written"). Then add the internal tier to `translatable_fields` (weight / vet-visit / prescription / intake notes, cause of death, behaviour notes) and attach the queueing trigger to those tables — shown to staff as a labelled machine translation under the original with **no** review step (the Weight tab finding from 2026-09-20). Before building, run twenty real bios and twenty real vet notes through two candidate models and let the two bilingual managers pick. Backfill in batches so the managers get ~20 Tier A drafts a day, not three hundred on Monday. **Status 2026-10-04: the worker is in, the item stays open** (`claude/translations-worker`, decisions `2026-10-04-translations-worker.md`): a cron on the existing Worker drafts pending rows through an engine seam (Workers AI, M2M100, or Ollama), `draft` only, with three-strike failure handling, a batch size and a 20-a-day reviewed-tier cap, no migration. **Still to do:** Lutan deploys to test and production and confirms Workers AI is on for the account (test plan, Left for manual verification); the two bilingual managers compare models on twenty real bios and twenty real vet notes (`TRANSLATE_MODEL` / `TRANSLATE_ENGINE`, drafts carry the model in `translations.engine`); then the schema PR that adds the `machine` tier fields and triggers.

- [x] **Fixed monthly outgoings in the cashflow forecast (salaries, rent and the like), as settings, not payroll.** Lutan, 2026-09-29, replacing the 2026-09-23 "Salaries: pay the people" item. **Payroll is out of scope for good:** no employee records, pay rates, pay periods, payslips or payment history, because per-person pay is the most sensitive data the app could hold, and the privacy risk grows again if the app ever serves several shelters. What the forecast does need is the shelter's regular fixed costs. So: a short list of **named fixed outgoings** managed by management/admin (e.g. "Salaries", "Rent", "Electricity", "Internet"): a label, a monthly amount in baht (`numeric(12,2)`, shown through `formatBaht`), an optional note, and an active flag. **Salaries is one total line** for the whole staff, never broken down by person. Nothing in it identifies anyone. **Where it lives:** a small table (schema PR first), readable and writable by admin and management only, with no anon or staff access (add it to `check-public-views.mjs`'s refusal checks). Not columns on `site_content`, whose `select using (true)` makes every column world-readable. Edited on a page under Management or Settings (whichever the Management/Settings split item settles; Management → Cashflow is the natural home). **Forecast:** `cashflow_forecast` gains one category per active outgoing, or one "Fixed outgoings" category with the lines as its breakdown. Either way it counts each active amount once per month in the window with `basis = 'priced'`, and the page's "no salaries" sentence comes off. Decide while building: a month that is only partly inside the window (pro-rata, or whole months only, matching how the page already groups by month), and whether an amount can change from a date (a start/end month per line is enough; no history table). Manual (Cashflow topic), both dictionaries, a releases line and a `docs/decisions.md` entry recording that payroll was deliberately dropped, and why. **Schema half done 2026-09-29 (0114, see `docs/decisions/2026-09-29-fixed-outgoings-not-payroll.md`):** `fixed_outgoings` (`label`, `monthly_amount numeric(12,2)`, `note`, `active`, plus optional `starts_on` / `ends_on` as the 1st of a month, `ends_on` inclusive, so a change of amount is one line ended and one started, no history table). Admin and management only via RLS, anon grants revoked, capped at 24 lines so it cannot hold one row per person; `check-public-views.mjs` refuses anon. **Feature half done 2026-09-29:** edit page at Management → Cashflow → Fixed outgoings, forecast category "Fixed outgoings" counted pro-rata by the day, manual, dictionaries and releases line (see `docs/decisions/2026-09-29-fixed-outgoings-in-the-forecast.md`).

(2) **Cumulative view, a line chart over the same 12 months:** **adoptions** and **deaths** as running totals from the first month shown (month 1's figure, then month 1 + 2, and so on); **intakes** the same, unless Lutan says to leave intakes out of this view; and a **residents in care** line. Recommended reading: **each month's point is the average number of residents in care during that month** (count on site each day from `placement_history`, shelter dates, then the month's mean; a resident in foster or hospital counts as in care, adopted and deceased do not; say which in the chart's note), which is honest about a month where many arrived and left. The residents line keeps its own scale, as before. *Done on claude/dashboard-cumulative-chart: hospital counts, intakes are in the view, cross-check found one Foster placement filed under the Unassigned enclosure (docs/decisions/2026-10-18-cumulative-trend-chart.md).*

It understates rather than overstates, which is the safe direction, but a window longer than the shortest interval is wrong by construction and worth fixing if anyone forecasts a year. (f) **Salaries, rent and other fixed costs** are excluded only because nothing holds them; the "Fixed monthly outgoings" item above adds them as named monthly amounts (one total line for salaries, no payroll) and takes the "no salaries" sentence off the page when it lands. **SORTED 2026-10-09 (`dashboard-cashflow-followups`; see `docs/decisions/2026-10-09-dashboard-and-cashflow-follow-ups-sorted.md`).** (f) **done** before this stream — `fixed_outgoings` (0114) and *Edit fixed outgoings*. (d) **decided: the split is permanent** — 7/30 columns suit stock, 30/90 suits money; recorded in the decision. (e) **spun out** to its own schema item, *Cashflow forecast function: second doses and Thai-time months*, together with the function's UTC month bucketing. **Still open: (a) forecast against actuals** (needs months of history, and a snapshot table to keep each month's forecast) **and (b) a per-clinic or per-reason average** for `site_content.clinic_visit_estimate` (renamed by 0172; on dev, 1 of September's 6 visits had a cost) — both wait on real data.

- [x] **Recurring jobs: only offer people who can actually do the job.** Lutan, 2026-09-27, Pass 1 (Vet) of the role walkthrough. **Done 2026-09-27** (`claude/recurring-jobs-eligible-assignees`): vets are never assignable (Lutan: their work comes from vet appointments), and otherwise who can do a job is derived from its link path in `src/lib/recurring-jobs/eligibility.ts`, borrowing each page's own role predicate; the picker filters by it as the link changes, save and Hand over refuse anyone it excludes, and a job already with such a person is flagged on Management → Recurring jobs and loses its link on their My tasks. No migration. Pass 0 assigned a stocktake to a vet, because the assignee picker offers every user regardless of role. Pass 1 then tapped it and was thrown out of the app — the job's link goes to `/stocktake`, which vets cannot open. The job was impossible from the moment it was assigned, and nothing said so at the point where it could have been prevented. **Filter the assignee list by what the job's target screen needs**: a stocktake job offers only the roles `canStocktake` allows (admin, management, staff, volunteer); a maintenance job only those who can write maintenance; and so on. That means a recurring job has to know which capability it needs — today it knows a link, not a permission — so part of this is deciding how that is expressed (a capability on the job type, or derived from its target path). **Also handle the ones already assigned**, since a filter on the form does not fix a job created before it: either validate on save and on display, or show an assignee who can no longer do it as a problem on the Management page rather than leaving it to fail in someone's face. The bounce itself is the public-website item under Quick wins; this is the half that stops the situation arising.

Code that saves 4 places into a 2-place column would round silently, which is why it waits. **STATUS 2026-10-08 (`claude/medications-diets-split`): most of the code half done.** `costPerBaseUnit` rounds to 4 places (still refuses only a price that 4 places cannot hold, e.g. 1 baht for 100 kg); the Medication stock and Diet stock cost inputs take 4 places (`parseUnitCost`) and show up to 4 (`formatUnitCost`, ฿0.0567 per g); the Units panel shows the per-base price to 4 places. **Left open:** the per-gram price *display* beside the pack price (batch 73), and the production order — **0161 must be on production before this release**, or 4-place prices save rounded to 2 there.
- [x] **Impact figures as a baseline plus a live count: enter a starting number and a date in Settings, and let the system add to it from then on (schema first).** **DECIDED 2026-10-07 (the Director and Lutan, decision brief q10):** asked for this instead of the brief's three options — *"can we have an option to add the baseline number in settings somewhere, then system calculates from that date onwards"*. **This is the right answer and it solves the general problem**, not just the website band: the shelter existed before the app, so every lifetime total is *a number nobody recorded* + *what the app has seen since*. **Shape:** a small table (one row per figure: key, label, label_th, baseline count, baseline date, who set it, when) edited on **Settings → Website** beside the other public-site fields; the public figure is **baseline + rows since baseline date**, computed, never stored. **Schema PR first**, as usual. **Which figures it serves on day one:** *animals rehomed* (adoptions in `placement_history` since the date, plus the baseline for everything before the app) and *sterilisations in local villages* **if** a project or a count field records them — check, and if nothing does, that figure is baseline-only until the item below exists. **Three things to get right:** (1) **say it is approximate where it is** — a hand-entered baseline is an estimate and the page should not imply a precise audit; (2) **both dictionaries**, since the labels are public; (3) **do not let a baseline be edited casually** — it changes a public claim, so Settings → Website is the right home and the change should be in the audit log. Replaces the "decide the source of each" half of the Impact band item. **Status 2026-10-07: schema half done (0156 `impact_baselines` + `public_impact_figures`, `claude/baseline-impact-schema`); app half open: Settings → Website editor, the "approximate" wording, both dictionaries (batch 64). Nothing records village sterilisations, so that figure is baseline-only. On dev only Admin holds `website.content`; Management needs the cell for the item's "→ Management" to be true.** **Status 2026-10-07 (later): app half done too** — Settings → Website → Home page editor, "About" wording on the band, both dictionaries, audit via the table trigger (`claude/baseline-impact-figures`). Admin-only until the Director rules on Management holding `website.content`. → *Management*

## Assistant

- [x] **Assistant demo: show it to the Director and record what they said.** The sketch is built and merged (2026-09-22): `/assistant` in the left nav with a *demo* badge, admin/management/staff, keyword parser in `src/lib/assistant/demo-parser.ts`, writes via the real move helper and vet-visit RPC after a preview card — see `docs/decisions.md` (2026-09-22, "hard-codes the understanding, not the doing") for what was deliberately left out of the sketch (slide-over, `dryRun`, env flag, audit table). **What remains:** walk the Director through "move Panda to B1" and "book a vet visit for Panda tomorrow 10am", then record what they said in `docs/decisions.md` and let that steer the full assistant item below. Original brief, kept for the real build — raised 2026-09-22: No LLM, no API key: a chat panel whose "brain" is a small keyword matcher that recognises two requests and walks each through the real flow — (1) "move <resident> to <enclosure>" and (2) "book a vet visit for <resident>" — everything else gets a polite "I can only help with moves and vet visits in this demo." **Build the reusable parts properly, hard-code only the brain:** `src/components/assistant/AssistantPanel.tsx` (slide-over from a header button, message list, input, typing indicator, works on the phone), `src/lib/assistant/types.ts` (the message / tool-call / request-details / confirm-card shapes the real assistant will use), `PreviewCard` ("Move Panda (R-0042) from A3 → B1 today" with Confirm / Change / Cancel) and `RequestDetailsModal` (a small form built from a field spec — used when the resident name is ambiguous or the enclosure / vet / date is missing). The scripted brain lives in `src/lib/assistant/demo-brain.ts` behind the same `respond(messages) → AssistantTurn` interface the LLM adapter will implement later, so swapping it out is one import. **It should do real work:** resident and enclosure lookups hit `resident_list_view` / enclosures for real (so the Director can try it on Panda), the move preview calls `src/lib/placements/move.ts` with `dryRun` and, on Confirm, for real; the vet visit preview pre-fills date / vet / reason and on Confirm inserts the `vet_appointments` row the same way `/vet-visits/new` does. Both paths reuse the existing capacity warning and the existing confirm wording, and the resulting rows carry a "via assistant (demo)" note. **Guard rails:** behind a `NEXT_PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_DEMO=1` env flag so it is on for the customer showing and off otherwise; admin/management/staff only; English and Thai trigger phrases (a handful of each — the matcher is a list of regexes, not NLP). **Not in scope:** anything the two scripts don't cover, memory between messages, streaming. Afterwards, record what the customer said in `docs/decisions.md` and let that steer the full item.

Original: Raised 2026-09-24 when the doctor-name feature shipped: `/vet-visits/new` and Edit take an optional doctor (`vet_appointments.doctor_name`, 0074), but the assistant's vet intent (`src/lib/assistant/intents/vet.ts`) strips "dr", "dr." and "doctor" as `VET_STOPWORDS` when matching the vet, so "book a vet visit for Panda with Dr Somchai" books the visit and drops the name. Accept it, but don't ask for it: parse a trailing "with Dr X" / "หมอ X" into the draft, show it on the preview card as an editable, optional field, and write it the way `bookVetVisit` does (see `docs/decisions.md`, 2026-09-24). If a schema PR touches vet visits first, fold a `p_doctor_name` parameter into `schedule_bulk_appointments` then, so both callers write the doctor in the RPC's own transaction.
- [x] **A volunteer turned away from an assistant write leaves no audit row.** Noticed building batch 1 (2026-09-23). Volunteers get the read-only lookups; if one types a write request the browser answers "that one is for staff and management" and nothing reaches the server, so `assistant_actions` (0070) never sees it. Those are worth having — they say what the people with the least access actually want the assistant to do, which is exactly what should steer whether volunteers get more of it. The status enum is created in `0070_assistant_actions.sql` as `('confirmed','cancelled','unmatched')` and none of them is true of a refusal, so a `refused` value has to be added before the client can record it. **Schema half in PR (2026-10-02, branch `claude/schema-assistant-refused`): `0130_assistant_action_refused.sql` adds `refused` to the enum.** It is one file, not two — the two-file rule (`docs/decisions.md`, PR #50) is `add value` plus a *use* of it in SQL, and nothing in SQL uses it (no check, view, function or policy reads `status`). Still to do, as its own feature branch from `main` once 0130 is applied: the client records a refusal — add `"refused"` to `AssistantActionStatus` in `src/lib/assistant/audit.ts` and have `AssistantConversation.tsx` send a row when it turns a volunteer away. (The old constraint that `claude/cashflow-schema` held the single migration slot is long gone; that branch merged.) Small, and not urgent — but the longer it waits the bigger the hole in the corpus. **Update 2026-10-06 (`perm-convert-settings`, `0150`):** the table policies now ask `assistant.record` on the caller's own row, so this is a one-policy change: insert asks `assistant.record` **or** (`assistant.ask`, `status = 'refused'`, own row). The volunteer holds `assistant.ask` and not `record`, so it is refused today. It widens who can write the table, so it is the item's own decision. **Update 2026-10-09 (`grants-lint-and-refused-row`):** confirmed still blocked — the only insert policies are `assistant_actions_insert_perm` (`assistant.record`, own row; 0150) and `assistant_actions_admin_all` (0153), and `logAssistantAction` writes under the caller's session, so a volunteer's row would be refused. The two-file client change was **not** built, so nothing half-done is on `main`. Lutan chose to leave it open: **next step is his yes on the policy widening**, then fold it into whichever schema PR is next, then the client change. **2026-10-10: Lutan's assistant answer reads as a yes.** He asked for a log of requests the assistant could not help with (see the DB-11 retention item), and a volunteer's refused write is exactly that. Treat the policy widening as approved in principle, confirm it in one line when the build is planned, and fold it into the same schema PR as the 2-day delete. **Update 2026-10-16 (`public-stories-schema`, `0214`): the policy half landed.** `assistant_actions_insert_perm` now also allows `assistant.ask` + `status = 'refused'` + own row; the volunteer still reads nothing. **Done 2026-10-17 (`claude/assistant-refused-row`, #686): the client.** The policy came from `0214` (#683), the client from this PR: `AssistantConversation.tsx` calls the new `recordRefusedTurn` server action when it turns a volunteer away, a bare fire-and-forget insert of the typed text only (no intent, no draft). Verified as a throwaway volunteer on dev. The retention period for this corpus (DB-11) and who may read other people's rows are unchanged and still open.
- [x] **`fetchAssistantContext()` has no role check of its own.** Noticed 2026-09-25 building `assistant-nav-link`. The server action in `src/app/assistant/actions.ts` calls `loadAssistantContext()` for whoever asks, so a vet — who has no Assistant button and whose `/assistant` page shows only "can't use the assistant" — can still call it directly and get the resident list, vets and enclosure options, limited only by RLS. Writes and lookups each re-check the role; this one does not. Return an empty context with `notAuthorized` unless `canUseAssistant(role)`, the way `lookups.ts` does, and check whether `page.tsx` should skip loading for the same roles.
- [x] **DONE 2026-10-30 (branch `claude/assistant-could-not-help-log`, `docs/decisions/2026-10-30-assistant-could-not-help-log.md`): all four deliverables shipped — `/admin/assistant` screen, CSV eval export, the could-not-help line on `/admin/status`, and the `assistant-could-not-help` production check. Version 2's prerequisite is discharged.** (Original item follows.) **NOTHING CAN READ THE ASSISTANT'S COULD-NOT-HELP LOG: IT IS COLLECTED, KEPT 90 DAYS, AND HAS NO WAY OUT. An admin screen and an export. Buildable now, app only, no schema.** **Asked by Lutan 2026-10-30, in chat:** *"where can admin view the logs?"* and *"how do I train the model for items that it couldn't answer"*. **Measured the same day, and the answer to both is: you cannot.** `assistant_actions` rows with status `unmatched` or `refused` are the could-not-help log and are kept **90 days** on purpose, against 2 days for everything else (`docs/decisions/2026-10-19-assistant-retention.md`, `0227`). They are written by `logAssistantAction()` (`src/lib/assistant/audit.ts`, statuses `confirmed` / `cancelled` / `unmatched` / `refused` from `0070`) and **read by nothing**: `grep -rln assistant_actions src/` returns only `src/lib/assistant/audit.ts`, `src/lib/assistant/types.ts` and `src/lib/status/usage.ts`, and the last of those only **counts all requests over N days** for `/admin/status` (`countAssistantRequests`, `usage.ts:91`, called at `usage.ts:201`) — it does not list rows and does not split by status. **No page, no route, no export, and no eval set exists anywhere in the repo.** **WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE:** the 90-day retention was chosen *so that this material would be there to use*, and version 2's whole hosting plan is to *"record every real exchange into an eval set that the self-hosted model is then measured against and, if needed, fine-tuned on"*. **That eval set is the thing the model swap is measured against, and today there is no way to build it.** So this is a PREREQUISITE for version 2's model swap and should land before the big version-2 build, not after. **DO:** (1) an Admin-only screen listing the could-not-help rows — what was typed, when, which status, and the resident or record it was about where one was inferred — newest first, filterable by status and date; (2) an export of the same rows in a shape that can become an eval set (one row per exchange: what was typed, what the assistant did or refused, and room for the correct answer to be written in); (3) a line on `/admin/status` splitting the count by status, so an admin can see the could-not-help number without opening the screen; (4) **an `assistant-could-not-help` check in `scripts/check-production.mjs`**, which today has no assistant check at all — so **the planner cannot answer *"what has it failed to answer?"* from the main checkout, which is the only place production can be read.** Ids, dates, statuses and what was typed; no names, in keeping with the other checks there. Lutan asked exactly that question on 2026-10-30 and it could not be answered without writing new code, which is why this is a deliverable and not a nicety. **NO CARD, and this is deliberate:** Lutan, 2026-10-19, *"Only admin should be able to read assistant rows"*, and the live policies already say so (`assistant_actions_admin_all`, `0153`; `assistant_actions_select_perm`, `0150`, own rows only — Management lost read-everything in `0150` and is not given it back). Admin sits outside the card system, so this screen needs no card and **must not be given one**, exactly as `reference.types` needs none. **Do not add a read policy for anyone else without asking him.** **No schema:** the rows, the statuses and the policies all exist. Manual topic, both dictionaries, a decision file. → *Assistant*

- [ ] **IN-APP CHAT ASSISTANT THAT DOES THINGS (LLM VERSION 2): SIZED 2026-10-30 INTO SEVEN STREAMS (the seven items below, plan in `docs/decisions/2026-10-30-assistant-v2-scoping.md`); this item is the umbrella and closes when stream 7 does. Not started. Nothing needs Lutan before stream 1.** SUPERSEDED 2026-10-30, the old title: *NOTHING LEFT TO DECIDE, buildable now; not started, and LARGE — size it before briefing anyone.* Also superseded by that file: the item's "new `assistant_actions` table" (it exists, 0070) and "admin/management/staff only" (it is the `assistant.ask` / `assistant.record` cards). **ANSWERED 2026-10-30 (Lutan, in chat), and the third was never open:** (1) **low-risk changes MAY skip the confirmation** — *"Yes low risk transactions can skip the confirmation"*; the build decides what counts as low risk from the activity the change asks, never from a role. (2) **Accuracy: *"needs to be high before it replaces Claude"*. There is deliberately NO NUMBER, and none is needed to start** — the item's own plan is to build against the Claude API first and record every real exchange into an eval set, so **the bar is set from that eval set at swap time, not now.** Do not put a figure to him before the eval set exists, and do not treat its absence as a blocker. (3) **HOW LONG CONVERSATIONS ARE KEPT WAS ALREADY DECIDED AND SHIPPED — THIS QUESTION MUST NEVER BE ASKED AGAIN.** Lutan, 2026-10-30: *"We already have a rule for length of time conversations are kept"*, and he is right: **2 days, 90 for the could-not-help log (DB-11)**, `docs/decisions/2026-10-19-assistant-retention.md`, proved by `scripts/check-assistant-retention.mjs`. **He has now been asked this FOUR times** — `CLAUDE.md` names the first three under *Answering a decision on a backlog item*, and the fourth happened because THIS ITEM'S TITLE still said *"three questions for Lutan first"* eleven days after the rule shipped. **That is the exact fault that rule exists to stop, and the title is why.** SUPERSEDED 2026-10-30, the old title: *In-app chat assistant that does things (LLM version 2): not started; three questions for Lutan first.* **STATUS 2026-10-21:** Before building, Lutan decides: may low-risk logs skip the confirm, what accuracy bar a self-hosted model must reach, and how long conversations are kept. Raised 2026-09-22: the Director's biggest pain point is time, and the ask is an experience like working with Claude here — type "move Panda from A3 to B1" or "Bella died last night, lung problems" and the system makes the changes, popping a modal only when it needs something it can't infer. **Hosting (user's direction 2026-09-22):** the production assistant should run on an LLM the shelter hosts itself — on the Raspberry Pi 5 at home or a cloud box — not on a metered Claude subscription. Claude is for the prototype and for teaching: build against the Claude API first because it gets tool use right with the least effort, and while doing so record every real exchange (request, tool calls, corrections) into an eval set that the self-hosted model is then measured against and, if needed, fine-tuned on. To keep that swap possible the model layer must be **provider-neutral from the first commit**: one `src/lib/assistant/llm.ts` adapter that takes messages + tool definitions and returns text / tool calls, with a Claude implementation (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `claude-opus-5`, streaming, adaptive thinking; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as a Cloudflare secret) and an OpenAI-compatible implementation for whatever the shelter hosts (Ollama / llama.cpp / vLLM all speak that shape), selected by env var. Nothing outside the adapter may import a vendor SDK. **Honest sizing note for the Pi:** a Pi 5 with 8–16 GB runs a 3–8B quantised model at a few tokens/second; that is workable for a short reply but tool-calling accuracy in mixed Thai/English at that size is marginal and each turn will take tens of seconds. Expect the self-hosted target to be a small cloud GPU (or a hosted open-weight endpoint) and treat the Pi as the stretch goal — measure both against the eval set before deciding. **Shape:** a chat panel (slide-over from a header button, also a full page `/assistant`; works on the phone) that sends the conversation to a route handler which calls the adapter with a **fixed toolset that wraps the app's existing server-side operations** — never raw SQL. First tools: find resident (by name/Thai name/code, returning candidates), find enclosure, move resident (`src/lib/placements/move.ts`), send to / return from hospital (`hospital.ts`), record death (`deceased.ts`, with cause), foster/adopt/return (`rehome.ts`), log weight, log vet visit, log immunization, add prescription, and read-only lookups (resident hub summary, who is in an enclosure, what's due). Each tool runs under the caller's own Supabase session, so RLS and the role checks apply exactly as in the UI and the assistant can never do more than the person could by clicking. **Confirmation:** every write is a two-step — the model calls the tool with `dryRun: true`, the UI shows a preview card ("Move Panda (R-0042) from A3 → B1 today, no notes") with Confirm / Change / Cancel, and only a Confirm re-invokes the tool for real; irreversible ones (death) use the existing `ConfirmDialog` wording. This matters doubly for a smaller self-hosted model: the confirm step is what makes a mis-parsed request harmless. **Missing information:** a `request_details` tool the model calls when a required field is unknown (which of two residents named Panda; date of death when "last night" is ambiguous across midnight; the enclosure when only a zone was named) that renders a small modal form built from the tool's field spec; the answers go back as the tool result. **Ambiguity:** resident lookup always returns candidates with code, enclosure and photo so the model can ask "the Panda in A3 or the one in Foster?" instead of guessing. **Audit:** log each assistant conversation and every executed tool call (who, when, input, result, which model served it) to a new `assistant_actions` table, and stamp the resulting rows' notes with "via assistant" so the hub history shows it — this table doubles as the eval/training corpus. **Scope of first cut:** the placement and medical tools above, English + Thai input, admin/management/staff only (volunteers get read-only tools), no memory across conversations, Claude behind the adapter. **Second cut:** stand up the self-hosted model, run the eval set, switch the env var when it clears the bar. **Later:** voice input on the phone, "what happened this week" summaries from the management dashboard queries, drafting the Facebook post for a project. **Decide with the user before building:** whether low-risk logs (weight, immunization) may skip the confirm to keep it fast; the accuracy bar the self-hosted model must reach on the eval set before it replaces Claude; whether conversations are retained beyond the audit rows. **DECIDED BY LUTAN 2026-10-30, AND IT CHANGES THE PLAN: SELF-HOSTED FROM THE START. There is NO Claude proof of concept and NO Anthropic API key is being bought.** His words, asked whether the free self-hosted solution was still the goal and then told what a prototype would cost: *"Let's not do the proof of concept, I'd prefer to look at the options we have to get this onto a self hosted model."* **This CONFIRMS the item's own hosting direction of 2026-09-22 and cancels only the staging** — "build against the Claude API first" is superseded; everything the item says about self-hosting, the eval set and the adapter stands. **What this does NOT cost us, because the question will be asked:** the eval set never depended on Claude — it is the could-not-help log (#1106), real sentences from real staff, labelled by hand in the exported CSV. **What it DOES cost:** Claude gets tool use right with little effort and a small model does not, so expect malformed tool calls, invented field names and wrong actions — that work moves into streams 3, 4 and 5 as strict schemas, input validation and retries, and those three need re-banding upward. **The development machine (established 2026-10-30): Lutan's spare laptop — i7, 16 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD, INTEGRATED GRAPHICS, no discrete GPU.** 256 GB is ample (a 4-bit model file is 3–9 GB) and ~12 GB of usable RAM reaches a 7–8B model comfortably or a 13–14B at a squeeze. **It is a BUILD AND MEASURE box, not the shelter's host:** on a CPU the slow part is reading the prompt before any reply begins, and our prompt carries all nine tool descriptions, so a turn is tens of seconds to over a minute. **Production hosting is deliberately NOT decided** — it is settled later from the eval numbers, and the options then are the laptop with a real GPU, a small cloud GPU (breaks the zero-cost rule), a hosted open-weight endpoint (data leaves the shelter, which was a reason for self-hosting: people type resident names and worries into the box) or the Pi, which the item already calls a stretch goal. **Nothing here is left for him to answer; do not re-ask.**

(a) A conversation remembers an `unavailable` verdict for THREE MINUTES and then asks once more, so a sleeping machine costs one 10.7 s wait and not one per sentence; the number and its reasoning are in `src/lib/assistant/model-wait.ts`, pure and tested, and reloading the page is the retry-sooner path. ## Auth

- [x] **Name card taps under the new permissions: a signed-in person must never see less than a visitor, and what they see beyond that follows their role.** Lutan, 2026-10-07: with permissions now set per role (the roles build), does tapping a resident's name card still work? The intended rule: **signed in → the resident's page with medical; anonymous → the resident with general information only.** **What happens today (checked in the code, 2026-10-07):** `/r/<code>` (`src/app/r/[code]/page.tsx`) shows the **public card** to anyone signed out or signed in without app access (`public_viewer`), which is right. Anyone with app access is sent to `/residents/<id>`, and that page now depends on the role: (a) **Admin, Management, Staff:** the full page with medical. Right. (b) **The 2IC, Head of Medical, Head of Maintenance and volunteers:** these roles borrow `volunteer` underneath (`legacy_role`, `0136`, `0141`, `0143`), and a role without `resident.record` gets **`ResidentWhoAndWhere`** (`0134`): who the resident is and where it lives, **no medical, and less than the public card shows a stranger** (no bio, temperament, age or adoption details). So for them a tap is *worse* than not being signed in. (c) **A vet or doctor login:** the page is limited to residents their clinics treat (`0108`), so a card for any other resident gives **404**, where a visitor would have seen the public card. **The fix:** (1) **Never less than the public card.** When a signed-in person may not open the full record, `/r/<code>` shows them the public card's information (the same `public_resident_cards` view anyone could read) plus whatever their role adds, instead of the who-and-where page or a 404. The same rule on `/residents/<id>` itself. - [x] **`/manual/pdf` on the Node origin fetches its screenshots unauthenticated and gets the login redirect.** Found 2026-10-01 while testing the Next 16.3.8 bump (#268), not caused by it. `src/app/manual/pdf/route.ts` `loadImage` falls back to `fetch(origin + src)` when there is no `ASSETS` binding (the Pi runs `next start`); `src/proxy.ts` redirects that request (307) to `/login`, so react-pdf receives HTML and logs `Incomplete or corrupt PNG file` once per image (~195 times for `?view=all`), and the request is slow. The Worker is unaffected. Fix: read the file from `public/` with `fs` when there is no binding, or forward the caller's cookie. Check that the PDF on the Pi actually has its pictures.

- [x] **A release note shipped for a feature whose own decision file said a manual step was outstanding — decide whether §7 may be ticked in that case (process; found 2026-10-10).** **What happened.** #518 (`claude/pi-visitor-count`, `f08b62aa`) fixed a real drift bug — two hand-kept optional-secret lists, so `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID` reached the Worker but not the Pi, which serves the pages — and added this note, tagged `roles: ["admin"]`: *"Settings → System status: the Website visitors tile now shows how many people visited the website, instead of saying Not set up."* **It did not.** The same PR's decision file (`docs/decisions/2026-10-10-one-optional-secrets-list.md`, "Not changed") closes by saying the Pi's copy of `.env.deploy.production` still needs the two lines by hand, and the backlog item still read *"the query has still never run against the live API"*. `0.25.0` was cut the same day, so **the note went out to admins in release mail for a feature that does not work.** Lutan reported it as an urgent bug; being fixed as `visitor-count-live`. **The bug itself is the BUG item in `## Admin`** (*the Website visitors tile still says Not set up…*, `4ed3d331`), being fixed as `visitor-count-live`; **this item is only the process question**, and it exists separately because that item carries its release-time lesson as prose and **that prose is lost the moment the bug is ticked.** **Why the gates did not catch it:** `check-test-plan.mjs` validates that §7 has a **new `unreleased` line**, not that the line is **true** — it cannot read a tile. So the checker is not at fault and **this is not a request to change it**; `continue-on-error` must not come back and the script must not start failing on unsigned plans (CLAUDE.md). **The decision to make:** may §7 be ticked when the same PR's decision file, README or backlog note records a manual step still outstanding? **Recommendation:** no — a note describes what a shelter user can now see, so if a step between the merge and the user seeing it is known to be outstanding, the honest answer is `n/a: <the step that is outstanding>` and the note goes in the PR that closes that step. A one-line rule in CLAUDE.md's testing section would carry it; whether it also becomes a check (grep the decision file for an outstanding-step phrase?) is a second question and probably not worth it. **The wider version, worth considering separately:** every one of the last three releases has had at least one note whose truth depended on a deploy step. → *Architecture*
- [x] **Promote the `test-plan` check from a red flag to a required check.** Requested 2026-09-23 by Lutan, alongside enlisting a test manager: every feature gets a test plan checklist, filled in during verification and signed off before the feature reaches production. The mechanism is built — `docs/test-plan-template.md`, copied per feature to `docs/test-plans/<feature>.md`, plus `scripts/check-test-plan.mjs` and a `test-plan` CI job that fails a PR which does not add or update a *completed* checklist (every line ticked or `n/a: <reason>`, no placeholders left, `Result:` one of three values, `fail` blocks). That is PR #55 — open, CI green, carrying its own completed checklist as the first one through the gate. **The part deliberately not enabled yet:** `test-plan` is not a required check in branch protection on `main`, so it reports red and the PR merges anyway. That is a GitHub settings change on the repo (Settings → Branches → `main` → require `CI` *and* `test-plan`). **No exemptions, including schema-only PRs** — ruled 2026-09-23: an exemption was granted and then reversed within minutes, on the grounds that a checklist which is mostly `n/a: no UI surface, no code reads these columns yet` costs about a minute and is exactly the record you want when that migration later turns out to matter. If it is ever revisited, derive the exemption from the diff (the PR touches nothing outside `supabase/migrations/`) rather than from a label: a label is a manual click that can land on a PR which is not schema-only, so it has to be verified against the file list anyway, at which point the file list is doing the work and the label only adds a way to get it wrong. Note also that the gate sits before merge, not before deploy — `main` moves several times a day (four merges on 2026-09-23 alone), so untested work accumulating on `main` would make every release all-or-nothing. Keep a thin release-time smoke list as well (sign in, residents list, one resident hub, `/adopt` signed out), because a per-feature gate cannot catch two features interacting badly. Everything merged up to `f32f2c1` (#51–#54) is the agreed baseline and is exempt; testing starts from the next feature. **Staged deliberately, 2026-09-23:** Lutan's call is to run `test-plan` as a red flag first and promote it to a required check once the process has visibly bedded in — "see how we go, and if it is working smoothly then we can change to a hard block". So red-without-blocking is a planned first stage, not an oversight, and this item is the scheduled revisit rather than a defect. The reasoning (a soft gate people follow beats a hard gate they resent, and nothing is live until the Pi lands) is recorded in `docs/decisions.md` on PR #55. **DECIDED 2026-10-19 by Lutan: stays advisory, not required. Evidence: of the last 112 PR CI runs test-plan went red 16 times (the most common red) and every one was fixed before merge; all 50 latest merged PRs ended green. Requiring it would add friction for no gain; the release-time check covers the gap. Do not reopen without new evidence of a PR reaching main with a bad plan.**

- [x] **`check-test-plan.mjs` can't tell a post-merge sign-off PR from a feature PR that forgot its release line.** Raised 2026-09-24 on PR #80. #77 (intake capacity warning) merged with its plan complete apart from a real-phone check; the phone pass was then recorded in a follow-up PR from the same branch that touched only `docs/test-plans/intake-capacity-warning.md`. The checker reads the plan's **Release notes.** line against *that PR's* diff, and a ticked line with no new `unreleased` entry fails ("gained no line in this PR"), even though #77 had added it. The workaround was to reword the line as `n/a: in this follow-up PR … went into unreleased with #77` — honest, but it rewrites the feature's permanent record to suit a later PR, and every sign-off recorded after merge will hit the same thing. This will be common: section 8's deployed smoke test can only happen after merge, so a manual check moved there (as the phone pass was) is always recorded post-merge. Fix options: (a) when a PR changes only files under `docs/test-plans/`, check the release-notes line against the diff that introduced the plan (`git log --diff-filter=A` on the file, or the first PR that touched it) rather than the current diff; (b) accept a ticked line when `unreleased` — or a cut release — already contains a line the plan quotes; (c) an explicit marker such as `release line: #77` that the checker verifies by looking at that PR's diff. (a) needs no new syntax and is probably the right default. Afterwards, restore #80's line to its ticked wording. Soft gate, so nothing is blocked meanwhile — but a false red on every sign-off PR is exactly what teaches people to ignore a red `test-plan`.

Write the result to `docs/architecture-review-2026-09-22.md` (dated, so later reviews sit beside it) and turn each finding worth acting on into its own backlog item under the matching heading. - [x] **Full security review and cyber threat assessment of the platform.** Requested 2026-09-24 by Lutan. The deliverable is an **assessment report**: `docs/security-review-<date>.md`, dated so later reviews sit beside it. It maps every threat surface, says who could attack each one and how, rates each risk, and proposes mitigations. This is a separate item from the Fable architectural review above. That review ranks security first but covers the whole architecture. This one is only about security, and it asks "who would attack this, and what would they get?" not "is this well built?". Whichever runs second reads the other's report and does not repeat its findings. **Threat surfaces to cover, at minimum:** (a) **the public website and anonymous access**: `/adopt`, `/foster`, `/volunteer`, `/donate`, `/our-work`, `/r`, `/e`, `/privacy`; the anon key that ships in the client bundle by design; every table and view anon can reach through PostgREST, found by listing grants and `pg_policies`, not from `scripts/check-public-views.mjs`'s four-view allowlist (note `site_content`'s unqualified `using (true)`: every column of it is world-readable); and spam and abuse on any public form; (b) **authentication and sessions**: Google OAuth (`src/app/auth/callback`), email/password with temporary passwords and `must_change_password` in `app_metadata`, the access-request queue (a stranger's Google sign-in leaves an auth row), archived users, the `src/proxy.ts` guards, `bootstrap-admin.mjs`, whether the pages under `/admin` and `/management` each check the role or rely on the nav hiding them, and MFA for admins (since 2026-09-27 Settings → Security and its actions require `aal2` — an authenticator-app step-up; review the step-up page `/admin/security/verify`, the per-action check in `src/app/admin/security/actions.ts`, the reset routes including `bootstrap-admin.mjs --reset-2step`, that a reset reaches an open session only at its next refresh, and that nothing else asks for 2-step; `docs/decisions.md` 2026-09-27); (c) **authorization and RLS**: role escalation (can a volunteer write `user_roles`?), `security definer` functions and triggers (0024, 0026 and later), write paths for each role, and service-role use in server actions; (d) **file handling**: the attachment and photo routes under `src/app/api/*` (upload type and size limits, who may read a `photos/[fileId]`, whether a Drive file ID can be guessed or enumerated) and the Google Drive service credentials, including what those credentials can reach beyond the shelter's folders; (e) **the assistant** (`/assistant`, `assistant_actions` 0070): prompt injection through resident notes, contact records or uploaded documents; what the assistant can read and write as the signed-in user; and whether its actions need confirmation; (f) **infrastructure and deployment**: the Cloudflare Worker (`worker/index.mjs`, including the Pi-origin fallback in `fetchFromOrigin`), `wrangler.jsonc`, the secrets in Workers and `.dev.vars`/`.env.local`, the dev/prod split (`test.lannacare.org` vs `lannacare.org`) and whether dev can ever reach prod data, `scripts/deploy.mjs`, the Pi host (`scripts/pi/`, `docs/pi-hosting.md`), security headers (CSP, HSTS, frame-ancestors) and Cloudflare WAF/rate-limit settings; (g) **the supply chain and repo**: npm dependencies (`npm audit`, lockfile integrity), GitHub Actions permissions in `ci.yml`, branch protection, the auto-push hooks, secrets in git history, and the Supabase Management API token that `apply-migrations.mjs` uses (who holds it, what it can do, and the 90-day token whose location is unknown); (h) **data protection and resilience**: what personal data is held (contacts, adopters, volunteers; payroll is deliberately out of scope, 2026-09-29), backups (`scripts/backup.mjs`, `backup-schedule.ps1`: where they go, whether they are encrypted, whether a restore has been tested), ransomware or account-takeover recovery, and PDPA (Thailand) obligations; (i) **people and process**: phishing of staff and admin Google accounts, shared logins, offboarding (archive vs delete), the lannacare.org email routing catch-all as a spoofing and impersonation risk (SPF, DKIM and DMARC on the domain), and how much depends on one developer with many AI sessions (bus factor, and what an AI session is permitted to do). **For each finding:** the surface, a plausible attacker (opportunist or bot, disgruntled ex-volunteer, targeted attacker), likelihood × impact → Critical / High / Medium / Low, evidence (file and line, or the query that showed it), and a concrete mitigation with a rough effort estimate. Also list what is already done well, so nobody "fixes" it. Open with a one-page executive summary and a top-5 list that a non-developer (the Director) can read. **Rules of engagement:** read-only, plus hands-on testing **against dev / `test.lannacare.org` only**, never production (production reads are off-limits from sessions). Use the anon key and a test token for each role to confirm what RLS actually allows, not what the policies appear to say. Do not load-test or fuzz Cloudflare. Do not write out real secrets in the report: name where a secret lives, never its value. **Afterwards:** turn every Critical/High finding into its own backlog item (on the `backlog` branch), note Medium/Low in the report only, and add a `docs/decisions.md` entry on any risk that is deliberately accepted. The report goes out as its own PR with a test-plan checklist, which is mostly `n/a: documentation only`. **TICKED 2026-10-07 (staleness sweep) — delivered 2026-09-30 under a different filename, and this item was never ticked.** `91c15c23` (#239, 2026-09-30): `docs/security/security-assessment-2026-09-30.pdf` and `.docx` (not `docs/security-review-<date>.md`), with its test plan `docs/test-plans/security-review.md`. It has what this item asks for: threat surfaces across database, code and front end; a severity scale and 33 rated findings (0 Critical, 1 High — the unencrypted backup — 13 Medium, 15 Low, 4 Info), each with mitigations; *"The five things to do first"* in plain words for the Director; a prioritised action plan; and an appendix of what it could not see. **Its findings are already the backlog:** every DB-n, WEB-n and CODE-n item under *Security* cites it, and most have since closed (DB-1 backups encrypted in 0.14.0, WEB-2 CSP enforced 2026-10-07). **One thing it did not do, now its own item below:** it was white-box only (*"Dynamic testing against a running instance"* is under *Not reviewed*), so this item's rule *"use the anon key and a test token for each role to confirm what RLS actually allows"* was not met by it.
